questions.explanation: The name Bhitai is derived directly from the Sindhi word 'bhit', meaning a mound.

questions.question: Do you know the name of any famous Sufi poet of Sindh?
questions.answer: Yes. The most famous Sufi poet of Sindh is Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai, who is lovingly called Lal Latif by his devotees. He is considered the greatest Muslim poet of the Sindhi language, and his poetry is collected in the Shah Jo Risalo. Another well-known Sufi figure of Sindh is Shah Inayat, but Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai is by far the best known.
questions.explanation: This pre-reading question activates background knowledge and leads the class towards the main reading text on Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai.

questions.question: The new academic year commences in our school in April.
questions.answer: The new academic year commences (begins) in our school in April.
questions.explanation: 'Commences' means begins or starts.

questions.question: It is a ______ fact that no living thing can survive without oxygen.
questions.answer: It is a universal fact that no living thing can survive without oxygen.
questions.explanation: 'Universal' means applicable to everyone and everything, so it suits a fact that is true for all living things.

questions.question: Shah Latif's forefather migrated to Sindh from Afghanistan. (Write the aspect number.)
questions.answer: 1 (Background and Family).
questions.explanation: The section on Background and Family states that Shah Latif's ancestral roots lay in Afghanistan and that his father or ancestors migrated to Sindh.

questions.question: Two other languages that he knew quite well.
questions.answer: He knew Arabic and Persian quite well.
questions.explanation: Although he received little formal education, the Risalo provides proof that Shah Latif had a good command of Arabic and Persian.

questions.question: Why did Shah Latif not marry again after his wife died?
questions.answer: Shah Latif did not marry again because after his wife Bibi Saidha Begum died at an early age and without children, his heart turned more and more towards religion and devotion. He felt restless and found it difficult to live a normal domestic life, so he devoted himself completely to prayer and deep thinking instead of marrying again.
questions.explanation: The section on Youth explains that his grief and spiritual inclination turned him away from ordinary domestic life.

questions.question: The devotees of some saints walk to shrines barefoot.
questions.answer: The devotees (followers) of some saints walk to shrines barefoot.
questions.explanation: A devotee is a person who is very devoted to a religion or to a person, that is, a follower.

questions.question: Much of what we know about our culture has been passed on to us through ______.
questions.answer: Much of what we know about our culture has been passed on to us through oral traditions.
questions.explanation: Culture is largely handed down by word of mouth, which is described as oral traditions.

questions.question: A shrine was built over his grave sometime after his death. (Write the aspect number.)
questions.answer: 6 (Death and Remembrance).
questions.explanation: The section Death and Remembrance says that King Ghulam Shah Kalhoro built a grand mausoleum over his grave after his death.

questions.question: Two main religious sources that he had knowledge about.
questions.answer: He had in-depth knowledge of the Holy Qur'an and the Hadiths.
questions.explanation: References in Shah Jo Risalo indicate his deep familiarity with the Holy Qur'an and the Hadiths.

questions.question: Why did people become Shah Latif's followers?
questions.answer: People became Shah Latif's followers because his spiritual power grew stronger with prayers and devotion. Anyone who came to him was strongly impressed by his gentle ways, so people began to be attracted towards him and his followers increased day by day.
questions.explanation: The section on Spiritual Growth links his growing spiritual power and gentle nature with the increase in his followers.

questions.question: Many people go to a mystic to ask for the fulfilment of their wishes.
questions.answer: Many people go to a mystic (a person with spiritual power) to ask for the fulfilment of their wishes.
questions.explanation: A mystic is a person who seeks direct union with God and is believed to possess spiritual power.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) person who lives alone (b) new person (c) person with spiritual power

questions.question: We may have different ______ but we are all the off springs of Adam.
questions.answer: We may have different ancestral roots but we are all the off springs of Adam.
questions.explanation: 'Ancestral roots' refers to the different origins or families from which people come.

questions.question: His poetry is mainly about Sindh but off places are also mentioned. (Write the aspect number.)
questions.answer: 7 (Shah Latif's Poetry).
questions.explanation: The section on Shah Latif's Poetry states that he wrote mainly about Sindh and its neighbouring regions but also mentions distant cities such as Istanbul and Samarqand.

questions.question: Two poets whose works were a part of his collection.
questions.answer: The Masnavi of Moulana Jalaluddin Rumi and the poems of Shah Karim were part of his poetic collection.
questions.explanation: The text mentions that Shah Latif's poetic collections included the Masnavi of Moulana Jalaluddin Rumi and Shah Karim's poems.

questions.question: What does Shah Latif's poetry and work tell us about his knowledge and skills?
questions.answer: Shah Latif's poetry and work tell us that he had wide and deep knowledge. Although he received little formal education, he knew Arabic and Persian quite well, had an in-depth knowledge of the Holy Qur'an and the Hadiths, and studied the Masnavi of Moulana Jalaluddin Rumi and the poems of Shah Karim. His poetry mentions distant cities such as Istanbul, Samarqand, China, Rome, Kabul, Kandahar, Delhi and Deccan, and also describes Sindhi sailors, their navigation techniques and their voyages as far as the Malabar coast, Sri Lanka and the island of Java. This shows that he had knowledge of geography, religion, poetry and seafaring, and great poetic skill.
questions.explanation: This question requires pulling together details from the sections on Early Life and Education and Shah Latif's Poetry.

questions.question: The sailors of Sindh used to travel to far off lands as they had good navigation skills.
questions.answer: The sailors of Sindh used to travel to far off lands as they had good navigation (ship directing) skills.
questions.explanation: Navigation is the skill of planning and directing the course of a ship or aircraft.

questions.question: Fasting ______ on the first day of Ramadan.
questions.answer: Fasting commences on the first day of Ramadan.
questions.explanation: 'Commences' means begins, which is exactly what fasting does on the first day of Ramadan.

questions.question: He loved studying and had a command over other languages. (Write the aspect number.)
questions.answer: 3 (Early Life and Education).
questions.explanation: The section Early Life and Education tells us that although he received little formal education, he knew Arabic and Persian quite well and had in-depth knowledge of the Holy Qur'an and the Hadiths.

questions.question: Two skills for which he is known.
questions.answer: He is known for (i) the skill of composing poetry (he started composing poetry as a boy and his verses are collected in Shah Jo Risalo), and (ii) his deep knowledge and skill as a Sufi scholar and mystic.
questions.explanation: The text describes him both as a poet of the people and as a Sufi scholar and saint with deep spiritual knowledge.

questions.question: Name the places in the text mentioned in Shah Latif's poetry. Why do you think these places have been mentioned by him?
questions.answer: The places mentioned in his poetry are Istanbul, Samarqand, China, Rome, Kabul, Kandahar, Delhi and Deccan; the text also mentions the Sindhi sailors' voyages to the Malabar coast, Sri Lanka and the island of Java. He mentions these places because he was a poet of the people with a wide outlook and knowledge of the world. The verse in which these places appear describes how the rain clouds return again and again, flashing lightning from all sides, and go to Istanbul, the west, China, Samarqand, Rome, Kabul, Kandahar and Delhi. By mentioning so many distant lands, he shows that the blessing of rain and God's mercy reach the whole world, and he uses this to pray that Allah may always make Sindh a land of abundance and make the whole universe prosperous. Thus the places help him connect his love for Sindh with his love for all humanity and for God.
questions.explanation: The verse translated in the text (Sur Sarang, Shah Jo Risalo) is the source for these place names and for the reason why they are mentioned.

questions.question: For centuries, the main medium for transfer of information was oral traditions.
questions.answer: For centuries, the main medium for transfer of information was oral traditions (passing of information by word of mouth).
questions.explanation: Oral traditions are customs, stories and information handed down from one generation to another by speaking, not by writing.

options.text: passing of information by word of mouth

questions.optionsRaw: (a) horses (b) passing of information by word of mouth (c) messages

questions.question: Pakistan has everything in ______ but we need strong policies to make good use of everything that we have.
questions.answer: Pakistan has everything in abundance but we need strong policies to make good use of everything that we have.
questions.explanation: 'In abundance' means in large quantities, which is what the sentence requires about Pakistan's resources.

questions.question: He is called Bhitai because he spent a good past of his life on a mound. (Write the aspect number.)
questions.answer: 2 (The Name Bhitai).
questions.explanation: This is the example already done in the book: 'bhit' means a mound in Sindhi, and because Shah Latif lived on a mound for the rest of his life he came to be known as Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai.

questions.question: Two places in Afghanistan mentioned in his poetry.
questions.answer: Kabul and Kandahar are the two places in Afghanistan mentioned in his poetry.
questions.explanation: In the translated verse quoted in the text, the poet says, 'Some wander to Rome, to Kabul and Kandahar.'

questions.question: Why is Shah Latif's key message in his verses acceptable to everyone?
questions.answer: Shah Latif's key message in his verses is acceptable to everyone because his spiritual and mystic poetry carries a message of love. Since love is a universal feeling, his message is universal and acceptable to the entire human race, regardless of religion, region or language. This is why his poetry has been translated into English, Urdu and other languages and is remembered with love and reverence.
questions.explanation: The section on Shah Latif's Poetry states directly that his message of love makes his poetry universal and acceptable to all.

questions.question: My brother is a restless person, always looking for new things to do.
questions.answer: My brother is a restless (change seeking) person, always looking for new things to do.
questions.explanation: 'Restless' means unable to stay still or content, always seeking change or new activity.

questions.question: Nelson Mandela won his people's ______ for his long struggle for the rights of people in South Asia.
questions.answer: Nelson Mandela won his people's reverence for his long struggle for the rights of people in South Asia.
questions.explanation: 'Reverence' means deep respect and admiration, which a leader earns through long struggle for people's rights.

questions.question: Two places in India mentioned in his poetry.
questions.answer: Delhi and Deccan are the two places in India mentioned in his poetry.
questions.explanation: In the quoted verse the poet says, 'some lie on Delhi, Deccan, thundering over.'

questions.question: Can we put his message into practice in today's world? If 'Yes' how, if 'No' why not?
questions.answer: Yes, we can put his message into practice in today's world. His message of love, devotion, tolerance and kindness can be practised in many ways: we can treat every human being with respect and kindness regardless of faith, race, nationality or social status; we can help the poor and the needy and share with them whatever we have in abundance; we can avoid hatred, violence and selfishness and instead promote peace and harmony in our families, neighbourhoods and country; we can stay devoted to God and to moral values in our daily lives by praying, being honest and being gentle in our dealings. If every individual follows these values, the hatred and conflict in today's world will be reduced and society will become peaceful and prosperous, just as Shah Latif prayed for.
questions.explanation: An open-ended inferential question; the answer draws on Shah Latif's universal message of love and links it to present-day life.

questions.question: Truly great persons deserve reverence as they play a positive role in our lives.
questions.answer: Truly great persons deserve reverence (respect and admiration) as they play a positive role in our lives.
questions.explanation: 'Reverence' means deep respect and admiration.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) richness and wealth (b) leadership positions (c) respect and admiration

questions.question: The art of ______ requires hard work and one needs to practise a lot to write beautifully.
questions.answer: The art of calligraphy requires hard work and one needs to practise a lot to write beautifully.
questions.explanation: The blank calls for the art of beautiful writing, that is 'calligraphy'. This word is not printed in the Exercise 2 list, so it has been inferred from the meaning of the sentence; the exercise appears to have a minor gap in its word bank.

questions.question: Two languages mentioned in which the 'Risalo' has been translated.
questions.answer: The Risalo has been translated into English and Urdu.
questions.explanation: The text states that his collected poems, compiled as Shah Jo Risalo, have been translated into English, Urdu and other languages.

questions.question: Islam's message of peace is universal, as without it there can be no happiness.
questions.answer: Islam's message of peace is universal (applicable to all the people in the world), as without it there can be no happiness.
questions.explanation: 'Universal' means applicable to or shared by all people in the world.

options.text: applicable to all the people in the world

questions.optionsRaw: (a) good (b) applicable to all the people in the world (c) acceptable

questions.question: The Pakistan Navy has very good ______ skills.
questions.answer: The Pakistan Navy has very good navigation skills.
questions.explanation: Navigation is the skill of directing the course of ships, which is a primary skill for a navy.

questions.question: What are some of the harmful things that people eat, drink or smoke?
questions.answer: Some of the harmful things that people eat, drink or smoke are cigarettes, bidi, sheesha, gutka, paan with tobacco, betel nut (chhaliya), naswar, alcohol, energy drinks, and too much junk food and sugary soft drinks. Many of these contain tobacco, nicotine, tobacco-specific nitrosamines and large amounts of sugar or harmful chemicals, which slowly damage the body. Student's sample answer: 'What do you think, what are some of the harmful things that people eat, drink or smoke? In my opinion, cigarettes, gutka, naswar and soft drinks are the most common harmful things.'
questions.explanation: Part of the Listening and Speaking exercise on asking and answering questions of a social nature; the answer uses the polite question starter 'what do you think'.

questions.question: After all the students in your group have asked all the questions, select one answer for each one of the questions that you would like to share with the class. Decide who will go and present each answer on behalf of the group.
questions.answer: Model group presentation: Question 1 (harmful things) - 'Our group thinks the most harmful things are cigarettes, gutka, naswar and sugary drinks.' Question 2 (physical health) - 'They cause cancer, heart disease and diabetes and make a person weak and addicted.' Question 3 (friendship) - 'Addiction causes irritability and quarrels and destroys the trust of friends.' Question 4 (family life) - 'It wastes the family's money and causes tension, quarrels and unhappiness at home.' Question 5 (life style) - 'It leaves a person with very little money for food, education and health, so his standard of living goes down.' The group decides that one member will present each answer in front of the class, and the group's best answers are shared with all the students.
questions.explanation: This is the presentation stage of the Listening and Speaking exercise; each group selects one answer for each of the five questions and presents it to the class.

questions.question: How does the use of these harmful things affect their physical health?
questions.answer: The use of these harmful things affects physical health very badly. Tobacco and cigarettes cause lung cancer, throat cancer, heart disease, high blood pressure and constant coughing, and they weaken the immune system. Gutka and betel nut damage the teeth, gums and mouth and can cause oral cancer. Alcohol destroys the liver and the kidneys and harms the brain. Junk food and sugary drinks lead to obesity, diabetes and weak bones. A person also becomes addicted, loses appetite and stamina, falls ill again and again and cannot study or work properly. Student's sample answer: 'In your opinion, how does the use of these harmful things affect physical health? In my opinion, they cause cancer, heart disease and diabetes and make a person weak and addicted.'
questions.explanation: This question uses the polite starter 'in your opinion' and requires a factual, social answer about health effects.

questions.question: How does their use affect their relationships with their friends and other people?
questions.answer: The use of these harmful things affects relationships with friends and other people in a very negative way. An addicted person becomes irritable, moody and unreliable, so friends begin to avoid him. Sometimes he starts mixing with bad company and is pushed towards stealing or lying to get money for these things, and this destroys the trust of friends. He may also become rude or aggressive and quarrel over small matters, which spoils good friendships. In this way, addiction slowly cuts a person off from his well-wishers and he is left alone. Student's sample answer: 'According to you, how does their use affect their relationships with their friends and other people? According to me, addiction spoils friendships, causes quarrels and makes a person lose the trust of his friends.'
questions.explanation: This question uses the polite starter 'according to you' and links addiction to social relationships.

questions.question: How does their use affect their family life?
questions.answer: The use of these harmful things affects family life very badly. A large part of the family income is wasted on buying cigarettes, gutka or alcohol, so the family faces poverty and cannot meet its needs for food, education and medicine. The addicted person becomes ill and short-tempered, quarrels with his wife, parents and children, and neglects his duties and responsibilities. Children, seeing such a bad example, may also start these harmful habits. In the end, the whole family suffers from tension, illness and unhappiness. Student's sample answer: 'What do you say, how does their use affect family life? What do you say, these habits waste the family's money, cause quarrels at home and set a bad example for children.'
questions.explanation: This question uses the polite starter 'what do you say' and requires a social answer about the effects on the family.

questions.question: How does the cost of these things affect a person's life style?
questions.answer: The cost of these things affects a person's life style in a harmful way. Cigarettes, gutka and alcohol are expensive, and an addicted person usually spends a large part of his income on them every day. He therefore has less money left for good food, clothes, education of children, proper housing and medical care, so his standard of living falls. To meet this cost he may take loans, sell household items or fall into debt, and in serious cases he may lose his job because he is often ill or absent. Thus, instead of enjoying a healthy and comfortable life, he is forced into a poor and difficult life style. Student's sample answer: 'Can you tell me, how does the cost of these things affect a person's life style? Can you tell me, it leaves him with very little money for food, education and health, so his standard of living goes down.'
questions.explanation: This question uses the polite starter 'can you tell me' and requires an answer about the economic effect of addiction.

questions.question: I ______ swim when I was a child but I ______ swim now.
questions.answer: I couldn't swim when I was a child but I can swim now.
questions.explanation: The first blank refers to the past time, so 'could/couldn't' is used, and the second blank refers to the present, so 'can' is used. (The reverse pair 'could ... can't' is also grammatically possible.)

questions.question: Write about your abilities/ inabilities in the following blanks. (When I was younger/ When I was nine years old: I could ______ / But, I couldn't ______ / Now, I can ______ / However, I can't ______ / When I grow up, I can ______)
questions.answer: When I was nine years old, I could ride a bicycle. But, I couldn't swim in deep water. Now, I can swim well and I can also ride a bicycle quickly. However, I can't drive a car because I am still too young. When I grow up, I can become a famous doctor and serve my country.
questions.explanation: The task uses 'could/couldn't' for past ability and 'can/can't' for present ability, and 'can' for future ability.

questions.question: Dialogue A: Using can/ could for ability. Complete the dialogue given below and add at least 10 lines. (Zahra: Can you speak Chinese, Najma? Najma: No, but I can speak Persian. Zahra: Wow! What about you Farah? Farah: I can't ...... but I can ......)
questions.answer: Zahra: Can you speak Chinese, Najma? Najma: No, but I can speak Persian. Zahra: Wow! What about you Farah? Farah: I can't speak Chinese, but I can speak Sindhi and English quite well. Zahra: That is wonderful, Farah. Could you speak English when you were in class five? Farah: No, I couldn't speak English then, but I can speak it fluently now. Zahra: Najma, could you write Urdu when you were younger? Najma: Yes, I could write Urdu, but I couldn't write it neatly. Now I can write it beautifully. Zahra: Can both of you recite poetry? Farah: I can recite a few verses of Shah Latif, but I can't sing them. Najma: I can't recite poetry, but I can sing folk songs. Zahra: That is great. Can you both join the school's language club? Farah: Yes, we can. We can also help other students learn new languages. Najma: We can teach them Sindhi and Persian, and they can teach us Chinese. Zahra: Then let us join today.
questions.explanation: A model dialogue of more than ten lines that uses 'can/can't' for present ability and 'could/couldn't' for past ability.

questions.question: A. Fill in the blanks with nouns formed by using the suffix 'ment' (employ, treat, manage, pay, retire, judge). 1. As soon as the judgement was given, the reporters left the court room.
questions.answer: Judgement (already done as the example in the book).
questions.explanation: The verb 'judge' becomes the noun 'judgement' with the suffix 'ment'.

questions.question: My brother ______ run fast when he was five years old but he ______ run fast now.
questions.answer: My brother couldn't run fast when he was five years old but he can run fast now.
questions.explanation: The past time ('when he was five years old') takes 'couldn't', and the present time ('now') takes 'can'.

questions.question: Now ask two of your class mates what they could/ couldn't do when they were younger, what they can/ can't do now and what they think they can do in the future. Write their responses in your notebook.
questions.answer: Model responses recorded from classmates: Classmate 1 (Ali): 'When I was six years old, I couldn't write my name neatly. Now I can write neatly in both Urdu and English. When I grow up, I can become an engineer.' Classmate 2 (Sana): 'When I was younger, I could sing well but I couldn't draw. Now I can draw simple pictures, but I can't sing in front of a large audience. In the future, I can become a teacher.' The questions asked were: 'What could you do when you were younger?', 'What couldn't you do when you were younger?', 'What can you do now?', 'What can't you do now?' and 'What can you do in the future?'
questions.explanation: This speaking-and-writing task continues the practice of 'can/can't' and 'could/couldn't' in questions and answers.

questions.question: Dialogue B: Using can/ could/ may for permission. Complete the dialogue given below and add at least 10 lines. (Areeb: I have completed my work. Can I play now? Mother: Yes, you can, but come back soon. Areeb: May I take my new ......? Mother: ...... Bilal: ......)
questions.answer: Areeb: I have completed my work. Can I play now? Mother: Yes, you can, but come back soon. Areeb: May I take my new cricket bat with me? Mother: Yes, you may take it, but take care of it. Bilal: May I also go with him, Mother? Mother: You may go, but only after you finish your homework. Bilal: Could I have half an hour to finish it? Mother: Yes, you can have half an hour, but then you must go straight to the ground with Areeb. Areeb: Can we stay out until sunset? Mother: No, you can't stay out so late; you must be home before dark. Areeb: May I take some water with me? Mother: Of course, you may. Bilal: Can we invite our cousin to play with us tomorrow? Mother: You can invite him, but you must also ask your uncle first.
questions.explanation: A model dialogue of more than ten lines using 'can', 'could' and 'may' to ask for and give permission.

questions.question: A. 2. Zaman is back to work after his ______.
questions.answer: Zaman is back to work after his treatment.
questions.explanation: The verb 'treat' forms the noun 'treatment' with the suffix 'ment', which fits returning to work after medical care.

questions.question: They ______ come early but they ______ find a bus earlier.
questions.answer: They can come early but they can't find a bus earlier.
questions.explanation: Both clauses refer to present ability and inability, so 'can' and 'can't' are used. The past pair 'could/couldn't' is also acceptable if the situation is understood as past.

questions.question: A. 3. The workers receive their weekly ______ every Friday.
questions.answer: The workers receive their weekly payment every Friday.
questions.explanation: The verb 'pay' forms the noun 'payment' with the suffix 'ment'.

questions.question: Nowadays, Sana ______ speak English fluently but she ______ speak so well a year ago.
questions.answer: Nowadays, Sana can speak English fluently but she couldn't speak so well a year ago.
questions.explanation: 'Nowadays' shows present ability, so 'can' is used, while 'a year ago' shows past time, so 'couldn't' is used.

questions.question: A. 4. My son is looking for ______ as he lost his job last week.
questions.answer: My son is looking for employment as he lost his job last week.
questions.explanation: The verb 'employ' forms the noun 'employment' with the suffix 'ment', meaning work or a job.

questions.question: Sameer ______ speak several languages when he was young but now he ______ speak only English fluently.
questions.answer: Sameer could speak several languages when he was young but now he can speak only English fluently.
questions.explanation: 'When he was young' refers to the past and takes 'could'; 'now' refers to the present and takes 'can'.

questions.question: A. 5. After his ______ at the age of sixty he has decided to write a book.
questions.answer: After his retirement at the age of sixty he has decided to write a book.
questions.explanation: The verb 'retire' forms the noun 'retirement' with the suffix 'ment', and sixty is the usual age of retirement.

questions.question: Little Shahzain ______ crawl but he still ______ walk.
questions.answer: Little Shahzain can crawl but he still can't walk.
questions.explanation: Both verbs refer to the baby's present abilities and inabilities, so 'can' and 'can't' are used.

questions.question: A. 6. The ______ of the school announced their new admission policy yesterday.
questions.answer: The management of the school announced their new admission policy yesterday.
questions.explanation: The verb 'manage' forms the noun 'management' with the suffix 'ment', which refers to the persons who run an institution.

questions.question: Sara ______ embroider and stitch clothes but her sister ______.
questions.answer: Sara can embroider and stitch clothes but her sister can't.
questions.explanation: Present ability and inability are expressed with 'can' and 'can't'.

questions.question: B. Fill in the blanks by using the suffix 'ness' (ill, bold, neat, kind, soft). 1. Her ______ has made her weak.
questions.answer: Her illness has made her weak.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'ill' forms the noun 'illness' with the suffix 'ness'.

questions.question: We ______ play after completing our homework but we ______ play before that.
questions.answer: We can play after completing our homework but we can't play before that.
questions.explanation: Permission/ability in the present is shown by 'can' and its negative 'can't'.

questions.question: B. 2. I love the ______ of our new sofa set.
questions.answer: I love the softness of our new sofa set.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'soft' forms the noun 'softness' with the suffix 'ness', which describes the feel of a sofa.

questions.question: B. 3. Our neighbour's son, who is a soldier, fought the enemy with ______.
questions.answer: Our neighbour's son, who is a soldier, fought the enemy with boldness.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'bold' forms the noun 'boldness' with the suffix 'ness', meaning courage.

questions.question: B. 4. The principal of our school treats everyone with ______.
questions.answer: The principal of our school treats everyone with kindness.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'kind' forms the noun 'kindness' with the suffix 'ness'.

questions.question: B. 5. My mother taught us ______ in all our work.
questions.answer: My mother taught us neatness in all our work.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'neat' forms the noun 'neatness' with the suffix 'ness'.

questions.question: C. Fill in the blanks by using the suffix 'al' (sign, survive, approve, propose, remove). 1. The ______ of the green turtle is in danger on the Karachi beaches.
questions.answer: The survival of the green turtle is in danger on the Karachi beaches.
questions.explanation: The verb 'survive' forms the noun 'survival' with the suffix 'al'.

questions.question: C. 2. Our ______ for setting up a dispensary was accepted by the minister.
questions.answer: Our proposal for setting up a dispensary was accepted by the minister.
questions.explanation: The verb 'propose' forms the noun 'proposal' with the suffix 'al'.

questions.question: C. 3. The ______ of garbage is the responsibility of the government.
questions.answer: The removal of garbage is the responsibility of the government.
questions.explanation: The verb 'remove' forms the noun 'removal' with the suffix 'al'.

questions.question: C. 4. The train moved out of the station as soon as the guard gave the ______.
questions.answer: The train moved out of the station as soon as the guard gave the signal.
questions.explanation: The verb 'sign' forms the noun 'signal' with the suffix 'al', which the guard gives to start the train.

questions.question: C. 5. I needed my parents' ______ for going to friend's wedding.
questions.answer: I needed my parents' approval for going to friend's wedding.
questions.explanation: The verb 'approve' forms the noun 'approval' with the suffix 'al', meaning permission or consent.

questions.question: Why was the twins' father worried?
questions.answer: The twins' father was worried because although Tanveer and Junaid looked exactly alike, they were quite different in nature. Junaid always thought carefully before doing anything, while Tanveer did things without thinking. The father was worried about Tanveer's careless habit and wanted to make him realize that he should think before doing things.
questions.explanation: This question is discussed orally after reading the story 'Two Brothers' to prepare for the narrative writing task.

questions.question: Imagine that you are Tanveer's teacher. You wanted him to win but he was not successful. What do you think he should do / not do? Write a narrative essay keeping the following points in mind: Explain the reason for the competition; state what he did and why; describe what his brother did; explain who won the competition and why; identify the mistakes that Tanveer made; express your regret and explain how you would like him to change.
questions.answer:
THE COMPETITION

Tanveer and Junaid were twin brothers in my class. They looked exactly alike, yet their natures were quite different. Junaid always thought carefully before doing anything, while Tanveer did things without thinking. Their father, who was worried about Tanveer's careless habit, decided to teach him a lesson. He announced that he had saved enough money to buy only one bicycle, and that he would give it to the winner of a competition. Both brothers were to set out right after the morning prayers, walk as far as each could, and return by sunset; the one who completed the task would win the bicycle. As their teacher, I understood that the real reason for the competition was to make Tanveer realize that he should think before acting, and I sincerely hoped that he would win.

On the morning of the competition, however, Tanveer made the very mistake his father was trying to cure. As soon as the prayers were over, he sprinted off without a plan, thinking only of covering the greatest distance and reaching home first. He ran to the end of the town and far beyond, proud that he had left Junaid far behind. He wanted the prize so badly that he never once stopped to ask himself whether he could return in time. Junaid, on the other hand, walked calmly until midday. Instead of running far away, he turned back at the right moment, so that he would be able to reach home comfortably before sunset.

By the time Tanveer realized how tired he was, it was too late. Because he had run so fast, his return journey was slow and painful, and he stumbled home long after sunset. Junaid was already there. Tanveer demanded the prize for having run the farthest, but his father explained that he had not returned within the given time, so the prize would go to Junaid, who had completed the task according to the instructions. Junaid therefore won the competition, not because he was stronger, but because he had planned carefully and kept the rules in mind.

Tanveer's mistakes were clear to me: he acted in haste, he was overconfident, he ignored the time limit and he thought only of distance instead of the whole task. I felt sorry for him and I wished I could have helped him win. Yet I also hope that this failure has taught him a lesson he will never forget. I would like him to change his habit of acting without thinking, to plan before he begins any task, to value patience and self-control, and to remember that success belongs to those who think first and act afterwards.
questions.explanation: This is a model narrative essay of more than four paragraphs written in the third person from the point of view of Tanveer's teacher, following all the points listed in the exercise.

questions.question: Work in groups of three. Think of one story related to you or someone you know quite well. Share your stories with each other, select one story and write a narrative essay by following the steps: brainstorm; select a topic; decide why you want to tell that story; select the points/ideas to include; prepare an outline; write the introductory paragraph giving background and purpose; narrate the incident; relate the incident to the purpose; write the concluding paragraph; and edit for organization, grammar, punctuation and paragraphing.
questions.answer:
MODEL STORY: THE DAY I LEARNED TO BE HONEST

Outline: (1) Introduction - background and purpose: my cousin Aamir, an honest shopkeeper, once found a purse; (2) Incident begins - a busy day at the shop, an old woman leaves her purse behind; (3) Complication - the purse contains a large amount of money and Aamir's friend advises him to keep it; (4) Climax - Aamir refuses and searches for the owner; (5) Resolution - he returns the purse and is rewarded with the woman's prayers and the town's respect; (6) Conclusion - honesty is the best policy.

Yesterday my cousin Aamir told me a story that I shall always remember. Aamir, who is only a few years older than me, runs a small general store in our town. I want to tell this story because it taught me, and everyone who heard it, the value of honesty. One busy afternoon, a heavy downpour had filled the shop with customers, and an old woman came in to buy medicine for her grandson.

While Aamir was serving the other customers, the old woman paid for her things and hurried out into the rain. A few minutes later, Aamir noticed a worn leather purse lying beside the counter. He opened it and was shocked to find a large amount of money inside, more than a whole month's profit of his shop. He remembered that the purse belonged to the old woman. Just then his friend Bilal came in and whispered that no one had seen the purse, so Aamir could easily keep the money. Aamir did not listen to him for a second.

He closed his shop at once, even though he would lose business, and ran through the rain towards the old woman's house, which was at the far end of the town. When the breathless old woman saw her purse, she burst into tears, for the money was meant for her grandson's treatment. She blessed Aamir again and again, and the next day the whole town heard how the young shopkeeper had returned the money.

That day I learnt an important lesson. Aamir's honesty, courage and kindness brought him far more than money; they brought him respect and the heartfelt prayers of a poor woman. From then on, I decided that I would always choose honesty, even when nobody is watching, because honesty is truly the best policy.
questions.explanation: This is a model narrative essay following every step listed in the exercise: brainstorming, topic selection, purpose, outline, introduction, narration, linking the incident to the purpose and a conclusion.

questions.question: Read the following passage about Moen-jo-Daro and underline the main ideas / words in each paragraph; do not include any details. (The first paragraph has been done as an example.)
questions.answer:
Paragraph 1 (example, already done): Moen-jo-Daro or the 'Mound of the Dead' is one of the oldest cities in the world, and it was one of the largest city-settlements of the Indus Valley Civilization of South Asia.

Paragraph 2 (main ideas to be underlined): Nobody knew anything about Moen-jo-Daro until 1922, when villagers found pieces of old smooth pots and old bricks; these were brought to Sir John Marshall, who recognized them as pieces of very old pots and decided that the area should be dug up as there might be remains of an old city.

Paragraph 3 (main ideas to be underlined): The men started digging and, bit by bit, a city of straight roads and well-built houses came up from what had been taken for mounds of clay and sand; each house was made of large baked bricks and had a bathroom and servant quarters, with covered drains beside streets of baked bricks, and a wide road with shops on both sides in the middle.

Paragraph 4 (main ideas to be underlined): The people must have been great traders, with the river Indus near and the sea within easy reach; the countryside was fertile with wheat, rice and cotton, the farmers kept cattle, and there were skilled craftsmen who made things from gold, silver and ivory.

Paragraph 5 (main ideas to be underlined): For a long time these people lived a happy, rich life and travelled from place to place for business or pleasure; their city was well-planned and clean, but we do not know what happened to them - either they were raided from the north or a great earthquake destroyed them.
questions.explanation: The exercise trains students to identify only the main ideas of each paragraph (not details) so that these key words can be used to write a summary in Exercise 5.

questions.question: Use the underlined key words and write a summary of the above passage about Moen-jo-Daro. Look at the Do's and Don'ts given in the boxes above. (You may begin like this: 'Moen-jo-Daro, in Sindh, was one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization...')
questions.answer: Moen-jo-Daro, in Sindh, was one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization. This civilization developed around 3000 BC in areas that today form Pakistan and North India, and Moen-jo-Daro, one of the oldest cities in the world, was built around 2600 BC. Nothing was known about it until 1922, when villagers found pieces of old pots and bricks and brought them to Sir John Marshall, who decided that the area should be dug up. When digging began, a well-planned city of straight roads and strong houses of baked bricks appeared, with bathrooms, covered drains and a wide road with shops on both sides. Its people must have been great traders, for the Indus was near and the sea was within easy reach; the fertile land produced wheat, rice and cotton, and skilled craftsmen worked in gold, silver and ivory. For a long time these people lived a happy and rich life, but we do not know what happened to them, for they may have been raided from the north or destroyed by a great earthquake.
questions.explanation: A model summary written from the underlined main ideas of the passage, using simple short sentences and linking words, without reproducing sentences from the original or adding new ideas.

questions.question: What did he decide to do?
questions.answer: He decided to set up a competition between the two brothers so that Tanveer would realize that he should think before doing things. He told them that he had saved enough money to buy only one bicycle, so the one who would win the competition would get it. The competition was that both brothers would set out right after the morning prayers and walk as far as each could, and return by sunset; the one who managed to complete the task would get the prize.
questions.explanation: The father's plan is the plot device that reveals the importance of thinking before acting.

questions.question: Who won the competition? Why did he win?
questions.answer: Junaid won the competition. He won because he thought about what he should do before setting off. He walked until midday and then turned around to return home, so he reached home well before sunset and completed the task according to the instructions. Tanveer, on the other hand, ran too far and returned late, so he failed.
questions.explanation: Junaid's careful planning and timely return made him the winner, which is the moral of the story.

questions.question: Who lost the competition? Why did he lose?
questions.answer: Tanveer lost the competition. He lost because he sprinted off without thinking and ran to the end of the town and further, wanting to cover a greater distance and win the prize. As he had been running so fast, he became very tired, so his return journey was slower and he reached home long after sunset. Since he had not returned within the time he was supposed to be back, he failed to complete the task according to the instructions.
questions.explanation: Tanveer's haste and overconfidence caused his failure, in contrast to Junaid's careful planning.

questions.question: What lesson do you think Tanveer learnt?
questions.answer: I think Tanveer learnt that one should always think and plan carefully before doing anything, and that haste and overconfidence lead to failure. He also learnt that covering a greater distance is useless if one cannot complete the task within the given time and according to the instructions. From that day he must have realized that wise planning, patience and self-control bring success, while acting without thinking brings loss.
questions.explanation: This question draws out the moral of the story, which is the theme of the narrative essay that follows.

questions.question: Editing Practice (C-test): Beginning from the second word of the second sentence, half or half plus one extra letters have been removed from every second word. Complete all the words and write the complete passage 'The Duties of a Good Citizen' in your notebook.
questions.answer:
THE DUTIES OF A GOOD CITIZEN

If we just think for a minute, about the things and services we use in one day, we shall realize how much we owe to society. The milkman brings milk for us; the baker bakes the bread; the printer prints our books; the driver drives the bus in which we go to school or the place of our work. The teacher teaches the pupils at school, the doctor treats the sick and the shopkeeper sells articles of daily use. The traffic police regulate the traffic so that we may travel without any fear of accident.

We must repay society for all these gifts. If a milkman mixes water in the milk, how can he expect other members of society to treat him fairly? If a shopkeeper gives short measure or sells sub-standard goods, he must be prepared to get the same kind of treatment from others. If we ignore traffic rules, we not only endanger the lives of others but our own as well.

Many benefits we enjoy are provided by our own country and society. It is, therefore, our duty to be loyal and patriotic to Pakistan. We should pay our taxes promptly, fully and honestly, so that we may continue to enjoy all social benefits.

Islam lays great stress on our duties as citizens. The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) once said, 'God lays so much stress on the rights of our neighbours that I almost thought they would get the right of inheritance in our property.' In short, we cannot be good Muslims without being good and dutiful citizens.
questions.explanation: This is the complete reconstructed passage for the C-test; the missing halves of words are supplied from the context of each sentence.

questions.question: You are the editor of your school magazine. Work in pairs to edit the following passage for the school magazine.
questions.answer:
CORRECTED PASSAGE

Students have mainly three basic duties. They must obey their parents, teachers and elders. Students must help their parents in simple home chores. They must not become unresponsive to parents or teachers.

Students must follow the standard discipline. They must establish a routine of studying. They must learn and practise good manners and habits. They must focus on their studies. Regular reading should be a part of their daily routine, and this reading habit makes them more intelligent and knowledgeable; moreover, it also improves their overall language skills and vocabulary. Besides studying, they must exercise daily. They must avoid watching too much TV. They must be polite and respectful towards everyone. They must eat healthy food and avoid eating food that is unhealthy.

LIST OF CORRECTIONS: 'there parent' corrected to 'their parents'; 'they must not became' corrected to 'They must not become'; 'must fellow' corrected to 'must follow'; 'practice' (verb) corrected to 'practise'; 'routine with studying' corrected to 'routine of studying'; 'Besides study' corrected to 'Besides studying'; 'They avoid watching' corrected to 'They must avoid watching'; 'languach' corrected to 'language'; 'every one' corrected to 'everyone'; 'eating good that is unhealthy' corrected to 'eating food that is unhealthy'.
questions.explanation: The task is to edit the passage for grammar, spelling and punctuation errors (pronouns, verb forms, capitalisation, spelling and word choice) before printing it in the school magazine.

questions.question: Here is one of Shah Latif's poems, 'Rain', translated by Elsa Kazi. Work in groups of four and recite it. Each group should read one verse only.
questions.answer: The poem 'RAIN' by Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai, translated by Elsa Kazi, has four verses, and each of the four members of the group recites one verse. Verse 1 (first member): 'The rain pours on the desert sands / On hills and vales around; / At early dawn we rise to hear, / The churns soft, humming sound-'. Verse 2 (second member): 'The hands are full of butter, wives / With merriment abound- / Each buffalo for milking brought; / Athwart the grassy ground; / In thatches here we never found / Mistress and mind so glad!'. Verse 3 (third member): 'Season's Orchestra's in full swing, / Fresh showers ease the mind; / On mountain-side so green with grass; / Cattle abundance find; / Gay herdsmen's wives about their necks / Of blossoms garlands wind;'. Verse 4 (fourth member): 'Cucumbers, mushrooms, vegetables / Food of every kind; / Lord! Days of dearth let lie behind, / Ne'er let them reach the earth.' For good recitation each member should speak clearly and slowly, pause correctly at the commas, and use a soft, happy tone for the joyful scenes and a prayerful tone for the last two lines. The poem describes the joy of the first rain in Sindh: the sound of churning butter, the herdsmen's happy wives, the green mountain-side and the abundance of food, and it ends with a prayer that days of scarcity should never come again.
questions.explanation: The Fun section poem is not to be formally assessed; the model answer gives the four verses with their group divisions and guidance on tone and expression for recitation.

questions.question: Continue working in the same groups of four and draw the scene described in the verse that you recited, on a chart paper. Colour or paint the picture. Write the verse in beautiful and fancy writing on the chart. All the charts will be displayed in the class and the group with the best drawing will be the winner.
questions.answer: For Verse 1, draw rolling desert sands and hills with heavy slanting lines of falling rain, a dark grey sky with flashes of lightning, and a small Sindhi village in the foreground where people stand at dawn listening to the soft humming of the churning pots. For Verse 2, draw a grassy ground with buffaloes being brought for milking, women with hands full of butter and happy smiling faces, and simple thatched huts behind them. For Verse 3, draw a green mountain-side covered with fresh grass, colourful wild flowers, cattle grazing in abundance, and the herdsmen's wives wearing garlands of blossoms around their necks. For Verse 4, draw baskets full of cucumbers, mushrooms and vegetables of every kind, with farmers thanking God, and use bright fresh colours. On each chart, write the verse neatly in fancy lettering using a good pen or marker, add a small border of raindrops or flowers, and write the poet's name (Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai) and the translator's name (Elsa Kazi) at the bottom so that all the charts can be displayed in the class and judged.
questions.explanation: The drawing-and-display activity is only for fun and is not formally assessed; the model answer describes exactly what each group should draw and write for its chosen verse.

questions.question: Think of five professions that you think are interesting and write them down in the table below. Give reasons why you think they are interesting. These may not necessarily be the professions that you might choose to follow.
questions.answer: Interesting professions and why they are interesting: 1) Doctor - saves lives, cures the sick and is respected by everyone. 2) Teacher - shapes young minds, spreads knowledge and builds the future of the nation. 3) Pilot - flies people across the world, sees different countries and works with modern machines. 4) Software engineer - designs apps, games and websites that make everyday life easier and faster. 5) Journalist - travels to new places, investigates facts and informs the public about the truth.
questions.explanation: This is a pre-reading task that activates prior knowledge about jobs before reading the text 'Chasing Dreams'. Any five sensible professions with a clear reason for each are acceptable.

questions.question: How many characters are there in the story?
questions.answer: There are nine characters in the story.
questions.explanation: Though the story is short, nine persons are named or take part in the action. Uncle Sarmad is only mentioned as having died, so he is not counted.

questions.question: Who said: 'You don't seem ok. Let's have dinner then we will talk about it.'?
questions.answer: Jameel's father.
questions.explanation: These words are spoken by the father when Jameel comes home looking upset and refuses to talk.

questions.question: The word 'shabby' means ________.
questions.answer: Shabby means in a poor, worn-out or untidy condition (of a building or thing).
questions.explanation: In the story the house is described as a 'shabby, mud house', i.e. old and poorly kept.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The old woman reluctantly got up from her bed. She had ______ many difficulties but now her ______ hands could not lift heavy things.
questions.answer: borne; weathered. Full sentence: She had borne many difficulties but now her weathered hands could not lift heavy things.
questions.explanation: 'Borne' completes 'had borne many difficulties' and 'weathered' describes the old woman's hands.

questions.question: What was Jameel's father doing when he came home?
questions.answer: Jameel's father was sitting in the courtyard of their mud house under the cool moonlit sky, drinking tea with his cup resting on the table beside his charpoy.
questions.explanation: The opening paragraph describes the father sitting in the courtyard with his cup of tea when Jameel arrives.

questions.question: Why do you think nobody spoke while eating dinner?
questions.answer: Everybody could see that Jameel was upset, so they did not want to disturb him or make him feel worse. They only stole sidelong looks at him and kept quiet out of respect for his feelings.
questions.explanation: The text says the family noticed Jameel was upset but did not say anything, showing tact and sympathy.

questions.question: Develop a plan for realizing your dream: Why do you want to become this?
questions.answer: I want to become a doctor because I want to serve the poor and the sick people of my village, who cannot afford to travel to the city hospital for treatment. I have also seen how quickly a disease can take away a loved one when there is no medical help nearby, and I want to save such lives.
questions.explanation: This is a personal planning task; the model answer chooses the profession of a doctor, but any profession may be used.

questions.question: Now, work in groups of three and tell each other which professions you think are interesting and why.
questions.answer: Model oral response: 'I find the profession of a doctor very interesting because a doctor saves human lives and relieves pain. My friend Sara finds teaching interesting because a teacher builds the character of the next generation, while Ahmed thinks flying a plane is exciting because a pilot travels to different countries. In our group we agreed that every profession is useful as long as it is done with honesty and hard work.'
questions.explanation: The task is a group speaking activity; the model answer shows how a student can share a chosen profession and its reason with two partners.

questions.question: Write their names.
questions.answer: The nine characters are: 1) Jameel, 2) Sara (his sister), 3) Khalid (his brother), 4) Jameel's father, 5) Jameel's mother, 6) Aunt Sadori, 7) Allah Dinno, 8) Uncle Noor Ali (the patient) and 9) Jameel's wife.
questions.explanation: All these characters appear in the two parts of the story, 'Chasing Dreams' and 'Twelve Years Later'.

questions.question: Who said: 'Only men have to worry about earning for their families.'?
questions.answer: Jameel.
questions.explanation: Jameel says this to justify why he is more worried about his career than his sister Sara.

questions.question: The word 'collapsed' means ________.
questions.answer: Collapsed means fell down suddenly or sank down heavily through tiredness.
questions.explanation: Jameel 'collapsed on the charpoy', meaning he dropped down heavily on it.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: As she looked, a smile came to her lips when she saw the big, ______, beautiful lawn, with plants and creepers, and mango trees serving as a ______.
questions.answer: impressive; backdrop. Full sentence: She saw the big, impressive, beautiful lawn, with plants and creepers, and mango trees serving as a backdrop.
questions.explanation: 'Impressive' describes the beautiful large lawn and 'backdrop' suits the mango trees behind it.

questions.question: Where did the family have dinner?
questions.answer: The family had dinner in the courtyard of their house, around a table that Sara and Khalid had brought close to the charpoy, under the moonlit sky.
questions.explanation: The text says Sara and Khalid picked up the table and brought it near the charpoy, and everybody sat around it to eat.

questions.question: Why was Jameel upset?
questions.answer: Jameel was upset because although he had got a good grade, his sister Sara had obtained more marks than him. More importantly, his dream of becoming a doctor seemed impossible because there was no college in his village or in any nearby village - the nearest one was 50 miles away in the city.
questions.explanation: Jameel's sadness comes from both a sense of comparison with his sister and the practical problem of there being no college near his home.

questions.question: What will you have to do to realize your dream?
questions.answer: I will have to study science subjects with full attention, get excellent marks in every test, join a good college, then clear the entry test and get admission to a medical college. After qualifying as a doctor, I will complete my house job, choose a specialisation, and finally open a clinic or hospital in my village.
questions.explanation: The answer lists the step-by-step academic and practical requirements of becoming a doctor.

questions.question: Who said: 'We don't get education only for earning money.'?
questions.answer: Khalid.
questions.explanation: Khalid corrects Jameel and explains that education is for improving ourselves and is equally necessary for males and females.

questions.question: The word 'reluctantly' means ________.
questions.answer: Reluctantly means unwillingly, hesitantly, or without wanting to do something.
questions.explanation: Jameel 'reluctantly' got up to eat, showing that he did not really want to.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She ______ on her bed once again and became ______ with her thoughts.
questions.answer: collapsed; preoccupied. Full sentence: She collapsed on her bed once again and became preoccupied with her thoughts.
questions.explanation: 'Collapsed' fits sitting or lying down heavily and 'preoccupied' fits being lost in thought.

questions.question: Where did Jameel and Sara go to study?
questions.answer: They went to the city where Aunt Sadori lived. There they attended a college and later joined the medical college to become doctors.
questions.explanation: Aunt Sadori offered them a home in the city, where the college and the medical college were.

questions.question: Why do you think Sara tried to hide her feelings?
questions.answer: Sara tried to hide her feelings because she was afraid that her father would refuse her the chance to study in the city and keep her at home to help her mother. She did not want her father to see how much studying meant to her, so she quietly wiped her tear away.
questions.explanation: The father had already said that Jameel could go but Sara should stay home, so Sara hid her disappointment.

questions.question: What are some of the factors that can help you in achieving your aim?
questions.answer: The factors that can help me are: the love, prayers and support of my parents; the guidance of my teachers; my own hard work, honesty and regularity; good time management; help from friends and relatives; and scholarships or other financial support.
questions.explanation: These are the positive forces a student can rely on while pursuing a career goal.

questions.question: Who said: 'We can ask Allah Bachayo, to take you to the city in his horse cart.'?
questions.answer: Jameel's mother.
questions.explanation: The mother suggests a practical way of sending Jameel to the city after quoting a Sindhi couplet.

questions.question: The word 'preoccupied' means ________.
questions.answer: Preoccupied means absorbed or lost in thought, thinking deeply about something so that one pays no attention to anything else.
questions.explanation: Jameel was 'preoccupied' with thoughts about his future, which is why he could not share his feelings with Sara.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She thought of her ______, old house, her five ______ and how they always used to offer their ______ prayers.
questions.answer: shabby; siblings; obligatory. Full sentence: She thought of her shabby, old house, her five siblings and how they always used to offer their obligatory prayers.
questions.explanation: 'Shabby' suits an old poor house, 'siblings' suits brothers and sisters, and 'obligatory' suits prayers that must be offered.

questions.question: Where did they build the hospital?
questions.answer: They built the hospital in their own village, standing against the backdrop of lush green fields, so that the villagers would not have to travel to the city for treatment.
questions.explanation: Jameel had dreamed of opening a hospital for the villagers, and he finally built it in the village.

questions.question: Both Sara and Jameel had to pass every test in the first go. Why was it so?
questions.answer: They could not afford to fail or repeat any examination because their family had very little money. Any extra year of study would have meant extra fees and expenses that the family could not bear, so they had to pass every test in the first attempt.
questions.explanation: The text says they could not afford to fail in any subject, since their parents were already struggling to meet the cost of their education.

questions.question: What are some of the problems that might come in your way?
questions.answer: Some problems that might come in my way are: shortage of money to pay the fees; the long distance between my village and the college; tough competition and difficult entry tests; poor health or lack of proper facilities; and sometimes the discouragement of people who do not value education.
questions.explanation: The answer lists the practical difficulties that a village student may meet on the way to a professional career.

questions.question: Who said: 'You people have done so much for me, I think now it's my turn to return the favour.'?
questions.answer: Aunt Sadori.
questions.explanation: Aunt Sadori offers to let Jameel and Sara live with her in the city as a way of repaying the family's kindness to her.

questions.question: The word 'obligatory' means ________.
questions.answer: Obligatory means compulsory or binding; something that must be done as a duty.
questions.explanation: Khalid says that seeking knowledge is 'obligatory' for every male and female.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She also recalled how her mother always ______ meetings for the village women to teach them various skills.
questions.answer: hosted. Full sentence: She also recalled how her mother always hosted meetings for the village women to teach them various skills.
questions.explanation: 'Hosted' means organised and held meetings for guests.

questions.question: How many children did Sara have?
questions.answer: Sara had two young children.
questions.explanation: The text states that two young children were waiting for Sara when Jameel dropped her at her house.

questions.question: How did Sara and Jameel, and their family, manage the expenses for their studies?
questions.answer: Sara and Jameel gave tuitions to the children of the neighbourhood to earn money. Their parents never let them know the problems they faced, and in the fourth year the father and Khalid had to sell a big piece of fertile land to pay their fees. In this way the whole family bore the hardships together.
questions.explanation: The answers show that the entire family sacrificed for the education of the two children.

questions.question: How will you overcome those problems?
questions.answer: I will overcome these problems by giving tuitions and doing part-time work to meet my expenses, by applying for scholarships, by studying with discipline and finishing all my work in time, by taking care of my health, and above all by keeping my faith in God and never losing hope.
questions.explanation: The model answer mirrors Jameel's and Sara's own strategy in the story - hard work and tuition work.

questions.question: Who said: 'Can I really go and study in the city?'?
questions.answer: Sara.
questions.explanation: Sara exclaims these words with joy when Aunt Sadori suggests that both she and Jameel can study in the city.

questions.question: The word 'siblings' means ________.
questions.answer: Siblings means brothers and sisters; children of the same parents.
questions.explanation: Jameel and Sara are the 'siblings' in the story who worked hard together.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Thinking of those times and the life she had now, she thanked God for making it possible for her to ______ her dreams.
questions.answer: realize. Full sentence: She thanked God for making it possible for her to realize her dreams.
questions.explanation: 'Realize' means to make a dream come true, and here the old woman's dreams have been fulfilled.

questions.question: Which vehicle did they travel in?
questions.answer: They travelled to the city in Allah Bachayo's horse cart, and in later years Jameel drove home in his small jeep.
questions.explanation: The mother suggested Allah Bachayo's horse cart for the journey to the city, while the grown-up Jameel uses a small jeep.

questions.question: How did life change for Jameel's family and the villagers?
questions.answer: Jameel became a doctor and opened a hospital in the village, and Sara became a doctor too and worked at the same hospital. The villagers could now get medical treatment in their own village instead of travelling to the city, personal and family health and hygiene improved because of Sara's seminars, and the whole family became prosperous, respected and grateful for their blessings.
questions.explanation: The second part of the story, 'Twelve Years Later', describes the happy and improved life of the family and the village.

questions.question: Who said: 'Jameel can go but Sara should stay here and help her mother.'?
questions.answer: Jameel's father.
questions.explanation: The father says this, showing the old attitude that a girl's place is at home with her mother.

questions.question: The word 'realize' means ________.
questions.answer: Realize means to achieve or make something (a dream or aim) come true.
questions.explanation: The family wanted their children to 'realize' their dreams, i.e. to fulfil them.

questions.question: How was Sara educating the village women?
questions.answer: Sara hosted successful seminars for the village women and guided them to improve their personal and family health and hygiene.
questions.explanation: The text mentions that Jameel was happy because Sara had hosted a successful seminar for the village women.

questions.question: Who said: 'Ok, son, I will follow your advice.'?
questions.answer: Uncle Noor Ali (the old patient).
questions.explanation: The old man replies politely to Dr. Jameel, who had advised him not to eat rice, potatoes and sugar.

questions.question: The word 'weathered' means ________.
questions.answer: Weathered means worn, lined or rough because of age and long exposure to weather.
questions.explanation: Jameel held the old man's 'weathered' hand, which showed the marks of age and hardship.

questions.question: What lessons do we get from the story?
questions.answer: The story teaches us that: (1) hard work, determination and patience can make our dreams come true; (2) education is equally important for boys and girls, and seeking knowledge is obligatory for every male and female; (3) family support and sacrifice are very precious; (4) unity and helping others bring blessings to all; and (5) we should never be discouraged by difficulties and distances.
questions.explanation: The moral is drawn from Jameel's and Sara's long journey of hardship, their family's sacrifices, and their final success in serving the villagers.

questions.question: Who said: 'No, there are no more patients.'?
questions.answer: Allah Dinno.
questions.explanation: Allah Dinno is the attendant at the hospital who answers Dr. Jameel's question about more patients.

questions.question: The word 'impressive' means ________.
questions.answer: Impressive means grand, remarkable or causing admiration because of size, beauty or quality.
questions.explanation: The hospital building was 'impressive', a thing of pride that stood for Jameel's dreams.

questions.question: Who said: 'Come on, let's have lunch.'?
questions.answer: Jameel's wife.
questions.explanation: Jameel's wife greets him with a beaming smile and calls him to lunch when he comes home from work.

questions.question: The word 'backdrop' means ________.
questions.answer: Backdrop means the background against which something is seen or set.
questions.explanation: The hospital stood against the 'backdrop' of lush green fields.

questions.question: The word 'hosted' means ________.
questions.answer: Hosted means organised and held an event and welcomed guests at it.
questions.explanation: Sara had 'hosted' a successful seminar for the village women.

questions.question: The word 'borne' means ________.
questions.answer: Borne means endured, suffered or carried (a burden or hardship).
questions.explanation: The family 'bore' the hardships so that their children could fulfil their dreams.

questions.question: Work in pairs and practise the following dialogue. First one student should take the role of Student A and the other of Student B. Then change roles and repeat the dialogue. Use your real names instead of saying Student A and Student B.
questions.answer:
Model completed dialogue (using the real names Ali and Bilal):
Ali: Assalam-o-Alaikum, Bilal. We missed you yesterday at the party. I wish you had been able to come. It was a nice party.
Bilal: Wa Alaikum Assalam, Ali. I am sorry. Wish you a very happy birthday. Yes, I know the party was good. Everyone enjoyed it. I wish I had come.
Ali: Yes, you really missed it. When are you going to Islamabad?
Bilal: I know, but I had some urgent work. I am going tomorrow evening.
Ali: Wish you a safe journey.
Bilal: Thank you.
questions.explanation: The dialogue shows three uses of 'wish': a wish about something impossible/regret ('I wish you had come'), a greeting ('Wish you a happy birthday') and goodwill ('Wish you a safe journey').

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: It's your friend's birthday today.
questions.answer: Wish you a very happy birthday! I wish you many more happy years of health and success.
questions.explanation: Here 'wish' is used to express a greeting and good will.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: Your friend can't come to your brother's wedding.
questions.answer: I wish you had been able to come to my brother's wedding; it was a wonderful occasion and we missed you a lot.
questions.explanation: Here 'wish' expresses regret about something that is not possible.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: You did not get good marks in your exams.
questions.answer: I wish I had studied harder and got good marks in my exams.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' with the past perfect expresses regret about a past action.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: Your cousins are going to Gilgit for their holidays.
questions.answer: Wish you a safe and pleasant journey, and a very happy holiday in Gilgit!
questions.explanation: 'Wish' is used here to express good will to someone who is travelling.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: It is Eid day today.
questions.answer:
Wish you a very happy Eid! May this Eid bring joy and peace to you and your family.
(Note: This is the example given in the book.)
questions.explanation: The book uses this statement as the worked example, showing 'wish' as a greeting.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: Your teacher is upset because you did not study hard.
questions.answer: I wish I had studied hard and not upset my respected teacher.
questions.explanation: The wish expresses regret about a past mistake.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: You cannot participate in the school sports' day events.
questions.answer: I wish I could participate in the school sports' day events; it is a great pity that I have to miss them.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + could expresses a wish for something that is not possible now.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: One of your classmates is celebrating Christmas.
questions.answer: Wish you a very merry Christmas and a happy New Year!
questions.explanation: 'Wish' expresses a greeting and good will on a festival.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: You have an upset stomach because you ate sweets on which there were flies.
questions.answer: I wish I had not eaten those sweets on which the flies had sat.
questions.explanation: The wish expresses regret about a careless past action.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: It is Independence Day today.
questions.answer: Wish you a very happy Independence Day! May our beloved country always prosper.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' is used here as a greeting on a national day.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: Your cousin has just got married.
questions.answer: Wish you a very happy married life and all the best for the future!
questions.explanation: 'Wish' is used to express good will on a happy occasion.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: You have malaria because you did not protect yourself from mosquitoes.
questions.answer: I wish I had protected myself from mosquitoes and used a mosquito net at night.
questions.explanation: The wish expresses regret about a past mistake that has caused illness.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: One of your close friends is going to Dubai.
questions.answer: Wish you a safe journey and a very pleasant stay in Dubai. I wish I could come with you!
questions.explanation: The first sentence expresses good will, and the second expresses a wish for something impossible.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: Your brother or sister is going for a job interview.
questions.answer: Wish you the very best of luck for your job interview; I hope you get the job!
questions.explanation: 'Wish' is used to express good will before an important event.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: Your neighbours are celebrating Diwali.
questions.answer: Wish you all a very happy Diwali and a year full of brightness and joy!
questions.explanation: 'Wish' is used as a greeting to neighbours on their festival.

questions.question: Express your wish in this situation: There is no electricity and you cannot watch an interesting cricket match.
questions.answer: I wish the electricity would come back soon so that I could watch the interesting cricket match.
questions.explanation: Here 'wish' with 'would' expresses a strong desire for a change in the present situation.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: Sabiha is shivering.
questions.answer: Declarative affirmative.
questions.explanation: This first sentence is done as the example in the book; it makes a statement and is not negative.

questions.question: Change the affirmative sentences in Exercise 1 into negative and the negative ones into affirmative: Sabiha is shivering.
questions.answer: Sabiha is not shivering. (declarative negative)
questions.explanation: The declarative affirmative sentence is made negative by adding 'not' after the verb 'is'.

questions.question: Group activity: Take a key noun and write four types of sentences - declarative affirmative, declarative negative, interrogative affirmative and interrogative negative. Repeat with different key nouns to make twelve sentences.
questions.answer:
Model twelve sentences, using three key nouns:
Key noun 'book':
1. Declarative affirmative: The book is very interesting.
2. Declarative negative: The book is not very interesting.
3. Interrogative affirmative: Is the book very interesting?
4. Interrogative negative: Isn't the book very interesting?
Key noun 'television':
5. Declarative affirmative: Television provides useful information.
6. Declarative negative: Television does not provide useful information.
7. Interrogative affirmative: Does television provide useful information?
8. Interrogative negative: Doesn't television provide useful information?
Key noun 'table':
9. Declarative affirmative: The table is made of wood.
10. Declarative negative: The table is not made of wood.
11. Interrogative affirmative: Is the table made of wood?
12. Interrogative negative: Isn't the table made of wood?
questions.explanation: Steps 1-5 of the exercise ask students to pass the paper round a group and write one type of sentence each turn. The model shows the finished set of twelve edited sentences.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with a, an or the where necessary: I know that ______ Indus is ______ longest river in ______ Pakistan.
questions.answer: I know that the Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used before the name of a river; 'the' is also used before the superlative 'longest'. No article is used before the name of a country such as Pakistan.

questions.question: Fill in the following blanks with the correct articles, where necessary. There are five extra blanks, where an article is not needed.
questions.answer:
In a poor zoo of Pakistan, a lion was very sad as he was given only one kg of meat a day. The lion thought he was the luckiest lion on earth when one day the manager of the Dubai Zoo visited the zoo where the lion was and requested the zoo management to shift the lion to the Dubai Zoo. The lion was very happy and started thinking of having an air conditioned cage and a goat to eat every day.
