On its first day after arrival, the lion was offered a big bag, sealed very nicely, for breakfast. The lion opened it quickly but was shocked to see that the bag contained a few bananas only. The lion thought that since he had recently come from Pakistan, may be the zoo management were worried about upsetting his stomach so they had given him bananas.
The next day the same thing happened. On the third day again when the same food bag of bananas was given to him, the lion stopped the delivery boy and shouted at him, 'Don't you know I am a lion, the king of the jungle? What's wrong with the management of this zoo? What nonsense is this? Why are you delivering bananas to me?'
The delivery boy politely said, 'Sir, I know you are the king of the jungle. But... you have been brought here on a monkey's visa!!!'
The moral of the story is, better to be a lion in your own country than a monkey elsewhere.
questions.explanation: Blanks that need no article are: before 'thinking' (started thinking), before 'stomach' (his stomach), before 'bananas' (given him bananas), before 'nonsense' (What nonsense), and before 'country' (your own country).

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: Are we going to the football field?
questions.answer: Interrogative affirmative.
questions.explanation: It asks a question (interrogative) and has no negative word, so it is affirmative.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: Are we going to the football field?
questions.answer: Aren't we going to the football field? (interrogative negative)
questions.explanation: The interrogative affirmative is turned into an interrogative negative by using 'Aren't'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: In order to learn ______ language, we need two things; ______ good teacher and ______ will to work.
questions.answer: In order to learn a language, we need two things; a good teacher and the will to work.
questions.explanation: 'A' is used with the singular countable nouns 'language' and 'teacher' when they are mentioned generally. 'The will to work' refers to a definite, particular quality.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: The stranger was not calling from the hospital.
questions.answer: Declarative negative.
questions.explanation: It is a statement (declarative) that contains the negative word 'not'.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: The stranger was not calling from the hospital.
questions.answer: The stranger was calling from the hospital. (declarative affirmative)
questions.explanation: The negative word 'not' is removed to make the sentence affirmative.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: ______ capital of ______ Pakistan is ______ Islamabad.
questions.answer: The capital of Pakistan is Islamabad.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used before 'capital' because it is a particular, definite capital. No article is used before Pakistan or Islamabad as they are proper names.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: Will you come to my house tomorrow to study?
questions.answer: Interrogative affirmative.
questions.explanation: It asks a question and is not negative.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: Will you come to my house tomorrow to study?
questions.answer: Won't you come to my house tomorrow to study? (interrogative negative)
questions.explanation: The affirmative question is made negative by contracting 'will not' to 'Won't'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: Some people have ______ bicycles, some have ______ car, I have ______ both.
questions.answer: Some people have bicycles, some have a car, I have both.
questions.explanation: No article is used before the plural 'bicycles' when speaking generally; 'a' is used before the singular countable 'car'; no article is used before 'both'.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: I like to play cricket.
questions.answer: Declarative affirmative.
questions.explanation: It makes a simple positive statement.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: I like to play cricket.
questions.answer: I do not like to play cricket. (declarative negative)
questions.explanation: The simple present affirmative takes the negative form 'do not'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: In many countries, children ______ go to ______ school at ______ age of five.
questions.answer: In many countries, children go to school at the age of five.
questions.explanation: No article is used before 'children' (general plural) or before 'school' in the phrase 'go to school'. 'The' is used in 'the age of five' because a particular age is meant.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: Isn't this your book?
questions.answer: Interrogative negative.
questions.explanation: It is a question that contains the contracted negative form 'Isn't'.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: Isn't this your book?
questions.answer: Is this your book? (interrogative affirmative)
questions.explanation: The negative contraction 'Isn't' is replaced by the affirmative 'Is'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: They are studying ______ geography, and in particular ______ geography of ______ United Arab Emirates.
questions.answer: They are studying geography, and in particular the geography of the United Arab Emirates.
questions.explanation: No article is used before a subject name like 'geography' in general; 'the' is used when it is particularised ('the geography of...'). 'The' is also used before the name of a country with a common noun in it, such as the United Arab Emirates.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: Aren't you the girl who won the gold medal?
questions.answer: Interrogative negative.
questions.explanation: It asks a question and uses the negative contracted form 'Aren't'.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: Aren't you the girl who won the gold medal?
questions.answer: Are you the girl who won the gold medal? (interrogative affirmative)
questions.explanation: The negative contraction 'Aren't' is replaced by the affirmative 'Are'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: Her friend loves eating ______ orange at breakfast time, ______ apple with her lunch, and ______ banana at dinner time.
questions.answer: Her friend loves eating an orange at breakfast time, an apple with her lunch, and a banana at dinner time.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before the vowel sounds 'orange' and 'apple', and 'a' before the consonant sound 'banana' - all singular countable nouns used generally.

questions.question: Write what type of sentence it is: Juman doesn't like to play hockey.
questions.answer: Declarative negative.
questions.explanation: It is a statement containing the negative form 'doesn't'.

questions.question: Change the sentence as directed: Juman doesn't like to play hockey.
questions.answer: Juman likes to play hockey. (declarative affirmative)
questions.explanation: The negative form 'doesn't like' becomes the affirmative 'likes'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: My mother says ______ more you exercise, ______ better your health.
questions.answer: My mother says the more you exercise, the better your health.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used with two comparative degrees used together, as in 'the more ... the better'.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: ______ Chinese are helping ______ Pakistanis to build ______ road from ______ Gwadar to ______ Chinese border.
questions.answer: The Chinese are helping the Pakistanis to build a road from Gwadar to the Chinese border.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used before nationalities used as nouns ('the Chinese', 'the Pakistanis'); 'a' is used before the singular countable 'road'; and 'the' before 'Chinese border' because it is a particular border. No article is used before the place name Gwadar.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles: ______ intelligent person always thinks before speaking, but many ______ people just say whatever comes to their mind.
questions.answer: An intelligent person always thinks before speaking, but many people just say whatever comes to their mind.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before the vowel sound in 'intelligent person' used in a general sense. No article is used before the general plural 'many people'.

questions.question: Email 1: Complete the table column-wise - Sent by, Sent to and Subject.
questions.answer: Email No. 1: Sent by - Iqbal. Sent to - fareed.khan@gmail.com (Fareed Khan). Cc to - sohail.ali@yahoo.com (Sohail Ali). Subject - sports day practice.
questions.explanation: The sender's name appears at the end of the email ('Iqbal'), and the To/Cc/Subject lines give the rest of the details.

questions.question: Work individually and write an informal email to a friend/class fellow asking/requesting for something that you need.
questions.answer:
To: ahmed.raza@gmail.com
Cc:
Subject: need your science notes

Hi Ahmed,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask you for a favour. Our science test is on Monday, and I have lost the notes on 'Matter and its States' that Sir gave us last week. I remember you copied all of them neatly in your notebook. Could you please send me pictures of those pages today or tomorrow? I promise to return the favour by helping you revise for the maths test, as fractions are my strong point.

Please reply soon so that I can start preparing.

questions.question: Read the compare and contrast essay 'Autumn versus Spring'. Underline the words that show similarity and those that show the difference. Then discuss with your partner how a compare and contrast essay is written.
questions.answer:
Words showing difference (contrast): 'But when it comes to culture and practices', 'obvious differences', 'However, there are obvious differences between the two seasons', 'on the other hand', 'instead of getting fully covered, as in spring', 'but this time', 'barren', 'about to come'.
Words showing similarity (comparison): 'one often sees two seasons receiving more attention than the others', 'These two seasons are spring and autumn', 'the arrival of these two seasons is celebrated in various ways', 'The spring season is also associated with rebirth', 'All in all'.
How a compare and contrast essay is written: it has an introductory paragraph with general facts and a clear thesis statement at the end, one body paragraph for each topic or point of comparison, and a concluding paragraph that begins with a signalling phrase such as 'All in all' or 'To sum up', sums up both sides and ends with a general concluding statement or recommendation. Contrast words such as 'however', 'on the other hand' and 'instead of' and comparison words such as 'also', 'both' and 'as in' are used to link the ideas.
questions.explanation: The essay 'Autumn versus Spring' is a model that follows the structure: introduction, one paragraph on spring, one on autumn, and a concluding paragraph summarising the contrast between the two seasons.

questions.question: Work with a partner and write a compare and contrast essay on any one of the following topics: Summer and Winter; Pet and wild animals; City and village life; Good neighbours and bad neighbours.
questions.answer:
City and Village Life

The world we live in offers two different ways of life: life in a big city and life in a small village. Both provide us with a home, work and society, yet they differ greatly in their facilities, environment and pace of life. Though neither way of life is perfect, each has its own advantages and disadvantages.

A city is a very busy and crowded place. It has tall buildings, wide roads, fast traffic and markets that are open till late at night. Cities offer many facilities such as good schools, colleges, hospitals, banks and entertainment centres, and there are many kinds of jobs to choose from. However, the air of a city is often polluted, the houses are small and expensive, and the noise of traffic never seems to stop. People live close together but often do not even know their neighbours.

Life in a village, on the other hand, is calm and simple. The air is fresh, the fields are green and people have more space to live in. In many places villagers still draw water from wells and work on their farms. Village life is also much cheaper, and the people are friendly and help one another in times of need. On the other hand, villages have few schools, colleges and hospitals, and the villagers often have to travel long distances to the city for education and medical treatment. There are also fewer jobs and fewer sources of entertainment.

All in all, city life gives us facilities and opportunities but at the cost of peace and cleanliness, while village life gives us peace and a healthy environment but at the cost of facilities and opportunities. The best way of life, therefore, would be to bring the facilities of the city to the villages so that everyone may enjoy the benefits of both.
questions.explanation: This is a complete model compare and contrast essay following the steps in the unit: brainstorming, a thesis statement in the introduction, one body paragraph for each side, and a concluding paragraph with the signalling phrase 'All in all'. Any of the four given topics may be chosen.

questions.question: Work individually and write a compare and contrast essay on any remaining topic from the four given in Exercise 4. Follow all the steps described above.
questions.answer:
Summer and Winter

A year is made up of four seasons, but summer and winter are the two seasons that affect our lives the most. Both come to us every year in turn, and both control the weather, our clothes, our food and our whole daily routine. Although they are alike in being seasons of the year, they are opposite to each other in every other way.

Summer is the season of heat and long days. The sun shines brightly, the days are long and the nights are short. People wear thin, light and mostly white clothes to keep themselves cool. The bazaars are full of mangoes, watermelons and cold drinks, and children enjoy their long holidays from school. Many families travel to the hills to escape the heat. However, the heat also makes people lazy and thirsty, and load-shedding and water shortage make life difficult for everyone.

Winter, on the other hand, is the season of cold and short days. The days become short and the nights long, and people wear warm clothes such as sweaters, coats and shawls. We like to sit in the sun and eat enjoy hot food such as soup, eggs and dry fruit. Schools open as usual and children get up early in the bitter cold. In many hilly areas, snow falls and covers everything with a white sheet. The cold, however, brings its own problems: poor people suffer a lot, and coughs and colds spread quickly.

All in all, summer fills our lives with heat, colour and holidays, while winter brings cold, quietness and a love of hot food and warm clothes. If summer teaches us to enjoy life in the open air, winter teaches us to bear hardship with patience. Both seasons are necessary for our health, our crops and our environment.
questions.explanation: This is a complete model essay on the remaining topic 'Summer and Winter', written according to the ten steps (a-j) listed in the unit for a compare and contrast essay.

questions.question: Do all the emails begin in the same manner?
questions.answer: No, they do not all begin in the same manner. Email 1 begins with the greeting 'Assalam-o-Alaikum', Email 2 begins with 'Dear Adil,', Email 3 begins directly with the name 'Sunil,' and Email 4 begins with the statement 'This is to inform all of you...'. So the opening of an informal email changes according to the receiver and the purpose.
questions.explanation: Comparing the salutations of the four emails shows that informal emails allow a variety of openings.

questions.question: Do all of them end in the same manner?
questions.answer: No, their endings are also different. Email 1 ends simply with the name 'Iqbal.', Email 2 ends with 'Regards' followed by 'Kapoor', Email 3 ends with 'See you on Saturday. Bye.' followed by 'Adil', and Email 4 ends with a good wish and the name 'Nadia'. The closing may therefore be very short or may include a friendly remark and a good wish.
questions.explanation: The final lines of the four emails show that informal emails have flexible closings.

questions.question: How is the style of these emails different from a letter to a friend?
questions.answer: The emails are short, brief and to the point, and they have a header of To, Cc and Subject instead of the postal address and date used in letters. A letter to a friend is usually longer and more personal, with an address, a date, a salutation and a subscription, while an email goes straight to the matter in a few lines and uses an informal, conversational style.
questions.explanation: Emails are meant to be quick, so unnecessary formalities such as addresses and dates are dropped.

questions.question: Is the language use and vocabulary same or different? How?
questions.answer: The language use and vocabulary are partly the same and partly different, depending on the receiver and the purpose. All four emails use simple, informal, conversational English with contractions and short sentences, but Email 1 and Email 3 are very friendly and chatty ('What do you say', 'Bye', 'See you'), while Email 4 is a group notice written in a more informative, matter-of-fact style. So the vocabulary stays informal but its tone changes with the occasion.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary in informal emails is chosen to suit the person being written to and the reason for writing.

questions.question: Did you notice what is written in the subject line?
questions.answer: Yes. The subject line gives a very short and clear idea of what the email is about. In the four emails the subjects are 'sports day practice', 'maths homework', 'maths homework' and 'wedding invitation'. Good subject lines are short, to the point and use a few key words so that the reader knows at once what the email is about.
questions.explanation: The subject line is one of the chief differences between an email and a letter.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you eat a diet that includes fruits and vegetables?
questions.answer: Always. A diet that includes fruits and vegetables supplies the body with vitamins, minerals and fibre, which keep us healthy and protect us from many diseases. A person who never eats them may suffer from weakness and deficiency diseases.
questions.explanation: This is a sample filled-in questionnaire; the answer given is the healthy one, with the reason why that habit matters.

questions.question: Creating a newspaper - think about: Name of your newspaper.
questions.answer: Model: We will name our newspaper 'The Healthy Times'. The name is short, easy to remember and clearly tells the reader that our newspaper is about health and healthy habits.
questions.explanation: The name should be short and should show the topic (unhealthy habits) at once.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you brush your teeth twice a day?
questions.answer: Always. Brushing the teeth twice a day removes plaque and food particles and prevents tooth decay, gum disease and bad breath.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that regular brushing protects the teeth.

questions.question: Creating a newspaper - think about: Articles, news items, stories that you will put in your newspaper.
questions.answer: Model contents: (1) A main article, 'Why We Must Wash Our Hands with Soap'. (2) A news item, 'Our School Launches a Cleanliness Drive'. (3) An interview with the school doctor, 'Eight Hours of Sleep: A Must for Students'. (4) A short story, 'A Week without Vegetables', showing the result of bad eating habits.
questions.explanation: The articles and items should all be about the unhealthy habits found in the questionnaire.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you bathe regularly?
questions.answer: Always. Taking a bath regularly keeps the skin clean, washes away sweat and germs, and prevents skin infections and body odour.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that regular bathing keeps the body clean and free of germs.

questions.question: Creating a newspaper - think about: Advertisements related to your topic / other advertisements.
questions.answer:
Model advertisements: (1) A health-based advertisement for a soap brand, 'Clean hands keep the doctor away'.
(2) An advertisement for a fruit and vegetable shop, 'Fresh fruits and vegetables - the secret of good health'.
(3) An advertisement for the local gym, 'Exercise daily, live longer'.
(4) A school event advertisement, 'Come to our Health Week exhibition!'
questions.explanation: The advertisements should be connected with the topic of healthy and unhealthy habits, and may be designed in boxes like real newspaper ads.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you wash your hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet?
questions.answer: Always. Soap removes the germs that our hands pick up, and so protects us from diseases such as diarrhoea, typhoid and cholera.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that hand-washing with soap is one of the best ways of stopping the spread of disease.

questions.question: Creating a newspaper - think about: Pictures, quotes, jokes, etc. that you will use.
questions.answer: Model material: Picture - a chart showing the six steps of washing hands; Picture - a drawing of a boy eating fruits and vegetables. Quote - 'Cleanliness is half of faith.' Quote - 'Health is wealth.' Joke - 'Pupil: Doctor, why do you always tell me to sleep early? Doctor: Because I want you to see your books in the morning as well!' Cartoon - a toothbrush telling a piece of chocolate, 'We must not meet so often!'
questions.explanation: Pictures, quotes and jokes make a school newspaper attractive as well as informative.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you sleep 8 hours at night?
questions.answer: Always. Eight hours of sleep at night rest and refresh the body and mind, improve memory and concentration, and keep a person active and cheerful during the day.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that enough sleep is necessary for good health.

questions.question: Creating a newspaper - think about: Who will do what? Which group member will do what and by when?
questions.answer:
Model work plan (group of four):
1. Ali (Editor) - will collect all the material, edit the language and arrange the layout. Deadline: Monday.
2. Sana (Writer) - will write the main article and the short story. Deadline: Tuesday.
3. Bilal (Reporter) - will prepare the news item, the doctor's interview and the advertisements. Deadline: Tuesday.
4. Hina (Artist) - will draw the pictures and cartoons, and do the final printing and display. Deadline: Wednesday.
questions.explanation: This is the model division of work and timetable that the group should decide before starting the newspaper.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you use a handkerchief or tissue while coughing or sneezing?
questions.answer: Always. Covering the mouth and nose with a handkerchief or tissue while coughing or sneezing stops our germs from flying into the air and spreading to other people.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that it is good manners and good health practice.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you wash your eyes with cold water regularly?
questions.answer: Always. Washing the eyes with clean cold water regularly removes dust and germs, soothes tired eyes and helps to prevent eye infections.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that clean eyes need regular washing.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you cut and clean your nails regularly?
questions.answer: Always. If the nails are long, dirt and germs collect under them, and these germs go into the body with food and cause illness. Cleaning and cutting the nails regularly keeps the hands clean and healthy.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that long dirty nails carry disease.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you read while lying down?
questions.answer: Never. Reading while lying down strains the eyes and can weaken the eyesight, so one should always read sitting up with good light.
questions.explanation: For this habit the healthy answer is 'Never' - the only question in the questionnaire where the good answer is a negative one.

questions.question: Complete the questionnaire: Do you exercise regularly?
questions.answer: Always. Regular exercise keeps the muscles and bones strong, controls body weight, and keeps the heart and lungs healthy. It also refreshes the mind and reduces stress.
questions.explanation: The healthy answer is 'Always', with the reason that exercise is essential for both physical and mental health.

questions.question: Pre-reading 1: What qualities does a visionary have? Work in groups of three and decide which of the qualities given in the web is the most important for a visionary leader to have and which is the least important. Add one more quality that is not given. Number all the listed qualities in order of priority, with 1 being the most important and 13 being the least important.
questions.answer:
The web lists twelve qualities of a visionary: inspiration, integrity, clear goals, good example, vision, clear communication, expects the best, support, encouragement, recognition, stimulating work, and focus on team interests and needs. One more quality that is not given can be added, for example 'honesty'.

Model order of priority (1 = most important, 13 = least important):
1. vision
2. integrity
3. clear goals
4. clear communication
5. honesty (added)
6. good example
7. inspiration
8. support
9. encouragement
10. focus on team interests and needs
11. recognition
12. expects the best
13. stimulating work

There is no single correct order; the importance of each quality depends on the aim, personality and resources of the leader and the situation.
questions.explanation: A visionary is a person who can plan the future with imagination and wisdom. The Pre-reading web task asks students to rank the qualities that make a good visionary leader and to add one of their own.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Complete the table given in task 2 of the Pre-Reading section: What did you learn after reading the text? Share your table with your partner.

questions.question: Exercise 3: Read the text. Find the following 24 words and underline them. Guess the meanings with your partner and check them in the glossary: dynamic, steadfastness, guiding principles, unparalleled, undesired, acumen, proponent, polarization, aspirations, envisioned, pluralistic, discrimination, prevailed, impartiality, transform, implementing, versatile, accomplishments, culminating, recall, victimization, distinction, homage, quest.
questions.answer:
Meanings of the words:
1. dynamic - full of energy, force and new ideas; active and vigorous.
2. steadfastness - firmness of purpose or loyalty; not changing one's determination.
3. guiding principles - the main rules or beliefs that direct one's actions.
4. unparalleled - having no equal; matchless.
5. undesired - not wanted or wished for.
6. acumen - sharp judgement and quick understanding, especially in practical matters.
7. proponent - a person who argues in favour of something; a supporter.
8. polarization - division into two sharply opposed groups.
9. aspirations - strong desires or ambitions; hopes.
10. envisioned - imagined or pictured as a future possibility.
11. pluralistic - made up of many different groups, ideas or beliefs.
12. discrimination - unfair treatment of people on the basis of race, religion, etc.
13. prevailed - won; proved stronger in the end.
14. impartiality - fairness; not favouring one side over another.
15. transform - to change completely in form or nature.
16. implementing - putting a plan or decision into effect.
17. versatile - able to do many different things well.
18. accomplishments - achievements; things done successfully.
19. culminating - reaching the highest or final point.
20. recall - to remember.
21. victimization - the act of treating someone unfairly or making them suffer.
22. distinction - a difference between things; also a mark of honour.
23. homage - deep respect or tribute shown to someone.
24. quest - a long search or effort to achieve something.
questions.explanation: This vocabulary exercise appears in the 'While Reading' section and asks students to locate the listed words in the text and derive their meanings from context before verifying them in the glossary.

8. polarization - The debate caused a polarization of opinion in the assembly.
12. discrimination - The law forbids discrimination on the basis of religion or caste.
16. implementing - The government is implementing a new plan to improve schools.
20. recall - I cannot recall the exact date of the event.
24. quest - The scientist's quest for knowledge never ended.
questions.explanation: This task ensures that the new vocabulary is actively used. Each student writes original sentences with the six words allotted to their number, after which the group exchanges notebooks and gives feedback.

questions.question: Exercise 5, Statement 1: Jinnah wanted Muslims to have more rights in Pakistan. Tick True or False.
questions.answer: False.
questions.explanation: The text says the Quaid envisioned a state ensuring equal rights for all citizens. He did not want more rights for Muslims; he wanted Muslims and people of other faiths to be equal citizens.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 1: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'You are free; you are free to go to your temples,'
questions.answer: Quote part: (d) 'you are free to go to your mosques or to any other place of worship in this state of Pakistan.' Person: Q (Quaid-e-Azam).
questions.explanation: This sentence comes from the Quaid-e-Azam's address to the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947, in which he declared that all citizens were free to worship as they wished.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Go back to Exercise 6 and find out when and where these words were spoken. Write a complete sentence: (1) 'You are free; you are free to go to your temples...'
questions.answer: On 11 August 1947, in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, the Quaid-e-Azam said these words.
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 requires students to turn the matched quotes into full sentences, adding the occasion, date and place at which each quotation was delivered.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Work in pairs and orally discuss the reasons for the statement, then rewrite it stating the reason: (1) Jinnah's achievement is unparalleled in recent history.
questions.answer: Jinnah's achievement is unparalleled in recent history because, unlike most other leaders who only freed their countries from foreign rule, he not only got freedom but also managed to create a new state for the Muslims.
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 asks students to explain and rewrite statements with reasons. This first item is worked as the example in the book.

questions.question: Exercise 9: Work in groups of three and make mind-maps on the following aspects of both these great personalities: (for the Quaid) Qualities as a person, Vision for Pakistan, What should we do to make Pakistan great; (for Iqbal) Academic achievements, Dream about Pakistan, Advice to Muslims.
questions.answer:
Mind-map: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah
- Qualities as a person: dynamic personality; determination and steadfastness; tolerance and acceptance of all faiths; honesty and integrity; a great barrister; forceful speaker; respect for all communities.
- Vision for Pakistan: a 'nation state' ensuring equal rights for all citizens; freedom of worship for every community; a state where justice and merit prevail; a united, exemplary nation working for peace and prosperity.
- What should we do to make Pakistan great: implement the Quaid's vision rather than merely praising him; work hard, honestly and unitedly; put the country before self; follow 'Unity, Faith and Discipline'; take Pakistan forward on the path of peace and prosperity.

Mind-map: Allama Muhammad Iqbal
- Academic achievements: M.A. in 1899; Professor of Arabic at the Oriental College, Lahore; studied law in London and became a barrister in 1905; awarded a Ph.D. by Munich University in Germany in 1908 for his work on Persian philosophy.
- Dream about Pakistan: a separate Muslim state where Muslims could live honourably and according to their faith and culture; a state uniting Punjab, the North West Frontier Province, Sindh and Baluchistan.
- Advice to Muslims: remain true to Islam and practise it in letter and spirit; do not lose faith in difficult times, for it is Islam that has saved the Muslims; stay strong and united; work hard and never give up hope.
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 asks students to organise the information about both leaders into mind-maps, using three aspects for each personality, so that knowledge is neatly classified.

questions.question: Pre-reading 2: Fill the first two columns of the following table about Quaid-e-Azam and Allama Iqbal (What I think I know / What I want to know). After you have filled the two columns, share with your partner.
questions.answer:
Model filled table.

What I think I know:
- Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was the founder of Pakistan and its first Governor-General.
- Allama Iqbal was a great poet and philosopher, called the 'Poet of the East'.
- Iqbal first put forward the idea of a separate Muslim state.
- Both men were lawyers and both worked for the Muslims of South Asia.

What I want to know:
- What exactly were Jinnah's personal qualities and achievements?
- What was Iqbal's political contribution to the Pakistan Movement?
- What kind of Pakistan did each of them dream of?
- How did Iqbal's and Jinnah's ideas for the Muslims differ or match?
questions.explanation: This K-W-L (Know-Want-Learned) table activates prior knowledge before reading. The first two columns are completed before reading and the third column (What I learned) is completed later in Exercise 1.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Find out the name of the student who collected information on: (b) Political acumen and contribution of Allama Iqbal.
questions.answer: Farheen collected the information on the political acumen and contribution of Allama Iqbal.
questions.explanation: Farheen's email (dated June 19, 2018) is headed 'Political Acumen and Contribution' and deals with Allama Iqbal's political work and his Allahabad address.

questions.question: Exercise 5, Statement 2: Zoya and Amber offered to find information about Allama Iqbal. Tick True or False.
questions.answer: False.
questions.explanation: The text says Lubna and Farheen agreed to find information about Iqbal, while Huma and Tahira looked up information on Jinnah. The names Zoya and Amber do not appear in the text.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 2: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'To me he was a friend, guide and philosopher,'
questions.answer: Quote part: (f) 'and during the darkest moments through which the Muslim League had to go, he stood like a rock.' Person: Q (Quaid-e-Azam).
questions.explanation: These words were spoken by the Quaid-e-Azam in a message of praise on the death of Allama Iqbal, describing Iqbal's steadfast support for the Muslim League.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Write a complete sentence stating when and where these words were spoken: (2) 'To me he was a friend, guide and philosopher...'
questions.answer: In a message issued after the death of Allama Iqbal in 1938, the Quaid-e-Azam said these words.
questions.explanation: The Quaid-e-Azam praised Iqbal's role in a message on his death, calling him a friend, guide and philosopher who stood like a rock in dark times.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (2) The Quaid was greatly respected by the people of all faiths.
questions.answer: The Quaid was greatly respected by the people of all faiths because he was tolerant and accepted all faiths; indeed, Hindu leaders like Gokhale and the famous Hindu poetess Sarojini Naidoo called him the best ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity.
questions.explanation: The reason is given in Huma's email, which explains that Jinnah was popular among Hindus, Christians, Sikhs and Parsis because of his tolerance and acceptance of all faiths.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Find out the name of the student who collected information on: (c) The Quaid's aspirations for the Muslims.
questions.answer: Huma collected the information on the Quaid-e-Azam's aspirations for Pakistan (i.e. his vision for the Muslims).
questions.explanation: Huma's email (dated June 17, 2018) is headed 'Aspirations for Pakistan' and describes the Quaid's vision of a nation state with equal rights for all.

questions.question: Exercise 5, Statement 3: Quaid-e-Azam first joined the Congress and then the Muslim League. Tick True or False.
questions.answer: True.
questions.explanation: The text states that initially the Quaid-e-Azam was an active member of the Indian National Congress and later left it to join the Muslim League, becoming its president.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 3: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'The Muslim demand to create a Muslim India within India'
questions.answer: Quote part: (a) 'is in no way without justice.' Person: A (Allama Iqbal).
questions.explanation: This statement comes from Allama Iqbal's presidential address at the Allahabad meeting of the All-India Muslim League in 1930.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Write a complete sentence stating when and where these words were spoken: (3) 'The Muslim demand to create a Muslim India within India is in no way without justice.'
questions.answer: In 1930, when he presided over the Allahabad meeting of the All-India Muslim League, Allama Iqbal said these words.
questions.explanation: In his famous Allahabad address of 1930, Iqbal made the first definite demand for a separate Muslim state in South Asia.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (3) Quaid-e-Azam left the Indian National Congress.
questions.answer: Quaid-e-Azam left the Indian National Congress because, as an outstanding political leader, he sensed that the Congress was leading the Hindus of the sub-continent towards Hindu-Muslim polarization, which would result in the political and economic victimization of the Muslims.
questions.explanation: This reason is given in Tahira's email under the heading 'Political Acumen and Contribution'.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Find out the name of the student who collected information on: (d) Allama Iqbal's aspirations for the Muslims.
questions.answer: Tahira collected the information on Allama Iqbal's aspirations for the Muslims.
questions.explanation: Tahira's email (dated June 20, 2018), headed 'Aspirations for Muslims', explains Iqbal's wish that Muslims should remain true to their faith and practise it in letter and spirit.

questions.question: Exercise 5, Statement 4: Both Quaid-e-Azam and Allama Iqbal were barristers. Tick True or False.
questions.answer: True.
questions.explanation: The text says the Quaid was one of the top barristers of Bombay, and that Allama Iqbal studied law in London and became a barrister by profession.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 4: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'At difficult moments in their history, it is Islam'
questions.answer: Quote part: (e) 'that has saved Muslims and not Muslims that have saved Islam.' Person: A (Allama Iqbal).
questions.explanation: This is from Allama Iqbal's Allahabad address, in which he advised the Muslims to keep their faith in Islam strong and united.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Write a complete sentence stating when and where these words were spoken: (4) 'At difficult moments in their history, it is Islam that has saved Muslims...'
questions.answer: In 1930, in his Allahabad address, Allama Iqbal said these words.
questions.explanation: In the same Allahabad address, Iqbal advised the Muslims that their strength and unity lay in putting their faith in Islam.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (4) Despite strong opposition by the British and the Hindus, Quaid-e-Azam succeeded in creating Pakistan.
questions.answer: Despite strong opposition by the British and the Hindus, Quaid-e-Azam succeeded in creating Pakistan because of his determination, steadfastness and political acumen, with which he intelligently pleaded the case of a separate homeland for the Muslims.
questions.explanation: The text states that Jinnah succeeded despite the two big power players in British India because of his intelligent pleading of the Muslim case and his determination.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Find out the name of the student who collected information on: (e) Personality and achievements of Allama Iqbal.
questions.answer: Lubna collected the information on the personality and achievements of Allama Iqbal.
questions.explanation: Lubna's email (dated June 18, 2018), headed 'Personality and Achievements', gives Allama Iqbal's academic and professional accomplishments.

questions.question: Exercise 5, Statement 5: Allama Iqbal wrote two letters to Quaid-e-Azam in 1938. Tick True or False.
questions.answer: False.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention any letters written by Iqbal to the Quaid. It only says that Iqbal died in 1938, nine years before the creation of Pakistan.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 5: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'My guiding principle will be'
questions.answer: Quote part: (c) 'justice and complete impartiality.' Person: Q (Quaid-e-Azam).
questions.explanation: The Quaid-e-Azam said these words while describing his guiding principle for the new state of Pakistan, promising justice and fair treatment for all.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Write a complete sentence stating when and where these words were spoken: (5) 'My guiding principle will be justice and complete impartiality.'
questions.answer: On 11 August 1947, in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, the Quaid-e-Azam said these words.
questions.explanation: The Quaid-e-Azam gave this assurance of justice and impartiality in his address to the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (5) Allama Iqbal could point out some of the defects in the philosophical systems of the West.
questions.answer: Allama Iqbal could point out some of the defects in the philosophical systems of the West because he was a versatile scholar and researcher who was awarded a Ph.D. degree by the Munich University in Germany for his work on Persian philosophy.
questions.explanation: Lubna's email describes Iqbal's deep scholarship and his Ph.D. on Persian philosophy, which enabled him to compare and criticise Western philosophical systems.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Find out the name of the student who collected information on: (f) The Quaid's political acumen and contribution.
questions.answer: Tahira collected the information on the Quaid's political acumen and contribution.
questions.explanation: Tahira's email (dated June 15, 2018), headed 'Political Acumen and Contribution', explains how Jinnah left the Congress and joined the Muslim League and successfully pleaded the case for a separate homeland.

questions.question: Exercise 5, Statement 6: In his letters he said that Muslims should demand a separate state. Tick True or False.
questions.answer: False.
questions.explanation: The demand for a separate Muslim state was made by Allama Iqbal in his Allahabad address of 1930, not in any letters. The statement about letters is therefore not supported by the text.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 6: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'I am sure that with your support and cooperation, I can look forward'
questions.answer: Quote part: (g) 'to Pakistan becoming one of the greatest nations of the world.' Person: Q (Quaid-e-Azam).
questions.explanation: The Quaid-e-Azam expressed this hope for Pakistan's future, urging the people to work together to make the new country an exemplary state.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Write a complete sentence stating when and where these words were spoken: (6) 'I am sure that with your support and cooperation, I can look forward to Pakistan becoming one of the greatest nations of the world.'
questions.answer: On 11 August 1947, in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, the Quaid-e-Azam said these words.
questions.explanation: The Quaid-e-Azam expressed this hope while urging the people of Pakistan to extend their support and cooperation to build the new nation.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (6) Dr. Iqbal did not seek re-election to the Punjab Legislative Council.
questions.answer: Dr. Iqbal did not seek re-election to the Punjab Legislative Council because he had by then become deeply involved with the activities of the Muslim League and with the cause of Muslim rights.
questions.explanation: Farheen's email explains that Iqbal was a member of the Punjab Legislative Council from 1926 to 1929, after which he devoted himself fully to the Muslim League.

questions.question: Exercise 6, Quote 7: Match the quote part and identify the person: 'We are all citizens'
questions.answer: Quote part: (b) 'and equal citizens of one State.' Person: Q (Quaid-e-Azam).
questions.explanation: In his first address to the Constituent Assembly, the Quaid-e-Azam declared that all citizens of Pakistan would enjoy equal rights with no distinction between communities.

questions.question: Exercise 7: Write a complete sentence stating when and where these words were spoken: (7) 'We are all citizens and equal citizens of one State.'
questions.answer: On 11 August 1947, in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, the Quaid-e-Azam said these words.
questions.explanation: In his first address to the Constituent Assembly, the Quaid-e-Azam stressed the fundamental principle that all citizens of Pakistan were equal.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (7) One of Iqbal's biggest political contributions is his Allahabad address.
questions.answer: One of Iqbal's biggest political contributions is his Allahabad address because it was on that historic occasion, when he presided over the Allahabad meeting of the All-India Muslim League in 1930, that he made a definite demand for a separate Muslim state in South Asia.
questions.explanation: The text says Iqbal's Allahabad address of 1930 planted the demand for a separate Muslim state, which later led to the Pakistan Resolution of 1940.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Rewrite the statement stating the reason: (8) Allama Iqbal wanted the Muslims to put their faith in Islam.
questions.answer: Allama Iqbal wanted the Muslims to put their faith in Islam because he had learnt from the history of the Muslims that at difficult moments it was Islam that had saved the Muslims, and that if they put their faith in Islam they would become strong and united once again.
questions.explanation: This reason is drawn from Tahira's email, which quotes Iqbal's Allahabad address advising Muslims to remain true to their faith in letter and in spirit.

questions.question: 4.2 Listening and Speaking (Focus: Asking and responding to questions of academic nature): Work in groups of eight/ten students and hold a press conference. Three or four students represent one ministry while five or six are reporters from the media. Each group represents one ministry (Ministry of Health, Power, Water, Sanitation or Education). The ministry members each say one thing their ministry is doing or plans to do; each reporter asks at least two questions and the panelists answer them.
questions.answer:
Model press conference outline (for the Ministry of Education).

Panelists' opening statements:
1. 'Our ministry is introducing interactive whiteboards and digital textbooks in all government high schools so that learning becomes more effective.'
2. 'We are launching a free midday meal programme so that no child has to study on an empty stomach.'
3. 'We are training ten thousand primary teachers every year in modern teaching methods.'

Reporters' questions and model answers:
Q1. 'How much of the education budget has actually been spent on these programmes this year?'
A. 'Nearly eighty per cent of the funds have been released and the rest will be spent before the end of the financial year.'
Q2. 'When will the midday meal programme reach the rural districts?'
A. 'The first phase, covering the major cities, is already complete; the rural districts will be covered within the next twelve months.'
Q3. 'How will you measure whether students are actually learning better?'
A. 'Standardised tests are conducted every term, and the results are compared with the previous year's performance to judge improvement.'
Q4. 'Will parents have to pay anything for the digital textbooks?'
A. 'No. The digital textbooks are completely free and are also available on the ministry's website.'

Procedure: brainstorm in groups, assign roles (at least three or four panelists and five or six reporters), prepare the dialogues, then role-play the conference in front of the class while other groups act as the audience and ask further questions.
questions.explanation: This is a speaking task in which students practise asking and answering questions of an academic nature by simulating a government press conference. The answer gives a complete model for the Ministry of Education, which can be adapted for the other ministries.

questions.question: 4.3 Exercise 1 (Revision: Fluency practice for changing the voice in sentences): Get ready to play an oral game. Change the voice of the sentence without changing the meaning. Divide the class into two groups; each group writes a list of 8-10 active and passive voice sentences; Group A says a sentence and Group B changes its voice aloud, and vice versa.
questions.answer:
Model sentences for the game (each active sentence with its passive version).

1. Active: The teacher praised the students. / Passive: The students were praised by the teacher.
2. Active: Ali ate the grapes. / Passive: The grapes were eaten by Ali.
3. Active: The government has released the funds. / Passive: The funds have been released by the government.
4. Active: The army is doing the rescue work. / Passive: The rescue work is being done by the army.
5. Active: Someone had emptied the cupboard. / Passive: The cupboard had been emptied.
6. Active: The peon will deliver the letter. / Passive: The letter will be delivered by the peon.
7. Active: Our team won the match. / Passive: The match was won by our team.
8. Active: The company prints these books. / Passive: These books are printed by the company.

Rule reminder: the passive voice is formed with the correct form of 'be' plus the past participle (is cleaned, were given, has been given, was being given, had been given); for the future we use 'will be' plus the past participle (will be given, will be told).
questions.explanation: This is a fluency game in which one group calls out a sentence and the other group converts it into the opposite voice. The answer gives ten ready examples plus the tense table needed to change the voice correctly.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Work in pairs and complete the following news report using the correct form of the passive, using the verbs given in brackets: 'The northern part of the country was hit (hit) by a massive earthquake this morning. The entire infrastructure ______ (damage) very badly. The roads ______ (break). The telephone lines ______ (destroy), and the mobile services ______ (disrupt). The people ______ (scare) as many aftershocks ______ (expect). Food, water and medical aid ______ (rush) to the area. An appeal ______ (make) by the government asking people not to panic. Work ______ (do) by the army to enable reaching of aid to the remote areas. Funds ______ (release) by the government to help people in this hour of grief.'
questions.answer: The northern part of the country was hit by a massive earthquake this morning. The entire infrastructure was damaged very badly. The roads were broken. The telephone lines were destroyed, and the mobile services were disrupted. The people were scared as many aftershocks were expected. Food, water and medical aid were rushed to the area. An appeal was made by the government asking people not to panic. Work was done by the army to enable reaching of aid to the remote areas. Funds were released by the government to help people in this hour of grief.
questions.explanation: All the blanks require the simple past passive (was/were + past participle) because the news report describes completed past events. The completed report is written in the notebook as instructed.

questions.question: Exercise 3: Read the story about Samina and her servant. Then work with a partner and orally complete Samina's report to the police, using the passive form and the verbs from the story: 'A new servant was hired by me. She ______ to submit a copy of her identity card. A copy ______ by her. I ______ someone else's card to me by her. Unfortunately, the details ______ by me. After a few days, I ______ by the servant for a loan. The loan ______ by me. The following week, I ______ told a sad story by the servant and again I ______ for some money. The servant ______ not to come to work from the next day. When I went to my room, after a couple of hours, it ______ in a mess, with all the things on the floor. The cupboard ______ by her. All the money and the jewellery ______ by her.'
questions.answer: A new servant was hired by me. She was asked to submit a copy of her identity card. A copy was given by her. I was given someone else's card by her. Unfortunately, the details were not checked by me. After a few days, I was asked by the servant for a loan. The loan was refused by me. The following week, I was told a sad story by the servant and again I was asked for some money. The servant was told not to come to work from the next day. When I went to my room, after a couple of hours, it was found in a mess, with all the things on the floor. The cupboard was emptied by her. All the money and the jewellery were taken away by her.
questions.explanation: The report is a continuous narrative of past events, so the simple past passive (was/were + past participle) is used throughout. Note the negative form 'were not checked' and the plural verb 'were taken away'.

questions.question: Exercise 4 A, Sentence 1: Fill in the blank using the prefix 're' with the appropriate given word (tell, do, claim, apply, print, arrange): 'The government is trying to ______ land from the sea in Karachi.' (done as example)
questions.answer: The government is trying to reclaim land from the sea in Karachi.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're' means 'again' or 'back'. The example 'reclaim' (re + claim) is completed in the book to show how the prefix is used.

questions.question: Exercise 4 A, Sentence 2: Fill in the blank using the prefix 're': 'The company had to ______ this book three times.'
questions.answer: The company had to reprint this book three times.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're' (again) is added to 'print' to form 'reprint', meaning to print again.

questions.question: Exercise 4 A, Sentence 3: Fill in the blank using the prefix 're': 'I advised my friend to ______ for a teaching position in our school.'
questions.answer: I advised my friend to reapply for a teaching position in our school.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're' is added to 'apply' to form 'reapply', meaning to apply again.

questions.question: Exercise 4 A, Sentence 4: Fill in the blank using the prefix 're': 'My father likes to ______ his childhood stories to his grandchildren.'
questions.answer: My father likes to retell his childhood stories to his grandchildren.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're' is added to 'tell' to form 'retell', meaning to tell again.

questions.question: Exercise 4 A, Sentence 5: Fill in the blank using the prefix 're': 'Saira and Khalida decided to ______ the furniture in their room.'
questions.answer: Saira and Khalida decided to rearrange the furniture in their room.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're' is added to 'arrange' to form 'rearrange', meaning to arrange again or differently.

questions.question: Exercise 4 A, Sentence 6: Fill in the blank using the prefix 're': 'The teacher told the class to ______ the exercise.'
questions.answer: The teacher told the class to redo the exercise.
questions.explanation: The prefix 're' is added to 'do' to form 'redo', meaning to do again.

questions.question: Exercise 4 B, Sentence 1: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'mis' with the appropriate given word (treat, match, behave, understand, place): 'When children ______ they are often punished by their parents.'
questions.answer: When children misbehave they are often punished by their parents.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis' means 'badly' or 'wrongly'. 'Misbehave' means to behave badly.

questions.question: Exercise 4 B, Sentence 2: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'mis': 'My brothers always ______ their mobile phones.'
questions.answer: My brothers always misplace their mobile phones.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis' is added to 'place' to form 'misplace', meaning to put something in the wrong place and then not be able to find it.

questions.question: Exercise 4 B, Sentence 3: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'mis': 'There is a ______ between their income and expenditure.'
questions.answer: There is a mismatch between their income and expenditure.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis' is added to 'match' to form 'mismatch', meaning a wrong or unsuitable pairing; the two things do not correspond.

questions.question: Exercise 4 B, Sentence 4: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'mis': 'Many people ______ their leader's message.'
questions.answer: Many people misunderstand their leader's message.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis' is added to 'understand' to form 'misunderstand', meaning to understand something wrongly.

questions.question: Exercise 4 B, Sentence 5: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'mis': 'It is not right to ______ servants.'
questions.answer: It is not right to mistreat servants.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis' is added to 'treat' to form 'mistreat', meaning to treat someone badly or cruelly.

questions.question: Exercise 4 C, Sentence 1: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'inter' with the appropriate given word (national, faith, personal, city, dependent): 'The ______ bus service is very good in some countries.'
questions.answer: The intercity bus service is very good in some countries.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'inter' means 'between'. 'Intercity' means between cities.

questions.question: Exercise 4 C, Sentence 2: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'inter': 'There is more ______ travel today than about fifty years ago.'
questions.answer: There is more international travel today than about fifty years ago.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'inter' is added to 'national' to form 'international', meaning between or among nations.

questions.question: Exercise 4 C, Sentence 3: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'inter': 'For success in any work good ______ skills are needed.'
questions.answer: For success in any work good interpersonal skills are needed.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'inter' is added to 'personal' to form 'interpersonal', meaning relating to relationships between people.

questions.question: Exercise 4 C, Sentence 4: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'inter': 'The quality of goods and their price are ______.'
questions.answer: The quality of goods and their price are interdependent.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'inter' is added to 'dependent' to form 'interdependent', meaning depending on each other.

questions.question: Exercise 4 C, Sentence 5: Fill in the blank using the prefix 'inter': '______ understanding is very important for peace in the world.'
questions.answer: Interfaith understanding is very important for peace in the world.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'inter' is added to 'faith' to form 'interfaith', meaning between or among different religions.

questions.question: 4.4 Exercise 1 (Paraphrasing a Poem): Underline the following words in the poem and discuss their possible meanings with a partner, then check them in the glossary: longing, supplication, sparkling, attain, elegance, moth, supportive, suffering.
questions.answer:
Meanings of the words in the poem 'A Child's Invocation':
- longing - a strong, deep desire; a heartfelt wish.
- supplication - a humble and earnest prayer or request made to God.
- sparkling - shining brightly with small flashes of light; glittering.
- attain - to reach or achieve something, especially after effort.
- elegance - beauty and grace in appearance or style.
- moth - a small winged insect that is attracted to a flame or light.
- supportive - giving help, encouragement or backing to others.
- suffering - experiencing pain, hardship or distress.
questions.explanation: Exercise 1 is a vocabulary step before paraphrasing. Students identify the difficult words of the poem and work out their meanings from context before confirming them in the glossary.

questions.question: Exercise 2, Couplet 1: Paraphrase the first couplet of Allama Iqbal's poem 'A Child's Invocation'. (The book gives this paraphrase as the example: 'Oh Allah! I pray that my life should be like a candle.') Original: 'My longing comes to my lips as supplication of mine / O God! May like the candle be the life of mine!'
questions.answer: Oh Allah! I pray that my life should be like a candle.
questions.explanation: This paraphrase is given as the worked example in the book. The paraphrase restates the candle imagery in simple prose: the poet prays that his life, like a candle, should give light and sacrifice itself for others.

questions.question: Exercise 3: Write the paraphrased poem 'A Child's Invocation' in the form of a paragraph in your notebook.
questions.answer:
A Child's Invocation (Paraphrase):
The poet humbly prays to Allah and asks that his life should be like a candle that burns itself to give light to others. He wishes that through the light of his life the darkness of the world should disappear and that every place should shine with his bright light. He prays that his homeland should gain grace and beauty through him, just as a garden becomes beautiful through its flowers. He asks the Lord to make his life like the moth that sacrifices itself for the flame, and to fill his heart with the love of the lamp of knowledge. He prays that his way of life should be to support the poor and to love the old and the suffering. Finally, he begs God to protect him from evil ways and to show him the path that leads to goodness.
questions.explanation: Exercise 3 combines all the couplet paraphrases into one flowing paragraph. The Four R's of paraphrasing - Reword, Rearrange, Realize and Recheck - are applied so that the message of Iqbal's poem is restated in simple prose.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (Application): On a sheet of paper, write a letter to your principal requesting him/her to allow your class to visit the Karachi Museum. Follow the sample given (address of the person, greeting/salutation, closing, body stating the purpose and request, and signature).
questions.answer:
The Principal
ABC School
Karachi

14 October 2026

Dear Sir/Madam,

With due respect, I wish to state that our class, IX-A, has been studying the history and culture of Pakistan in our English and Pakistan Studies lessons. We believe that an educational visit to the Karachi Museum would greatly deepen our understanding of our country's rich heritage, its ancient civilisations and its national heroes. Such a visit will make our classroom learning real and memorable, and it will also encourage a sense of national pride among the students.

Therefore, I request you to kindly permit our class to visit the Karachi Museum next Friday during school hours. Our class teacher has agreed to accompany us and to make all the necessary arrangements for transport.

We shall be highly obliged if you grant us this permission.

Thank you.

Yours sincerely,
Sara Khan
Student, Class IX-A
questions.explanation: This exercise teaches the correct format of an application. The answer follows the five parts shown in the sample: (1) the address of the person to whom the letter is written, (2) the greeting or salutation, (3) the body stating the purpose and the request, (4) the closing, and (5) the signature with the writer's name and position.

questions.question: Exercise 2, Couplet 2: Paraphrase the couplet: 'May the world's darkness disappear through the life of mine! / May every place light up with the sparkling light of mine!'
questions.answer: I pray that through my life the darkness of the world should vanish, and that every place should brighten and shine with my glowing light.
questions.explanation: The paraphrase keeps the meaning of the original: the poet wishes that the light of his life should remove the world's darkness and illuminate every place.

questions.question: Exercise 2, Couplet 3: Paraphrase the couplet: 'May my homeland through me attain elegance / As the garden through flowers attains elegance'.
questions.answer: May my homeland achieve beauty and grace through me, just as a garden becomes beautiful through its flowers.
questions.explanation: The poet prays that his efforts should bring charm and honour to his country, in the same way that flowers give elegance to a garden.

questions.question: Exercise 2, Couplet 4: Paraphrase the couplet: 'May my life like that moth be, O Lord! / May I love the lamp of knowledge, O Lord!'
questions.answer: O Lord, may my life be like that moth, and may I love the lamp of knowledge!
questions.explanation: The moth sacrifices itself for the flame; likewise the poet prays that he may devote his life completely to the love of knowledge.

questions.question: Exercise 2, Couplet 5: Paraphrase the couplet: 'May supportive of the poor my life's way be / May loving the old, the suffering my way be'.
questions.answer: May my way of life be to support the poor, and may it be to love the elderly and the suffering.
questions.explanation: The poet prays that his life should be spent helping the poor and showing love and compassion to old people and those who suffer.

questions.question: Exercise 2, Couplet 6: Paraphrase the couplet: 'O God! Protect me from the evil ways / Show me the path leading to the good ways'.
questions.answer: O God, keep me safe from evil ways and guide me onto the path that leads to good ways.
questions.explanation: The concluding couplet of the poem is a prayer for protection from wrongdoing and for guidance towards the right path.

questions.question: 4.5 Exercise 1, Q1 (Listening for Academic Purpose): Listen to the story and circle the characters of the story. hare, tortoise, fox, dove, stork
questions.answer: The characters of the story are the fox and the stork.
questions.explanation: The listening text is the story of the fox and the stork. The hare, tortoise and dove do not appear in the story.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Draw the two spider webs in your notebook. Listen to the story again and fill in the required information in the two webs. Web 1 (centre blank) with branches: famous for, invited, meal, served (in, what?), result. Web 2 (centre blank) with branches: famous for, invited, meal, served (in, what?), result.
questions.answer:
Web 1 (the fox):
- Centre: The Fox
- famous for: being cunning
- invited: the stork (for dinner)
- meal: soup
- served: in a flat dish
- result: the stork could not eat and returned home hungry

Web 2 (the stork):
- Centre: The Stork
- famous for: being kind and gentle
- invited: the fox (for dinner)
- meal: fish
- served: in a narrow vase
- result: the fox could not reach the fish and returned home hungry
questions.explanation: Exercise 2 is a graphic organiser task. Filling the two webs helps students remember the key details of who invited whom, what meal was served, in which utensil, and the result of each dinner.

questions.question: Exercise 3, Sentence 1: Listen to the story again and complete the statement: 'The stork followed the rule of ______.'
questions.answer: The stork followed the rule of 'tit for tat'.
questions.explanation: The listening text states, 'This is called tit for tat. He did to the fox what the fox had done to him.'

questions.question: 4.5 Exercise 1, Q2: What was the relationship between the characters? Circle the correct answer. relatives, friends, neighbours, siblings
questions.answer: The relationship between the characters was that of friends.
questions.explanation: The listening text begins, 'Long ago, there was a stork and his friend the fox,' so the two were friends.

questions.question: Exercise 3, Sentence 2: Complete the statement: 'God tells us to ______.'
questions.answer: God tells us to replace the bad with the good.
questions.explanation: The listening text says, 'God tells us to replace the bad with the good. We must follow this rule.'

questions.question: 4.5 Exercise 1, Q3: Who served in the following utensils? Write the names of the characters in the space provided. (First utensil: a flat dish/plate; second utensil: a narrow-necked vase)
questions.answer: Flat dish/plate: the fox served the soup in a flat dish. Narrow-necked vase: the stork served the fish in a narrow vase.
questions.explanation: In the story, the fox invited the stork and served soup in a flat dish, which the stork could not eat with its long beak; later the stork invited the fox and served fish in a narrow-necked vase, which the fox could not reach.

questions.question: Exercise 3, Sentence 3: Complete the statement: 'The key message of the article is ______.'
questions.answer: The key message of the article is that we should not follow the rule of 'tit for tat' with our friends and family; instead, we should replace the bad with the good, so that our relationships improve and the world becomes a better place.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph of the listening text draws the moral of the story: if we stop returning evil for evil and instead repay bad with good, our relationships and the world will improve.

questions.question: 4.5 Exercise 1, Q4: Tick the choices that the stork had according to the author. (a) The stork could have invited other animals and served all of them in jugs. (b) The stork could have served in a container suitable for the fox. (c) The stork could have invited other animals too and served them all in containers suitable for each of them. (d) The stork could have served in a bottle that had a broad base.
questions.answer: The correct choice is (c): The stork could have invited other animals too and served them all in containers suitable for each of them.
questions.explanation: The author says the stork had many choices: he could have served the fox in a suitable utensil and set an example of true hospitality; 'better still', he could have invited some other animals as well and served each one their favourite food in the utensils that would suit them. Choice (c) matches this best.

The stork could have served in a container suitable for the fox.

questions.question: 4.6 Fun (Role Play of a Poem): Work in trios to plan a role play of Allama Iqbal's poem 'A Mountain and a Squirrel'. One student reads the poem, one acts as the mountain, and the third acts as the squirrel; each trio presents its role play in front of the class. First discuss and check the meanings of these words: self-respect, insignificant, arrogant, shrewd, splendour, pose, grandeur, expel, beetlenut, Omnipotence.
questions.answer:
Meanings of the words:
- self-respect - a proper pride in oneself; regard for one's own dignity and worth.
- insignificant - small or unimportant; of no great value.
- arrogant - proud and haughty; showing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance.
- shrewd - having or showing sharp practical intelligence; clever.
- splendour - great beauty, grandeur or magnificence.
- pose - to behave in a way meant to impress others; to pretend to be what one is not.
- grandeur - greatness; magnificence and impressiveness.
- expel - to drive or force out.
- beetlenut (betel nut) - the seed of the betel palm, which a squirrel can crack, used here as an example of a small but useful skill.
- Omnipotence - the state of being all-powerful; a quality of God alone.

Role play plan (in trios):
- Reader: reads the poem aloud with feeling, sentence by sentence.
- Mountain: speaks proudly and boastfully about its greatness, size and splendour, looking down on the tiny squirrel.
- Squirrel: replies calmly and firmly, pointing out that smallness is not worthlessness, and concludes that 'nothing is useless in this world; nothing is bad in God's creation.'

Model dialogue:
Mountain: 'You are insignificant, yet so arrogant! You are neither wise nor clever. Compared with my splendour even the earth is low. A poor animal like you cannot equal a great mountain!'
Squirrel: 'Hold your tongue! These are immature thoughts - drive them out of your heart. I do not mind that I am not large like you, but you are not a little thing like me either. Everything shows the omnipotence of God; some are large, some small - that is God's wisdom. God made you large, and He taught me to climb the tallest trees. You cannot even walk a single step, so what greatness have you? If you are so great, show me some of the skills that I have - show me how you crack this betel nut as I can. Nothing is useless in this world, and nothing is bad in God's creation.'
questions.explanation: This is the Fun activity of the unit. Students first learn the difficult words of Iqbal's poem, then divide the three roles (reader, mountain, squirrel), practise, and finally present the role play before the class. The dialogue is based on the poem's own words.

questions.question: Pre-Reading: Work in groups of three and write down at least three health-related problems that people in your area face. Also list what steps people should take to protect themselves from some of these problems. Write these in your notebook in the given format (Health Problems - Problem 1 - Steps for protection).
questions.answer: HEALTH PROBLEMS. Problem 1: Mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue and chikungunya. Steps for protection: Do not let water collect around the house; clean water tanks, coolers and flower pots regularly; keep buckets, pots and tyres covered so that there is no stagnant water; use mosquito nets and wear clothes that cover the body; apply mosquito repellent; and seek medical help as soon as symptoms appear. Problem 2: Contaminated drinking water causing diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid. Steps for protection: Drink boiled or filtered water, keep drinking water covered, wash hands with soap before eating, and keep the kitchen and toilets clean. Problem 3: Air pollution causing cough, asthma and chest infections. Steps for protection: Keep the house well ventilated, avoid burning garbage or plastic, plant more trees, and wear a mask when the air is dusty or smoky.
questions.explanation: This pre-reading task draws on learners' prior knowledge about common health problems in their locality so that they can connect it with the reading text on diseases caused by mosquitoes.

questions.question: Tick the right answer. The text is about:
questions.answer: c) Diseases caused by mosquitoes
questions.explanation: The whole passage deals with malaria, dengue and chikungunya, all of which are spread by mosquitoes, so option (c) correctly states the central idea.

options.text: The life cycle of a mosquito
Use of pesticides for mosquito control

questions.optionsRaw: (a) The life cycle of a mosquito (b) Different kinds of dangerous mosquitoes (c) Diseases caused by mosquitoes (d) Use of pesticides for mosquito control

questions.question: Circle the diseases mentioned in the text: tuberculosis, diphtheria, cholera, yellow fever, jaundice, malaria, tonsillitis, chikungunya, hepatitis, dengue, influenza, cerebral malaria.
questions.answer: The diseases mentioned in the text are: malaria, dengue, chikungunya and cerebral malaria (a severe form of malaria). All the other names listed (tuberculosis, diphtheria, cholera, yellow fever, jaundice, tonsillitis, hepatitis and influenza) do not appear in the passage.
questions.explanation: The reading text discusses only the three mosquito-borne diseases - malaria, dengue and chikungunya - and mentions cerebral malaria as a complication of malaria, so only those four names are to be circled.

questions.question: Read the text. Find the following words and underline them: parasite, transmitted, saliva, clot, chills, constipation, dysfunction, disorientation, transfusion, antibodies, immune, respiratory, stagnant, contagious, nausea, fatal, display, inflammation, intense, pronounced.
questions.answer: All twenty words occur in the text. Their meanings are: parasite - an organism that lives on or inside another organism and feeds on it; transmitted - passed on from one person or thing to another; saliva - the watery liquid produced in the mouth; clot - to change from liquid into a thick, semi-solid mass; chills - a feeling of coldness accompanied by shivering; constipation - difficulty in emptying the bowels; dysfunction - the abnormal or impaired working of an organ; disorientation - confusion about time, place or identity; transfusion - the transfer of blood from one person into another; antibodies - proteins produced by the body to fight a particular infection; immune - protected against a disease; respiratory - connected with breathing; stagnant - (of water) not flowing; contagious - spreading from one person to another by contact; nausea - a feeling of sickness with an urge to vomit; fatal - causing death; display - to show or exhibit; inflammation - a painful swelling of part of the body; intense - very strong or extreme; pronounced - very noticeable or marked.
questions.explanation: This vocabulary exercise helps learners infer the meaning of difficult words from context and then confirm them from the glossary at the end of the book.

questions.question: Work in pairs and see how many of these words you can use in your own sentences. The pair that will make the most correct sentences will be the winner.
questions.answer: Model sentences: 1. Malaria is caused by a parasite called plasmodium. 2. The disease is transmitted to humans by the bite of an infected mosquito. 3. The virus enters the body through the saliva of the mosquito. 4. In severe cases, the blood may clot inside the vessels. 5. The patient had high fever along with chills. 6. Constipation and kidney dysfunction are seen in some malaria patients. 7. Disorientation may occur when the brain is affected. 8. A blood transfusion can also spread dengue. 9.
