Our body produces antibodies to fight the infection. 10. A person who has once recovered from chikungunya becomes immune to it. 11. Dengue can cause respiratory difficulties. 12. Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water. 13. Chikungunya is not contagious from person to person. 14. Nausea and vomiting are common in chikungunya. 15. The disease is rarely fatal. 16. The rashes display a clear pattern on the skin. 17. Joint pain and inflammation are severe in chikungunya. 18. The eye pain may become intense with bright light. 19. The joint pain caused by chikungunya is more pronounced than that of dengue. 20. A parasite lives on another living organism.
questions.explanation: This pair-work task gives learners practice in using the new vocabulary of the reading text actively in their own sentences.

questions.question: Read the text and select the correct answer: It is important to find out what the exact disease is so that
questions.answer: c. it can be treated properly
questions.explanation: The text says it is important to find out the exact disease 'for it to be properly treated', so option (c) is correct.

options.text: we can tell everyone about it
the patient can decide what to do

questions.optionsRaw: (a) the patient can rest (b) we can tell everyone about it (c) it can be treated properly (d) the patient can decide what to do

questions.question: Read the text and complete the following table in your notebooks: Disease | Source(s) of Transmission | Organs/Cells Attacked | Symptoms.
questions.answer: 1) Malaria - Source(s) of transmission: bite of an infected mosquito (the parasite plasmodium is injected through the mosquito's saliva). Organs/cells attacked: red blood cells (leading to severe liver infection and, if blood flow to the brain stops, cerebral malaria). Symptoms: high fever up to 40 degrees Celsius, chills, sweating, constipation, kidney dysfunction and disorientation. 2) Dengue - Source(s) of transmission: bite of an infected mosquito; also infected blood transfusion, organ donation and from mother to child. Organs/cells attacked: white blood cells and antibodies (the immune system); also the capillaries. Symptoms: high fever, severe body pain, pain behind the eyes that increases with bright light, decreased urine output, respiratory difficulties, intense headache, skin rashes and excessive bleeding from the nose and gums. 3) Chikungunya - Source(s) of transmission: bite of an infected mosquito (which breeds near stagnant or polluted water). Organs/cells attacked: muscle cells, joints, skin, connective tissues and even the central nervous system. Symptoms: fever, skin rash almost identical to dengue rash, headache, nausea, vomiting, muscle weakness, severe joint pain and partial loss of taste.
questions.explanation: The table organises the key information about the three mosquito-borne diseases from the reading passage.

questions.question: What are the most common diseases caused by mosquito bites?
questions.answer: The most common diseases caused by mosquito bites are malaria, dengue and chikungunya. All three are spread by mosquitoes.
questions.explanation: The opening paragraph of the passage states that malaria, dengue and chikungunya are all spread by mosquitoes.

questions.question: You have heard on the news about the spread of malaria, dengue and chikungunya in the nearby villages. You and your classmates decide to launch a campaign to create awareness about these diseases. Work in groups of three and develop a flow chart of one disease (malaria / chikungunya / dengue) following the flow chart given (Disease - Cause(s) - Symptoms - Prevention - Advice).
questions.answer: Model flow chart on MALARIA: MALARIA -> CAUSE(S): Caused by plasmodium, a single-celled parasite, often transmitted by infected mosquitoes and injected into a person's circulatory system through the mosquito's saliva. -> SYMPTOMS: High fever up to 40 degrees Celsius, chills and shivering, sweating, constipation, kidney dysfunction and disorientation. -> PREVENTION: Wear clothes that keep you fully covered; use net coverings; live in hygienic surroundings; ensure there is no stagnant water in uncovered buckets, pots or cans; apply mosquito repellent; and take extra precaution from dawn to dusk. -> ADVICE: Seek medical help as soon as you notice the symptoms, because the earlier the disease is treated, the quicker the recovery. (A group working on dengue would use: Cause(s) - four types of dengue viruses spread by mosquito bites, also by infected blood transfusion, organ donation or from mother to child; Symptoms - high fever, severe body pain, pain behind the eyes, decreased urine output, rashes and excessive bleeding from nose and gums; Prevention - the same protective steps as above; Advice - seek immediate medical help. A group working on chikungunya would use: Cause(s) - a virus transmitted by mosquitoes that breed near stagnant or polluted water; Symptoms - fever, skin rash, headache, nausea, vomiting, muscle weakness and severe joint pain; Prevention - the same protective steps; Advice - see a doctor at once and rest well.)
questions.explanation: This group activity asks learners to organise the information about one disease into an awareness flow chart using the pattern Disease, Cause(s), Symptoms, Prevention and Advice.

questions.question: The malaria parasite attacks the
questions.answer: d) red blood cells
questions.explanation: The text states that the parasite infects the red blood cells until they burst, so the correct option is (d).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) white blood cells (b) brain (c) stomach (d) red blood cells

questions.question: Which specific part of the body becomes highly infected in Cerebral Malaria?
questions.answer: In cerebral malaria the brain becomes highly infected. When the infected red blood cells become sticky and clot easily, the flow of blood to the brain stops, causing cerebral malaria.
questions.explanation: The passage links cerebral malaria with the stoppage of blood flow to the brain.

questions.question: Once the dengue virus enters the system it affects the
questions.answer: a) immune system
questions.explanation: The passage explains that the dengue virus attacks white blood cells and other antibodies, thus affecting the immune system.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) immune system (b) digestive system (c) circulatory system (d) nervous system

questions.question: What can lead to severe liver infection when one has malaria?
questions.answer: In malaria the parasite infects the red blood cells until they burst. The newly developed plasmodium from the burst red blood cells spreads and infects more red blood cells throughout the body, killing all the cells. This process can lead to severe liver infection.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that the spread of the parasite from burst red blood cells to fresh ones can cause severe liver infection.

questions.question: In severe cases of dengue, bleeding may occur in the
questions.answer: d) gums and nose
questions.explanation: The text says that in severe cases bleeding is common in the nose and gums, so option (d) is correct.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) eyes and ears (b) brain (c) stomach and intestine (d) gums and nose

questions.question: How is the immune system affected through dengue?
questions.answer: Once the dengue virus enters the body, it circulates around the body and attacks the white blood cells and other antibodies, thus affecting the immune system. The virus then replicates within the cell until the cell bursts and dies. The death of the white blood cells results in leakage of other fluids from the cells, leading to low protein, fluid in the lungs and stomach area, low blood pressure, shock and eventually death.
questions.explanation: The text describes how dengue damages the white blood cells that form an important part of the immune system.

questions.question: Chikungunya patients usually have fever with
questions.answer: b) rashes
questions.explanation: The text states that chikungunya is usually accompanied by fever and skin rash, so option (b) is correct.

questions.question: How often can one get infected with chikungunya? Why?
questions.answer: One can normally get infected with chikungunya only once in life. The reason is that the virus remains in the system for five to seven days and, once a person recovers from the infection, he or she becomes immune to it for the rest of life.
questions.explanation: The passage states that after recovery from chikungunya a person is immune to it for the rest of their life.

questions.question: Which two of the three diseases have similar symptoms? What are these?
questions.answer: Chikungunya and dengue have almost identical symptoms and disease processes, so much so that one can be mistaken for the other. Both display joint pain and skin rashes that are almost identical. However, the joint pain and inflammation caused by chikungunya are more intense and pronounced, while low platelet count, high bleeding risk and pain behind the eyes are the main symptoms of dengue.
questions.explanation: The passage compares chikungunya and dengue and notes that their symptoms are very similar but with some differences.

questions.question: How often does one have fever and chills when one has malaria?
questions.answer: In malaria the main symptoms are chills or shivering, followed by fever and sweating. These symptoms usually occur every two days.
questions.explanation: The passage states that the fever and chills of malaria typically recur every two days.

questions.question: How do all these diseases affect our life?
questions.answer: All these diseases, that is, malaria, dengue and chikungunya, affect a person's health. They affect the quality of one's work because it takes some time to recover from the weakness caused by them. They also cause loss of working days, weakness, pain and, in severe cases, death, which disturbs the whole family and the community.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that these diseases reduce the quality of a person's work and make recovery slow because of the weakness they cause.

questions.question: How can we protect ourselves from these three diseases?
questions.answer: We can protect ourselves by: wearing clothes that keep us fully covered; using net coverings; living in hygienic surroundings; ensuring that there is no stagnant water, whether clean or dirty, in our locality, not even in uncovered buckets, pots, cans or other things; applying good quality mosquito repellent lotion or natural repellent products; taking extra precaution from dawn to dusk; and seeking medical help as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: The passage gives a list of preventive measures under the heading 'Prevention'.

questions.question: What should we do if we want to recover quickly from these diseases?
questions.answer: If we want to recover quickly from these diseases, we should seek immediate medical help as soon as we observe the symptoms of these diseases. Because the earlier they are treated, the quicker the recovery.
questions.explanation: The closing lines of the passage advise seeking immediate medical help for faster recovery.

questions.question: Work in pairs. Practise the dialogue between Shama and Ahmer orally, then add one more dialogue of your own. Complete the missing lines (Ahmer and Shama).
questions.answer: Completed dialogue. Ahmer: Are you satisfied with the way the teacher explained the poem today? Shama: Well, to tell you the truth, I didn't really understand what he explained. I still have a number of things to ask him. What about you? Ahmer: No, I'm dissatisfied. I don't think the teacher was prepared. But yesterday he explained the vocabulary very well. What do you say? Shama: You're right. The class was fun. I loved the way he made us all get up and move around to find the right meanings. Ahmer: I was very satisfied with yesterday's lesson too, but today I was quite disappointed. Shama: Let us ask him politely to explain the poem once again tomorrow. Additional dialogue of our own. Ahmer: I am extremely happy with the way the teacher treats us when we ask questions. Shama: Yes, but I don't like the way the homework is given at the last moment. Ahmer: I agree. I hope tomorrow's explanation will be clearer. Shama: I am sure it will be, and then we will all be satisfied.
questions.explanation: This speaking task gives practice in expressing satisfaction and dissatisfaction politely, using the phrases given in the boxes.

questions.question: Context 1: Sharif and Rayan took a train to Multan. They had reserved seats in the air conditioned compartment. Mostly things were very good and the seats were comfortable. However, when the train started, they found that the air conditioning wasn't working. Role play a dialogue expressing satisfaction with some things and dissatisfaction with the air conditioning.
questions.answer: Model dialogue. Sharif: I am really satisfied with the train service today - the seats are comfortable and the compartment is very clean. Rayan: Yes, I'm extremely happy with the seating and the cleanliness. But I'm very disappointed with the air conditioning, as it is not working at all. Sharif: You're right. I don't like the way the air conditioning has failed on such a hot day. Rayan: Let's call the caretaker and tell him politely about it. Caretaker: Yes, how can I help you? Sharif: We are satisfied with everything else, but the air conditioner in our compartment isn't working. Could you please get it repaired? Caretaker: I'm sorry for the inconvenience. I will get it checked right away. Rayan: Thank you. We are very happy with your prompt response.
questions.explanation: The role play requires the learners to express both satisfaction and dissatisfaction politely using the given phrases.

questions.question: Context 2: The power supply system in your area is generally good, and complaints are usually solved promptly. However, there has been a power breakdown for 48 hours that has not been solved in spite of repeated complaints. You and a group of neighbours go to the electricity department to complain. Role play a dialogue expressing general satisfaction and current dissatisfaction.
questions.answer: Model dialogue. Spokesman: Good morning. We are satisfied with the electricity service in our area in general, because complaints are usually solved in a timely manner. Officer: Thank you very much for that. What is the problem now? Spokesman: We are very dissatisfied at the moment. There has been a power breakdown in our neighbourhood for 48 hours, and the problem has not been solved in spite of our repeated complaints. Officer: I am sorry for the inconvenience. There is a fault in the main cable, and our team is working on it. Spokesman: We are disappointed with the delay, as it has caused great hardship to the whole street, especially to students and old people. Officer: I understand your concern. The supply should be restored within a few hours. Spokesman: Thank you. We are happy with the good service generally, and we hope the fault will be fixed soon.
questions.explanation: This context trains learners to balance general satisfaction with current dissatisfaction in a polite complaint.

questions.question: Context 3: You are a teacher in a school. Your student Khalid usually does very well in all the tests, but in the last couple of tests his performance has been unsatisfactory. Call him and express your satisfaction with his work generally and dissatisfaction with the way he has been performing lately. Ask him how he feels about his own progress.
questions.answer: Model dialogue. Teacher: Khalid, I called you to talk about your work. I have always been very satisfied with your performance, as you usually do very well in all the tests. Khalid: Thank you, sir. Teacher: However, I am not happy with the way you have been performing in the last couple of tests. Your marks have dropped, and I am quite disappointed with this sudden change. Khalid: I am sorry, sir. I have not been keeping well, and I could not revise properly. Teacher: I understand, but you must not let your studies suffer. How do you feel about your own progress? Khalid: I am not satisfied with my progress either, sir. I have promised myself to work harder and get back to my usual standard. Teacher: I am glad to hear that. I hope you will improve in the coming tests.
questions.explanation: The role play practises polite expression of satisfaction and dissatisfaction in a teacher-student conversation.

questions.question: Look at the sentences in the table. Against each sentence put a tick in the column that identifies whether it is a simple or a compound sentence. Sentence 1: This year has started on a positive note for the students.
questions.answer: Simple sentence. (It has one subject and one predicate.)
questions.explanation: The book gives this sentence as the example; it contains a single subject 'This year' and a single predicate, so it is simple.

questions.question: Join the two sentences to form a compound sentence, using any conjunction: Najma and Rehana studied very hard. They both got A grades in their exams.
questions.answer: Najma and Rehana studied very hard, so they both got A grades in their exams.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'so' shows the result of studying hard, joining the two clauses into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Work in pairs and write sentences in your notebooks by following the steps: Step 1 - Write 8-10 simple sentences about the people and things in your classroom. Step 2 - Write one more simple sentence for each of the sentences you have written. Step 3 - Join the simple sentences to form compound sentences.
questions.answer: Step 1 (simple sentences): 1. Our classroom is very big. 2. Samir is reading a book. 3. Ayesha is writing on the whiteboard. 4. The teacher is explaining the lesson. 5. There are thirty students in our class. 6. The walls are painted light blue. 7. There are two fans in the room. 8. Ali is sharpening his pencil. 9. The windows are open. 10. Sana is smiling at her friend. Step 2 (one more simple sentence for each): 1. Our classroom is very big. It does not have enough light. 2. Samir is reading a book. He seems to be enjoying it. 3. Ayesha is writing on the whiteboard. Her handwriting is very neat. 4. The teacher is explaining the lesson. The students are listening carefully. 5. There are thirty students in our class. They come from different areas. 6. The walls are painted light blue. The paint looks fresh. 7. There are two fans in the room. Both of them are working well. 8. Ali is sharpening his pencil. He is making too much noise. 9. The windows are open. Fresh air is coming in. 10. Sana is smiling at her friend. She looks very happy. Step 3 (compound sentences): 1. Our classroom is very big, but it does not have enough light. 2. Samir is reading a book, and he seems to be enjoying it. 3. Ayesha is writing on the whiteboard, and her handwriting is very neat. 4. The teacher is explaining the lesson, and the students are listening carefully. 5. There are thirty students in our class, and they come from different areas. 6. The walls are painted light blue, and the paint looks fresh. 7. There are two fans in the room, and both of them are working well. 8. Ali is sharpening his pencil, but he is making too much noise. 9. The windows are open, so fresh air is coming in. 10. Sana is smiling at her friend, for she looks very happy.
questions.explanation: This guided writing task moves learners from simple sentences to compound sentences through three clear steps, as shown in the book's model.

questions.question: Sabiha keeps repeating the same words in her letter to her friend Munira. Help her write a mix of simple and compound sentences to make her writing interesting. Rewrite the letter (Sabiha's letter to Munira, pages 120-121).
questions.answer: Sabiha's letter to Munira. I have some exciting news for you about my town, for there is a 'Housing boom' in our town. Builders are building new houses, and they are planning to build at least 300 new houses. These houses are small, so they can easily accommodate single families. The houses will be mainly two storeyed. The people of our town are really excited, and they think that the town needs new people and new business. It will be nice to have new people and new friends. More people will mean more progress for our town, but more people will also require more facilities. New roads will have to be built, and more transport facilities will be required. We will have to build more schools, and we will also need to build more colleges. The town will need more shopping areas, and it will also have to provide other facilities. New water and electricity facilities will have to be provided. Some people are not so happy, for they feel that more people will make the town crowded. There will be more electricity problems and more pollution. There will be more garbage in the town, and there will be more vehicles and factories. Travelling in the town will take a longer time, because there will be more traffic. The houses will be built soon, and they are expected to be built within two years. Many people are interested, for many people want to buy a house in our town. The town is being connected to the port through a new highway. The town is near a river, so water can be supplied easily to the town from the river. Many people have already selected their property, but there are still properties available. Those interested in buying a house should hurry, for all the houses will soon be sold. People can contact the builders, and the builder's office can give them more details.
questions.explanation: The rewritten letter mixes simple and compound sentences, and uses suitable conjunctions (and, but, so, for, because) to avoid the repetition of short sentences in the original.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "I have many friends and I have to invite all of them tomorrow," said Abid.
questions.answer: Abid said that he had many friends and he had to invite all of them the next day.
questions.explanation: A statement is changed with 'said that'; the present tense becomes past ('have' becomes 'had', 'have to' becomes 'had to') and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.question: Work in pairs, read the story 'Avoiding Criticism' and put all the direct speech sentences into indirect speech. The story has statements, exclamations, wishes, promises and hopes.
questions.answer: Avoiding Criticism. Nasrudin and his son were travelling with their donkey. Nasrudin preferred to walk while his son rode the donkey. Soon they passed a group of bystanders, and one of them said that the boy was so selfish, adding that he was riding on a donkey while his poor old father was forced to walk alongside. Another man said that it was so disrespectful and exclaimed what a horrible and spoiled child he was. Nasrudin and his son felt embarrassed, so they changed places - this time Nasrudin rode the donkey while his son walked. Nasrudin said to himself that he hoped he was doing the right thing then. Soon they passed another group of people. Seeing them, one of them exclaimed that the poor young boy had to walk while his selfish father was riding the donkey, and added that he was a heartless parent. Nasrudin was upset to hear this. He said that he wished people would mind their own business. Since he wanted to avoid any further comments, he decided that both he and his son would ride the donkey at the same time. As they both rode, they passed another group of people. One bystander commented that that man and his son were so cruel, adding that they were forcing that poor donkey to bear the weight of two people and that they should be put in jail for that act. Nasrudin heard this and told his son that the only way they could avoid people's comments was that they both walked. The son replied that he supposed that his father was right. Nasrudin said happily that he promised that nobody would be able to say anything to them as they were doing the right thing that time. So they got off the donkey and continued on foot. But as they passed another group of people, they heard them laughing. They said that those people were so stupid that both of them were walking in that heat and neither of them was riding the donkey, and exclaimed what foolish people they were.
questions.explanation: All the direct speech in the story is converted to indirect speech following the rules for statements, exclamations, wishes, promises and hopes (tenses shifted back, pronouns and time/place words changed).

questions.question: The classrooms smell of fresh paint, as they were painted during the holidays.
questions.answer: Compound sentence. ('The classrooms smell of fresh paint' and 'they were painted during the holidays' are two complete sentences joined by comma + 'as'.)
questions.explanation: It contains two independent clauses joined by the conjunction 'as' with a comma, so it is compound.

questions.question: Her father is a pilot. He has flown many different types of planes.
questions.answer: Her father is a pilot, and he has flown many different types of planes.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'and' adds a related piece of information, joining the two clauses into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: Reshma said, "I hope I will get admission in the medical college this year."
questions.answer: Reshma hoped that she would get admission in the medical college that year.
questions.explanation: 'Said + hope' becomes 'hoped'; 'will' becomes 'would' and 'this year' becomes 'that year'.

questions.question: The students love the newly painted classrooms, and they like the newly polished desks.
questions.answer: Compound sentence. (Two complete sentences joined by comma + 'and'.)
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by comma + 'and', making it a compound sentence.

questions.question: Our car is very old. Its engine is in good condition.
questions.answer: Our car is very old, but its engine is in good condition.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'but' shows contrast between the age of the car and the good condition of its engine.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "I wish I had ten hands and a hundred fingers to do all this work," said Feroza.
questions.answer: Feroza wished that she had ten hands and a hundred fingers to do all that work.
questions.explanation: 'Said + wish' becomes 'wished'; 'this' becomes 'that'. The past subjunctive 'had' does not change.

questions.question: Their motivation has increased and their enthusiasm is clearly visible.
questions.answer: Compound sentence. (Two complete sentences joined by 'and'.)
questions.explanation: It has two independent clauses joined by the coordinating conjunction 'and', so it is compound.

questions.question: The boys were playing cricket. It was the first day of their summer vacations.
questions.answer: The boys were playing cricket, for it was the first day of their summer vacations.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'for' or 'because' gives the reason, joining the two clauses into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: The student said, "I promise I will do my homework regularly from today."
questions.answer: The student promised that he would do his homework regularly from that day.
questions.explanation: 'Said + promise' becomes 'promised'; 'will' becomes 'would' and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.question: Most of the students come to school regularly now.
questions.answer: Simple sentence. (One subject and one predicate.)
questions.explanation: The sentence has a single subject 'Most of the students' and a single predicate, so it is simple.

questions.question: My brother is a good artist. He cannot sing at all.
questions.answer: My brother is a good artist, but he cannot sing at all.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'but' shows the contrast between his skill as an artist and his inability to sing.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "They want to buy a new car," said the lawyer, "but they don't have any money."
questions.answer: The lawyer said that they wanted to buy a new car but they did not have any money.
questions.explanation: 'Said that' is used, the present tense becomes past ('want' becomes 'wanted', 'don't have' becomes 'did not have'), and the two parts of the quotation are joined into one statement.

questions.question: They actively participate in various class activities.
questions.answer: Simple sentence. (One subject and one predicate.)
questions.explanation: It contains only one independent clause, so it is simple.

questions.question: You may buy only a new dress now. You may buy a new dress and new shoes next month.
questions.answer: You may buy only a new dress now, or you may buy a new dress and new shoes next month.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'or' presents a choice between two alternatives, joining the clauses into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "We hope we will be able to get permission from our parents," said the children.
questions.answer: The children hoped that they would be able to get permission from their parents.
questions.explanation: 'Said + hope' becomes 'hoped'; 'we' becomes 'they', 'our' becomes 'their', and 'will' becomes 'would'.

questions.question: The students enjoy being outdoors, because they all like sports activities.
questions.answer: Compound sentence. (Two complete sentences joined by comma + 'because'.)
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by comma + 'because', so it is compound.

questions.question: The baby cannot walk. The baby can crawl very fast.
questions.answer: The baby cannot walk, but the baby can crawl very fast.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'but' contrasts the baby's inability to walk with the ability to crawl fast.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "I never thought that a son of mine would get such bad marks!" said his father.
questions.answer: His father exclaimed that he had never thought that a son of his would get such bad marks.
questions.explanation: The exclamation is changed with 'exclaimed that'; the past tense 'thought' becomes 'had thought' and 'mine' becomes 'his'.

questions.question: They are happy with the new look of the school, but they are not happy with the sports facilities that they have.
questions.answer: Compound sentence. (Two complete sentences joined by comma + 'but'.)
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by comma + 'but', so it is compound.

questions.question: I love gardening. I can grow my own fresh vegetables.
questions.answer: I love gardening, for I can grow my own fresh vegetables.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'for' or 'because' gives the reason, joining the two clauses into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: The blind boy said, "I wish I could see this interesting match on the television."
questions.answer: The blind boy wished that he could see that interesting match on the television.
questions.explanation: 'Said + wish' becomes 'wished'; 'this' becomes 'that'. The modal 'could' remains unchanged.

questions.question: They have requested their principal for better sports and game facilities.
questions.answer: Simple sentence. (One subject and one predicate.)
questions.explanation: It has a single subject and a single predicate, so it is simple.

questions.question: The flowers in this pot are very colourful. The flowers in your garden have a lovely fragrance.
questions.answer: The flowers in this pot are very colourful, and the flowers in your garden have a lovely fragrance.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'and' joins two related statements about the flowers into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "Next week, we promise, we will clean the whole house," the children said to their parents.
questions.answer: The children promised their parents that the following week they would clean the whole house.
questions.explanation: 'Said + promise' becomes 'promised'; 'next week' becomes 'the following week' and 'will' becomes 'would'.

questions.question: The students are hopeful that they will have good facilities soon, because their principal has promised that new play grounds will be developed.
questions.answer: Compound sentence. (Two complete sentences joined by comma + 'because'.)
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by comma + 'because', so it is compound.

questions.question: This book is very informative. It is also very interesting.
questions.answer: This book is very informative, and it is also very interesting.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'and' adds a second quality of the book, joining the clauses into a compound sentence.

questions.question: Change from direct to indirect speech: "Our team has won the champion's trophy here for the first time!" said the coach.
questions.answer: The coach exclaimed that their team had won the champion's trophy there for the first time.
questions.explanation: The exclamation is changed with 'exclaimed that'; the present perfect 'has won' becomes past perfect 'had won' and 'here' becomes 'there'.

questions.question: Work in pairs and write a descriptive essay of at least four paragraphs on one of the following topics: 1. My favourite Aunt / Uncle  2. A teacher that I remember  3. Our school principal  4. My grandmother / grandfather.
questions.answer: A Teacher That I Remember. Of all the teachers I have met, the one I remember most fondly is Miss Saima, who taught us English in class seven. She was not just a teacher; she was a friend, a guide and an inspiration to the whole class. Even today, whenever I think of my early school days, her smiling face comes to my mind at once. Miss Saima was a slim and graceful lady of about forty. She always dressed neatly in simple, light-coloured shalwar kameez with a matching dupatta. Her hair was tied back in a tidy bun, and she wore thin, round spectacles that made her look wise and kind. Her most striking feature was her warm smile, which could put even the shyest student at ease. She spoke in a soft, clear voice that was a pleasure to listen to, and her bright eyes always sparkled with interest and affection. What made Miss Saima truly memorable, however, was her patience and her love for teaching. She would explain a difficult lesson again and again until every single student understood it. If any of us made a mistake, she never scolded us harshly; instead, she would gently point out the error and encourage us to try again. She was particularly fond of reading, and she taught us to love books by telling us wonderful stories after every lesson. Her cheerful nature and her sense of humour turned even the dullest grammar lesson into an enjoyable experience. Miss Saima left our school many years ago, but her influence on me has never faded. She was the person who first taught me to love the English language, and it is because of her that I still enjoy reading and writing today. She was hard-working, kind, patient and full of warmth, and these are the qualities that make her the teacher I will always remember.
questions.explanation: The essay describes a person in four paragraphs - introduction, appearance, qualities and behaviour, and why the person is memorable - as required by the descriptive essay guidelines.

questions.question: Read the brochure about the Health Day celebration in school and complete the Health Day Registration Form using block letters.
questions.answer: Health Day Registration Form. Registration Form No.: 024. Name: FATIMA ZAHRA. S/o, D/o: AHMED ALI. Father's CNIC No.: 42101-1234567-8. Address: 24, Gulshan Colony, Karachi. Class: IX. Section: B. Roll No: 17. Age: 14. Gender: Female. Activities that you are interested in: Health information talks, eye test and dental check-up. Number of people who will accompany you: Two (my mother and my younger sister).
questions.explanation: The form is filled with block letters as instructed, using information taken from the Health Day brochure (date, venue, activities) to complete the personal-detail fields.

questions.question: Work in pairs and ask each other the following questions. One student plays Student A and the other Student B. Read the dialogue and fill in the blanks given below. Student A: You look quite stressed, what's the problem? Student B: The problem is that we are short of money and I can't pay my fees. Student A: Since when have you been worried? Student B: Ever since my father told me that .... Student A: Have you talked to anybody about this? Student B: No, I don't know .... Student B: Who do you think I should talk to? Student A: Well, you could talk to .... Maybe, someone can help. Student B: What should I do in the meantime? Student A: You should .... Student B: Do you think I will be able to arrange something? Student A: I'm sure ....
questions.answer: Completed dialogue. Student A: You look quite stressed, what's the problem? Student B: The problem is that we are short of money and I can't pay my fees. Student A: Since when have you been worried? Student B: Ever since my father told me that he had lost his job and that our income had suddenly stopped. Student A: Have you talked to anybody about this? Student B: No, I don't know whom I should talk to about such a personal problem. Student B: Who do you think I should talk to? Student A: Well, you could talk to our class teacher. Maybe, someone can help. Student B: What should I do in the meantime? Student A: You should explain your situation to the principal and request him to give you some time to pay the fees. Student B: Do you think I will be able to arrange something? Student A: I'm sure you will find a way out, and I will help you in whatever way I can.
questions.explanation: This listening-and-speaking task practises informal interviewing, reciprocal language and appropriate responses while discussing a friend's personal problem.

questions.question: Work in pairs and select one of the following situations for an informal interview, or think of another situation: (i) Your friend has severe fever (ii) Cleanliness of toilets in schools (iii) Your brother wants to buy a mobile phone. Discuss how you will deal with the situation, prepare three to four questions, informally interview each other, prepare notes and report to the class.
questions.answer: Model informal interview on Situation (i) 'Your friend has severe fever'. Preparation questions asked by the interviewer: 1. Since when have you had this high fever? 2. Have you seen a doctor or taken any medicine? 3. What symptoms, such as headache, body ache or shivering, do you have? 4. Have you told your parents about it? Responses received (notes): Fever started two days ago; temperature is very high and comes with shivering; has taken only a paracetamol tablet so far; has not seen a doctor yet; parents have been informed. Report to the class: My friend has been suffering from severe fever for the last two days, with shivering and body ache. He has taken only a paracetamol tablet and has not yet consulted a doctor. I have advised him to drink plenty of water, take complete rest, and visit a doctor immediately so that the illness is properly treated and does not become serious. (For Situation (ii) 'Cleanliness of toilets in schools' the questions would be: How often are the school toilets cleaned? Is clean water and soap available there? What problems do students face? What can be done to improve them? For Situation (iii) the questions would be: Why do you want a mobile phone? How much can you spend? Have you discussed it with our parents? How will you use it responsibly?)
questions.explanation: This task develops interviewing skills - preparing relevant questions, listening attentively, taking notes and reporting the findings to the class, as described in the tip boxes on page 127.

questions.question: Vocabulary building - Word chain: In groups of four, write a new word beginning with the last alphabet of the previous word. You cannot repeat words, and each word must have a minimum of four letters. The book's example is: chain - number - ring - grow - elephant - think. Create your own word chain.
questions.answer: Model word chain (each word begins with the last letter of the previous word, has at least four letters, and is used only once): house -> engine -> eggs -> snail -> lemon -> nest -> table -> eight -> tree -> energy -> yard -> dark -> kite -> artist -> star -> rain -> night -> tower -> river -> round. A shorter sample that matches the book's example: chain -> number -> ring -> grow -> wide -> elephant -> tree -> early -> yard -> desk.
questions.explanation: This fun vocabulary activity helps learners revise spelling and vocabulary by forming a chain in which every new word starts with the last letter of the previous word.

questions.question: Pre-Reading Q1: The title of the text is 'The Role of Women in Pakistan's Creation and Development'. What do you think the lesson will be about?
questions.answer: The title tells us that the lesson will be about the part played by women in the making of Pakistan and in its progress afterwards. I think it will describe women who worked shoulder to shoulder with men during the freedom movement, and also women who have served the country in education, health, social welfare and other fields since 1947. It will probably show that Pakistan could neither have been created nor developed without the sacrifices and services of its daughters.
questions.explanation: This is a prediction task: the students must use the title and key words to guess the content of the text before reading it. Predicting from the title prepares the mind for the topic and makes reading faster and more meaningful.

questions.question: Exercise 1 Q1: How many students were there in Sana's group? Write their names.
questions.answer: There were six students in Sana's group. Their names were Aliya (who was the group leader), Sana, Sameer, Ahmad, Hania and Razia.
questions.explanation: The answer is found in the first part of the reading text, where Aliya divides the work among the members and each student tells the group which source of information he or she will use.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (Vocabulary): Work in pairs, find the following words in the text and underline them: opinions, access, contribution, philanthropist, tireless, simultaneously, renowned, inspired, recognition, rehearsed, enthusiasm. Then try to guess the meanings of these words and check them from the glossary.
questions.answer:
Meanings of the given words as they are used in the text:
1. opinions - the views or beliefs that a person holds about something.
2. access - the right or opportunity to use, approach or obtain something.
3. contribution - something that a person gives to help achieve or supply something.
4. philanthropist - a rich person who generously helps others, especially by giving money to good causes.
5. tireless - working without becoming tired; full of continuous energy and effort.
6. simultaneously - at the same time.
7. renowned - famous and admired for a special quality or skill.
8. inspired - filled with the desire and confidence to do something, usually after seeing somebody else's good example.
9. recognition - the appreciation or honour shown to a person for what he or she has done; the act of knowing somebody or something again.
10. rehearsed - practised a speech, play or performance before presenting it in public.
11. enthusiasm - a strong feeling of eager interest and excitement.
questions.explanation: These words are taken directly from the reading text. Guessing their meaning from the surrounding sentences, and then checking in the glossary, trains the students to use context clues instead of memorising words.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q1: Fill in the blank using the words given in Exercise 2 (each word once): My brother decided to become a soldier because he was ______ by my uncle's disciplined way of life.
questions.answer: My brother decided to become a soldier because he was inspired by my uncle's disciplined way of life.
questions.explanation: This sentence is done in the book as the example. 'Inspired' means filled with the desire to do something after seeing a good example, which fits the meaning of the sentence perfectly.

questions.question: Exercise 4: Complete the statement about the IDEAL problem-solving tool. D stands for ______. Here we ______.
questions.answer: D stands for Define. Here we define what exactly we want to do to solve the problem.
questions.explanation: IDEAL is the five-step problem-solving tool described by Ahmad in the text: Identify, Define, Explore, Action and Look back. D is the second step, in which the problem is clearly defined.

questions.question: Exercise 5 Q1: Which of the following sources of information were not used by the students?
questions.answer: (d) Radio and television (TV)
questions.explanation: The students used library books, a laptop with internet, old and new newspapers, a smart phone, magazines, journals and books. Radio and television are not mentioned anywhere in the text, so option (d) is correct. The book does not print an answer key, so the answer has been inferred from the text.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Laptop and internet (b) Newspapers and magazines (c) Books and smart phone (d) Radio and television (TV)

questions.question: Exercise 6 Q1: Write two things or achievements about Fatima Jinnah.
questions.answer:
Two things/achievements about Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah (1893-1969):
1. She gave up her dentistry practice and went to live with her elder brother, Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, and supported him in the struggle for the establishment of Pakistan for about twenty-eight years, including the last nineteen tiring years of his life.
2. Through her, the Muslim women of the sub-continent were able to interview Mohammad Ali Jinnah and seek his guidance; in recognition of her services the grateful nation gave her the title 'Madr-e-Millat', which means 'Mother of the Nation'.
questions.explanation: The exercise asks the students to pick out two main achievements of each famous woman and to discuss them orally before writing. This answer is based on the information box about Fatima Jinnah.

questions.question: Exercise 7 Q1: Fill in the table for Fatima Jinnah - year of birth, year of death, chronological order by year of birth, chronological order by year of death, and main contribution for Pakistan.
questions.answer: Name: Fatima Jinnah. Year of birth: 1893. Year of death: 1969. Chronological order by year of birth: 1st. Chronological order by year of death: 1st. Main contribution for Pakistan: She gave up her dentistry and lived with her brother, Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, supporting him in the struggle for Pakistan for about twenty-eight years. Through her, the Muslim women of the sub-continent could interview the Quaid and seek his guidance. The nation gave her the title Madr-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 requires the students to arrange the five women in chronological order. Fatima Jinnah was born in 1893 and died in 1969, so she is the earliest both in birth and in death among the five.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q1: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Sana was worried because ______.
questions.answer: Sana was worried because she did not have a computer for gathering information for the social studies assignment.
questions.explanation: This sentence is done in the book as the example. Sana's worry is the very first problem mentioned in the text, and it is solved by Aliya's plan of sharing the work among the group members.

questions.question: Exercise 9: Work in groups of three. Think of one thing that you can do during the summer vacations that will help people or improve things in the area where you live. Use the IDEAL tool to identify the problem and find the solution (Identify, Define, Explore, Action, Look back). Next decide: who will do what, what things you will need, by what time you will do the different things, and when you will complete the task. Then share your plan with the class.
questions.answer:
Model group plan (groups of three): 'Turn a rubbish corner of our street into a small green reading corner for children.'

IDENTIFY - What is the problem we want to address? The open corner of our street is used as a dumping place for garbage. It is dirty and smelly, mosquitoes breed there, and the small children of the street have no clean, safe place to sit and read or play during the summer holidays.

DEFINE - What do we want to do? We want to clean that corner, plant a few shady plants in pots and set up a small 'summer reading and games corner' where the young children of the street can spend two hours every afternoon.

EXPLORE - Find details about the problem. We visited the corner and counted how much rubbish was there. We found out that the municipal office will give two dustbins free of cost if we apply in writing. We asked the neighbours and they promised to give old story books, board games and a mat. We also asked the children what they would like.

ACTION - What steps will we take to address the problem?
(1) Hold a clean-up day and clear all the rubbish.
(2) Write an application to the municipal office for two dustbins.
(3) Collect story books, games, a mat and two benches from the neighbours.
(4) Plant four small shady plants in pots.
(5) Fix a duty rota so that two of us look after the corner every afternoon.

LOOK BACK - How will we check that we have done our task? At the end of the vacation we will see whether the corner is still clean, count how many children used it every day, and ask the neighbours and the children for their opinion. If the plan has worked, we will request the school to continue it.

Next, decide:
- Who will do what: Sana will lead the clean-up and write to the municipal office; Bilal will collect the books, games and benches; Ayesha will keep the daily register and invite the children; all three of us will take turns on afternoon duty.
- What things we will need: brooms, gloves, garbage bags, two dustbins, a mat, two benches, story books, board games, four potted plants and a small notice board.
- By what time: the clean-up and the collection of materials in the first week of the vacation; the setting up of the corner and the duty rota in the second week.
- When we will complete the task: the whole task will be completed by the end of the second week of the summer vacation, and we will present our report to the class on the first day of the new session.
questions.explanation: This is a group activity in which the IDEAL tool is applied to a real, small problem of the students' own area. The plan shows all five steps of IDEAL together with the four planning questions (who, what, by when, completion).

questions.question: Pre-Reading Q2: Can you think of names of some famous women in Pakistan's history?
questions.answer: Yes. Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah (Madr-e-Millat), Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan, Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz, Lady Sughra Hidayatullah, Lady Nusrat Haroon, Begum Shaista Ikramullah, Begum Salma Tassaduque Hussain, Bi Amman, Begum Mahmooda Salim Khan and Fatima Begum are some of the famous women of Pakistan's history. They are remembered for their services to the freedom movement and to the new country.
questions.explanation: This pre-reading question activates the students' prior knowledge of history. Naming famous women of the past helps them connect the new text with what they already know.

questions.question: Exercise 1 Q2: How many famous women of Pakistan are mentioned in the text? Write their names in the order of appearance in the text.
questions.answer: Five famous women of Pakistan are mentioned in the text. In the order in which they appear they are: (1) Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah, (2) Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan, (3) Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz, (4) Professor Anita Ghulam Ali, and (5) Bilquis Bano Edhi.
questions.explanation: The six students divided the work among themselves and the written information about each of these five women is presented in the text immediately after the story of the assignment.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q2: There are many charitable institutions in Pakistan that are funded by ______.
questions.answer: There are many charitable institutions in Pakistan that are funded by philanthropists.
questions.explanation: 'Philanthropist' means a rich person who helps others by giving money to good causes, so it is the correct word for people who fund charitable institutions.

questions.question: Exercise 4: Complete the statement about the IDEAL problem-solving tool. E stands for ______. Here we ______.
questions.answer: E stands for Explore. Here we try and find out as much as we can about how to solve it.
questions.explanation: In the Explore step the group gathers all the information it can about the problem so that the best solution may be chosen.

questions.question: Exercise 5 Q2: Madr-e-Millat means:
questions.answer: (c) Mother of the nation
questions.explanation: The text says that the grateful nation gave Fatima Jinnah the title 'Madr-e-Millat' which means 'Mother of the Nation'. The book prints no answer key, so the answer is inferred from the passage.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Leader of Asia (b) Leader of the nation (c) Mother of the nation (d) Pride of the nation

questions.question: Exercise 6 Q2: Write two things or achievements about Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan.
questions.answer:
Two things/achievements about Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan (1905-1990):
1. She worked as an honorary secretary and typist to her husband, Liaquat Ali Khan, because at that time the Muslim League could not afford the salary of a secretary, and she arranged meetings of the Muslim League women with the wife and daughter of the Viceroy so that they could explain to them the issues and problems of Muslim women.
2. She organised the Muslim voluntary service and, later, the Women's National Guards, consisting of three battalions with 2,400 girls, in which she herself held the rank of a Brigadier; she was also the founder of the All Pakistan Women Association (APWA).
questions.explanation: The answer is taken from the information box on Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan, which shows her as an organiser and the founder of APWA.

questions.question: Exercise 7 Q2: Fill in the table for Bilquis Bano Edhi - year of birth, year of death, chronological order by year of birth, chronological order by year of death, and main contribution for Pakistan.
questions.answer: Name: Bilquis Bano Edhi. Year of birth: 1947. Year of death: Not given in the text (she was still alive when the book was written). Chronological order by year of birth: 5th (the youngest of the five). Chronological order by year of death: not applicable, as no year of death is given. Main contribution for Pakistan: She is a philanthropist and trained nurse who heads the Edhi Foundation, which gives nationwide support and care to the public through shelter homes, ambulance services and other welfare work. She received the Hilal-e-Imtiaz for her tireless efforts for the betterment of society and is called the Mother of Pakistan.
questions.explanation: Bilquis Edhi, born in 1947, is the last of the five women by year of birth. The text gives no year of death for her, so that column remains blank.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q2: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Aliya suggested that they use the IDEAL tool because ______.
questions.answer: Aliya suggested that they use the IDEAL tool because it is a tool for solving all kinds of problems and for planning too, and their problem of gathering information from different sources and dividing the work had to be planned carefully.
questions.explanation: In the text the group agrees with Sameer that IDEAL is a tool for solving all kinds of problems and for planning, which is exactly why Aliya, the group leader, recommends it.

questions.question: Pre-Reading Q3: Can you think of some names of women who have recently achieved fame in Pakistan?
questions.answer: Yes. Some women who have recently achieved fame in Pakistan are: Samina Baig, the first Pakistani woman to climb Mount Everest; Malala Yousafzai, the youngest ever winner of the Nobel Peace Prize; Bilquis Bano Edhi, the social worker who heads the Edhi Foundation; Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, the Oscar-winning film-maker; Arfa Karim, who became the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional; and Ayesha Farooq, Pakistan's first female fighter pilot.
questions.explanation: This question links the past with the present. It shows the students that women continue to bring honour to Pakistan in every field, which is exactly the theme of the reading text.

questions.question: Exercise 1 Q3: How many students shared their dreams at the end of the presentations? Write their names.
questions.answer: Three students shared their dreams at the end of the presentations. They were Maryam, who wanted to be an educationist; Hira, who wanted to be a philanthropist like Bilquis Edhi; and Daniyal, who wanted to help all human beings in trouble like Abdul Sattar Edhi.
questions.explanation: After the presentations the teacher asked a few students to share their future dreams, and their replies show how the lives of the famous women had inspired the class.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q3: The whole class ______ said 'Yes' when the teacher asked if they wanted to go for a picnic.
questions.answer: The whole class simultaneously said 'Yes' when the teacher asked if they wanted to go for a picnic.
questions.explanation: 'Simultaneously' means at the same time, which is exactly what a whole class saying 'Yes' together does.

questions.question: Exercise 4: Complete the statement about the IDEAL problem-solving tool. A stands for ______. Here we ______.
questions.answer: A stands for Action. Here we take the best possible action to try and solve it.
questions.explanation: The Action step is the practical stage in which the group actually does the work that it has planned.

questions.question: Exercise 5 Q3: The first woman who represented the Muslim women in three round table conferences in London was:
questions.answer: (a) Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz
questions.explanation: The text states that Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz represented the Muslim women at the three Round Table Conferences held in London and was the first woman to speak in London's Guild Hall. No answer key is printed, so the answer is inferred from the passage.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz (b) Bilquis Edhi (c) Fatima Jinnah (d) Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan

questions.question: Exercise 6 Q3: Write two things or achievements about Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz.
questions.answer:
Two things/achievements about Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz (1896-1979):
1. She represented the Muslim women at the three Round Table Conferences held in London and was the first woman to make a speech in London's Guild Hall.
2. She travelled widely and explained to the people of other countries why the Muslims in India wanted a separate state, and so she helped the cause of Pakistan abroad.
questions.explanation: The information box on Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz stresses her role as the spokeswoman of Muslim women in London and abroad.

questions.question: Exercise 7 Q3: Fill in the table for Anita Ghulam Ali - year of birth, year of death, chronological order by year of birth, chronological order by year of death, and main contribution for Pakistan.
questions.answer: Name: Professor Anita Ghulam Ali. Year of birth: 1934. Year of death: 2014. Chronological order by year of birth: 4th. Chronological order by year of death: 4th. Main contribution for Pakistan: She was a popular English newsreader, a well-known teacher and a writer of articles and books. She served twice as the Sindh Minister of Education and also held the portfolios of Culture, Science and Technology, and Youth and Sports. As founding manager of the Sindh Education Foundation she promoted quality education and brought many out-of-school children, especially in rural Sindh, to school, and she received the Pride of Performance and Sitara-e-Imtiaz.
questions.explanation: Anita Ghulam Ali was born in 1934 and died in 2014. Among the five women she is fourth both by year of birth and by year of death.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q3: Complete the statement by giving a reason: The Muslim women benefitted from Fatima Jinnah's support because ______.
questions.answer: The Muslim women benefitted from Fatima Jinnah's support because, through her, the Muslim women of the sub-continent were able to interview Mohammad Ali Jinnah and seek his guidance.
questions.explanation: The information box on Fatima Jinnah says that she was the link between the Muslim women and the Quaid-e-Azam, so the women could reach him and get his advice.

questions.question: Pre-Reading Q4: Read the names of the women given in the table and tick the smiling face column if you have heard of them or the sad face column if you don't know about them. Famous Women of Pakistan: 1. Fatima Jinnah, 2. Lady Sughra Hidayatullah, 3. Lady Nusrat Haroon, 4. Anita Ghulam Ali, 5. Samina Baig, 6. Bilquis Edhi, 7. Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz, 8. Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan, 9. Bi Amman, 10. Rosheen Khan.
questions.answer:
A model response, in which the smiling face is ticked against all ten women because every one of them is a distinguished Pakistani woman:
1. Fatima Jinnah - younger sister of Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah; worked for Pakistan for about twenty-eight years and was given the title Madr-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).
2. Lady Sughra Hidayatullah - wife of Sir Ghulam Hussain Hidayatullah, the first Premier of Sindh; an educationist and social worker who worked for women's education.
3. Lady Nusrat Haroon - wife of Sir Abdullah Haroon; a noted social worker and politician of Sindh who promoted education for girls.
4. Anita Ghulam Ali - educationist, English newsreader and writer; twice Sindh Minister of Education and founding manager of the Sindh Education Foundation.
5. Samina Baig - the first Pakistani woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
6. Bilquis Edhi - trained nurse and philanthropist who heads the Edhi Foundation; called the Mother of Pakistan.
7. Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz - represented the Muslim women at the three Round Table Conferences in London.
8. Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan - wife of Liaquat Ali Khan; founder of the All Pakistan Women Association (APWA) and organiser of the Women's National Guards.
9. Bi Amman - mother of Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali; a fearless speaker of the Khilafat movement.
10. Rosheen Khan - a well-known Pakistani artiste of stage and television.
(A student who has honestly not heard of any of these names would tick the sad face for that name; the purpose of the table is to see how many of these great women we already know and to learn about the rest from the lesson.)
questions.explanation: The table simply checks the students' background knowledge before reading. Every name in it is a notable Pakistani woman, so as a model we tick the smiling face column for all of them and give one line of information about each so that the students can recognise them later in the passage.

options.text: I have heard of her (smiling face)
I do not know about her (sad face)

questions.optionsRaw: (a) smiling face - I have heard of her  (b) sad face - I do not know about her

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q4: Every year, the government awards titles to people in ______ of their services in different fields.
questions.answer: Every year, the government awards titles to people in recognition of their services in different fields.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'in recognition of' is a fixed collocation meaning as an appreciation or acknowledgement of something done.

questions.question: Exercise 4: Complete the statement about the IDEAL problem-solving tool. L stands for ______. Here we ______.
questions.answer: L stands for Look back. Here we look back to see whether the problem has been solved or not.
questions.explanation: The last step, Look back, is the checking and evaluation stage, in which the group decides whether its action has really solved the problem and what could be improved.

questions.question: Exercise 5 Q4: Bilquis Edhi was awarded:
questions.answer: (a) Hilal-e-Imtiaz
questions.explanation: The text about Bilquis Bano Edhi says that she received Hilal-e-Imtiaz from the Government of Pakistan in recognition of her tireless efforts for the betterment of society. No answer key is printed, so the answer is inferred from the passage.

questions.question: Exercise 6 Q4: Write two things or achievements about Professor Anita Ghulam Ali.
questions.answer:
Two things/achievements about Professor Anita Ghulam Ali (1934-2014):
1. She was a popular newsreader of the English news and a well-known teacher of her time, and she wrote several articles and books; she served twice as the Sindh Minister of Education and also held the portfolios of Culture, Science and Technology, and Youth and Sports.
2. She was the founding manager of the Sindh Education Foundation, under whose leadership the Foundation promoted quality education and brought many out-of-school children, particularly in the rural areas of Sindh, to school; for this life-time contribution to education she was awarded the Pride of Performance and Sitara-e-Imtiaz.
questions.explanation: The information box on Professor Anita Ghulam Ali highlights her services as an educationist, writer and minister.

questions.question: Exercise 7 Q4: Fill in the table for Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz - year of birth, year of death, chronological order by year of birth, chronological order by year of death, and main contribution for Pakistan.
questions.answer: Name: Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz. Year of birth: 1896. Year of death: 1979. Chronological order by year of birth: 2nd. Chronological order by year of death: 2nd. Main contribution for Pakistan: She represented the Muslim women at the three Round Table Conferences held in London and was the first woman to make a speech in London's Guild Hall. She travelled widely and explained to the people of other countries why the Muslims in India wanted a separate state.
questions.explanation: Born in 1896 and died in 1979, Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz stands second both by year of birth and by year of death among the five women.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q4: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Begum Rana Liaquat Ali worked as a secretary because ______.
questions.answer: Begum Rana Liaquat Ali worked as a secretary because, at that time, the Muslim League could not afford the salary of a secretary, so she served her husband Liaquat Ali Khan as an honorary secretary and typist.
questions.explanation: The text explains that the Muslim League was short of funds, so Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan gave her services free of cost to help her husband.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q5: My father always asks for our ______ before buying any new furniture or other household things.
questions.answer: My father always asks for our opinions before buying any new furniture or other household things.
questions.explanation: 'Opinions' means the views of the family members, which the father asks for before taking a decision about the house.

questions.question: Exercise 5 Q5: Professor Anita Ghulam Ali was appointed twice as a minister of:
questions.answer: (b) Education
questions.explanation: The passage says that Professor Anita Ghulam Ali 'served twice as the Sindh Minister of Education', in addition to being Minister of Culture, Science and Technology, and Youth and Sports. Since she held the education portfolio twice, option (b) is correct. No answer key is printed, so the answer is inferred from the passage.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Culture (b) Education (c) Science and Technology (d) Youth and Sports

questions.question: Exercise 6 Q5: Write two things or achievements about Bilquis Edhi.
questions.answer:
Two things/achievements about Bilquis Bano Edhi (born 1947):
1. She is a philanthropist who is also trained as a professional nurse, and she now heads the Edhi Foundation, which provides nationwide support and care to the public, such as shelter homes and ambulance services.
2. She has received the Hilal-e-Imtiaz from the Government of Pakistan in recognition of her tireless efforts for the betterment of society, and she has also been called the Mother of Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The information box on Bilquis Bano Edhi presents her as the head of the Edhi Foundation and a nationally honoured social worker.

questions.question: Exercise 7 Q5: Fill in the table for Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan - year of birth, year of death, chronological order by year of birth, chronological order by year of death, and main contribution for Pakistan.
questions.answer: Name: Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan. Year of birth: 1905. Year of death: 1990. Chronological order by year of birth: 3rd. Chronological order by year of death: 3rd. Main contribution for Pakistan: She worked as an honorary secretary and typist to her husband, Liaquat Ali Khan, and arranged meetings of Muslim League women with the wife and daughter of the Viceroy. She organised the Muslim voluntary service and the Women's National Guards of three battalions with 2,400 girls, holding the rank of Brigadier, and she founded the All Pakistan Women Association (APWA).
questions.explanation: Born in 1905 and died in 1990, Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan is third in chronological order both by birth and by death.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q5: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Begum Jahan Ara could explain Muslims' point of view to people in many countries because ______.
questions.answer: Begum Jahan Ara could explain Muslims' point of view to people in many countries because she travelled widely and was an experienced speaker who had represented the Muslim women at the three Round Table Conferences in London and had spoken in London's Guild Hall.
questions.explanation: The passage tells us that she travelled widely and explained to the people of other countries why the Muslims in India wanted a separate state, which she could do because of her political experience and powers of speech.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q6: Our principal praised all the students for their ______ to the flood relief fund.
questions.answer: Our principal praised all the students for their contribution to the flood relief fund.
questions.explanation: 'Contribution' means the money or help given to a common cause, here the flood relief fund.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q6: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Professor Anita Ghulam Ali was awarded the Pride of Performance and Sitara-e-Imtiaz because ______.
questions.answer: Professor Anita Ghulam Ali was awarded the Pride of Performance and Sitara-e-Imtiaz because of her tremendous (life-time) contribution to the cause of education in Sindh and Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The text says that the Government of Pakistan recognised her remarkable services to education, especially her work in bringing out-of-school children in rural Sindh back to school, and honoured her with these two awards.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q7: Everyone clapped with ______ when the small children ran in the race.
questions.answer: Everyone clapped with enthusiasm when the small children ran in the race.
questions.explanation: 'Enthusiasm' means eager interest and excitement, which is the feeling with which the people clapped for the children.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q7: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Bilquis Edhi has received the Hilal-e-Imtiaz award because ______.
questions.answer: Bilquis Edhi has received the Hilal-e-Imtiaz award because of her tireless efforts for the betterment of society, through the shelter homes, ambulance services and other welfare work of the Edhi Foundation.
questions.explanation: The information box on Bilquis Bano Edhi clearly states that she received Hilal-e-Imtiaz in recognition of her tireless efforts for the betterment of society.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q8: Our group ______ many times before the finals of the folk song competition.
questions.answer: Our group rehearsed many times before the finals of the folk song competition.
questions.explanation: 'Rehearsed' means practised a performance before presenting it in public, which is what the group did before the finals.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q8: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Maryam said that she wanted to be an educator because ______.
questions.answer: Maryam said that she wanted to be an educator because she wished to work for the improvement of female education, and she had been inspired by Anita Ghulam Ali and by her own grandmother, who was also an educationist.
questions.explanation: After the presentations Maryam shared her dream of becoming an educator like Anita Ghulam Ali and her grandmother, and her aim was to improve education for girls.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q9: Pakistan was created through the ______ efforts of many Muslims working under the leadership of Quaid-e-Azam.
questions.answer: Pakistan was created through the tireless efforts of many Muslims working under the leadership of Quaid-e-Azam.
questions.explanation: 'Tireless' means working without getting tired, which correctly describes the long and continuous struggle for Pakistan.

questions.question: Exercise 8 Q9: Complete the statement by giving a reason: Daniyal said that he wanted to be like Abdul Sattar Edhi because ______.
questions.answer: Daniyal said that he wanted to be like Abdul Sattar Edhi because Edhi Sahib was a renowned social worker and Daniyal too wanted to help all human beings in trouble.
questions.explanation: Daniyal was inspired by the example of Abdul Sattar Edhi, the founder of the Edhi Foundation, whose life was spent in the service of suffering humanity.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q10: All the children in Pakistan should have ______ to quality education.
questions.answer: All the children in Pakistan should have access to quality education.
questions.explanation: 'Access to' means the right or opportunity to obtain something, here quality education.

questions.question: Exercise 3 Q11: Allama Iqbal is a ______ poet of the sub-continent.
questions.answer: Allama Iqbal is a renowned poet of the sub-continent.
questions.explanation: 'Renowned' means famous and admired, which is a suitable word for so great a poet as Allama Iqbal.

questions.question: Exercise 1 (Role play): Work in groups of four, each taking one character. It is time to go on study leave. You and your friends are discussing how to plan your studies so that you can revise all the subjects effectively and efficiently and be well prepared for the exams. Discuss your schedule, expressing your preferences of time, place and subject, giving reasons. Continue the dialogue that begins: Tariq: I don't understand why you want to study so early in the morning. I find it very hard to do so. Saira: One reason is that I'm quite used to waking up early for school as it is... Adnan: Yes, that's the time the mind is fresh after a good night's sleep. What about you, Zohair? Zohair: Well, I ...
questions.answer:
A model continuation of the dialogue:

Zohair: Well, I am afraid I cannot agree with Saira. I prefer studying at night, because the house is quiet then and nobody disturbs me. However, since you all want to start early, I am ready to try the morning routine for one week and see how it works.

Tariq: That is fair enough. As for me, I would rather revise in the afternoon, after a short rest, because I feel sleepy early in the morning. But I do agree that we should all sit together for group study at least three times a week.

Saira: I am glad you agree, Tariq. Now, which subject shall we revise first? I think we should begin with Mathematics, because it needs a fresh mind and daily practice; in my opinion it is the most difficult subject.

Adnan: I am not sure about that. I would prefer to start with English, because it needs more time for reading and writing, and we can do Mathematics later with the help of our group. What do you think, Zohair?

Zohair: I agree with Adnan that English should come first, as we can improve it only by reading and writing every day. But I would suggest that we keep the last hour of every evening for Mathematics practice.

Tariq: That sounds sensible. Where shall we study? I like studying in my own room because there is no noise there.

Saira: I prefer the school library, because it has reference books and there are no distractions. I think we should study there in the mornings and at home in the evenings.

Adnan: I am happy with that plan. Then let us fix our timetable: morning study of English from six to eight at home or in the library, evening group study of Mathematics from five to six, and the remaining subjects on alternate days. We shall meet on Sunday to make the final timetable.

Zohair: I am quite satisfied with this schedule. Let us also agree, politely, that if any of us disagrees later, he will give his reasons with respect, as we have done today.
questions.explanation: This speaking exercise practises asking for and expressing preferences and giving reasons. The model dialogue uses a variety of polite structures such as 'I prefer', 'I would rather', 'I think we should', 'in my opinion' and 'I am afraid I cannot agree', and it ends with an agreed schedule.

questions.question: Exercise 1 Q1: Rewrite the sentence by replacing the bold synonym 'miniature' with an appropriate synonym from the options: He is a brilliant carpenter. He has made a doll house with miniature furniture for every room.
questions.answer: He is a brilliant carpenter. He has made a doll house with tiny furniture for every room.
questions.explanation: 'Miniature' means very small in size, so 'tiny' is the correct synonym here. 'Pretty', 'fresh' and 'tall' do not carry the meaning of smallness.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (a): Select the most appropriate synonym to complete the sentence: This cup of tea tastes like tea flavoured water. It is very ______ (weak, frail, fragile).
questions.answer: This cup of tea tastes like tea flavoured water. It is very weak.
questions.explanation: 'Weak' is used for drinks that have too little flavour or strength. 'Frail' and 'fragile' are used for people or things that break easily, not for tea.

questions.question: Exercise 3 (a): Four of the following five words are synonyms; circle the word that is different: friendly, agreeable, pleasant, decent, amicable.
questions.answer: The different word is 'decent'. The other four - friendly, agreeable, pleasant and amicable - all mean kind and easy to get along with.
questions.explanation: 'Decent' means proper, acceptable or respectable; it does not mean friendly, so it does not belong to the group.

questions.question: Exercise 4: Work with a partner. Select any six groups in Exercise 3. Next, pick two synonyms from each of the selected groups and use both these synonyms in your own sentences. Do this work on a piece of paper, exchange it with another pair for feedback, make changes where necessary, and then write the sentences in your notebooks.
questions.answer:
