questions.question: Translation introduction: Translate literally, then give the real meaning and translate: 'This news is music to my ears.'
questions.answer: Literal translation (word for word): یہ خبر میرے کانوں کے لیے موسیقی ہے۔ Real meaning: I am very pleased / delighted to hear this news. Meaningful Urdu translation: یہ خبر سن کر مجھے بہت خوشی ہوئی۔
questions.explanation: The expression 'music to my ears' is figurative; it means that the news is very pleasing to hear.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'There is plenty of light in this room.'
questions.answer: اس کمرے میں کافی روشنی ہے۔ (Here 'light' is a noun meaning brightness = روشنی۔) Sindhi: هن ڪمري ۾ گهڻي روشني آهي.
questions.explanation: 'Light' is used here as a noun (brightness), unlike sentence 4 where it is used as a verb.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: 'It was time to go home but the bell refused to ring.'
questions.answer: Real meaning: It was time to go home but the bell did not ring. Urdu: گھر جانے کا وقت ہو گیا تھا مگر گھنٹی بجی ہی نہیں۔ Sindhi: گهر وڃڻ جو وقت ٿي ويو هو پر گهنٽي وڳي ئي نه.
questions.explanation: The bell is personified as refusing; the real meaning is simply that the bell did not ring.

questions.question: Exercise 4(A): 'People who are ______ never thank others for helping them.' (happy, friendly, wise, healthy, grateful)
questions.answer: People who are ungrateful never thank others for helping them.
questions.explanation: 'Ungrateful' means not thankful, which fits people who never thank others.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'Please, light all the candles on the cake.'
questions.answer: براہ کرم کیک پر تمام موم بتیاں روشن کر دیں۔ (Here 'light' is a verb meaning to set on fire or make bright = روشن کرنا۔) Sindhi: مهرباني ڪري ڪيڪ تي سڀ موم بتيون ٻاريو.
questions.explanation: 'Light' here is a verb, contrasted with its noun use in sentence 3.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: 'The angry sky roared and threw lightening around.'
questions.answer: Real meaning: There was loud thunder and flashes of lightning all around. Urdu: غضبناک آسمان گرج اٹھا اور چاروں طرف بجلیاں چمکنے لگیں۔ Sindhi: ڪاوڙيل آسمان گرج ڪئي ۽ چوڌاري وڄون چمڪيون.
questions.explanation: The sky is personified as an angry being; 'roared' means thundered and 'threw lightning' means lightning flashed.

questions.question: Exercise 4(A): 'Badar was very ______ because he lost his favourite watch.' (happy, friendly, wise, healthy, grateful)
questions.answer: Badar was very unhappy because he lost his favourite watch.
questions.explanation: Losing a favourite watch makes a person 'unhappy' (not happy).

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'Jamal offered to book our seats on the bus.'
questions.answer: جمال نے بس میں ہماری نشستیں بک کرانے کی پیشکش کی۔ (Here 'book' is a verb meaning to reserve = بک کرنا۔) Sindhi: جمال بس ۾ اسان جون سيٽون بڪ ڪرائڻ جي آڇ ڪئي.
questions.explanation: 'Book' is used here as a verb (to reserve), unlike sentence 6 where it is a noun.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: 'The delicious smell of pudding pulled me to the kitchen.'
questions.answer: Real meaning: The pleasant smell of the pudding attracted me strongly towards the kitchen. Urdu: پڈنگ کی لذیذ خوشبو مجھے کھینچ کر کچن کی طرف لے گئی۔ Sindhi: ڪسٽرڊ جي لذيذ خوشبوءِ مون کي ڇڪي رسوئي ڏانهن وٺي وئي.
questions.explanation: The smell cannot really pull a person; it simply attracted the speaker strongly (personification).

questions.question: Exercise 4(A): 'My uncle took an ______ decision due to which he suffered a big loss.' (happy, friendly, wise, healthy, grateful)
questions.answer: My uncle took an unwise decision due to which he suffered a big loss.
questions.explanation: An 'unwise' (not wise) decision would result in a big loss.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'Have you seen my new book?'
questions.answer: کیا تم نے میری نئی کتاب دیکھی ہے؟ (Here 'book' is a noun meaning a reading book = کتاب۔) Sindhi: ڇا توھان منهنجي نئين ڪتاب ڏٺي آهي؟
questions.explanation: 'Book' here is a noun, contrasted with its verb use in sentence 5.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: 'I can see that news travels quickly.'
questions.answer: Real meaning: It is clear to me that news spreads very quickly. Urdu: میں دیکھ رہا ہوں کہ خبریں بہت تیزی سے پھیلتی ہیں۔/ مجھے معلوم ہو گیا ہے کہ خبریں جلد پھیل جاتی ہیں۔ Sindhi: مان ڏسان ٿو ته خبرون تمام تيزيءَ سان پکڙجن ٿيون.
questions.explanation: 'News travels' is figurative; news does not literally travel but spreads fast among people.

questions.question: Exercise 4(B): Fill in the blank using the prefix 'in' with the appropriate word (correct, sufficient, active, attentive, complete): 'This small boy is very ______ and does not take part in any work.'
questions.answer: This small boy is very inactive and does not take part in any work.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'in-' means 'not'; 'inactive' means not active, which matches a boy who takes no part in any work.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'The principal asked the students to state their reasons for being late.'
questions.answer: پرنسپل نے طلبہ سے دیر سے آنے کی وجوہات بیان کرنے کو کہا۔ (Here 'state' is a verb meaning to say or declare = بیان کرنا۔) Sindhi: پرنسپال استادن کي دير سان اچڻ جا سبب بيان ڪرڻ لاءِ چيو.
questions.explanation: 'State' is used here as a verb (to declare), unlike sentence 8 where it is a noun.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: "I wish you weren't always such a chicken."
questions.answer: Real meaning: I wish you were not always so cowardly / afraid. Urdu: کاش تم ہمیشہ اتنے بزدل نہ ہوتے۔ Sindhi: ڪاش توهان هميشه ايترو ڊڄڻو نه هجو.
questions.explanation: In English, calling someone 'a chicken' means that the person is a coward; it has nothing to do with a real bird.

questions.question: Exercise 4(B): 'The judge was upset with the prisoner for giving an ______ statement to the court.' (correct, sufficient, active, attentive, complete)
questions.answer: The judge was upset with the prisoner for giving an incorrect statement to the court.
questions.explanation: An 'incorrect' (wrong) statement would upset a judge.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'The state should ensure that all people follow the rules.'
questions.answer: ریاست کو یقینی بنانا چاہیے کہ تمام لوگ قوانین کی پاسداری کریں۔ (Here 'state' is a noun meaning a country or government = ریاست۔) Sindhi: رياست کي يقيني بڻائڻ گهرجي ته سڀ ماڻهو قاعدن جي پيروي ڪن.
questions.explanation: 'State' is a noun here (a country/government), contrasted with its verb use in sentence 7.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: 'The kids at that school are all brains.'
questions.answer: Real meaning: The students of that school are all very intelligent. Urdu: اُس اسکول کے بچے سب بہت ذہین ہیں۔ Sindhi: ان اسڪول جا ٻار سڀ تمام هوشيار آهن.
questions.explanation: 'All brains' is a figure of speech meaning extremely clever or intelligent.

questions.question: Exercise 4(B): "Don't leave your work ______ or the boss will be angry." (correct, sufficient, active, attentive, complete)
questions.answer: Don't leave your work incomplete or the boss will be angry.
questions.explanation: 'Incomplete' means not finished, which would make a boss angry.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'This is exactly my point that we should leave early.'
questions.answer: میرا بالکل یہی نکتہ ہے کہ ہمیں جلدی روانہ ہونا چاہیے۔ (Here 'point' is a noun meaning an idea or opinion = نکتہ۔) Sindhi: اها ئي منهنجي ڳالهه آهي ته اسان کي جلد روانو ٿيڻ گهرجي.
questions.explanation: 'Point' is used as a noun (an idea) here, unlike sentence 10 where it is a verb.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: 'You are my guardian angel.'
questions.answer: Real meaning: You are my kind protector who always helps and saves me. Urdu: تم میرے محافظ / نجات دہندہ فرشتہ ہو۔ Sindhi: توهان منهنجا محافظ فرشتا آهيو.
questions.explanation: 'Guardian angel' is an idiom for a person who protects and cares for someone lovingly.

questions.question: Exercise 4(B): 'Sajid is very ______ in class; hence, he often fails in the tests.' (correct, sufficient, active, attentive, complete)
questions.answer: Sajid is very inattentive in class; hence, he often fails in the tests.
questions.explanation: 'Inattentive' means not paying attention, which explains his failure in tests.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: "Don't point at people when you are speaking about them."
questions.answer: جب تم لوگوں کے بارے میں بات کر رہے ہو تو ان کی طرف اشارہ نہ کرو۔ (Here 'point' is a verb meaning to show with the finger = اشارہ کرنا۔) Sindhi: جڏهن توهان ماڻهن بابت ڳالهائي رهيا آهيو ته انهن ڏانهن آڱر سان اشارو نه ڪريو.
questions.explanation: 'Point' is a verb here (to indicate with the finger), contrasted with its noun use in sentence 9.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi bringing out the real meaning: "I've been on cloud nine all day."
questions.answer: Real meaning: I have been extremely happy all day. Urdu: میں سارا دن بے حد خوش رہا۔ Sindhi: مان سڄو ڏينهن بيحد خوش رهيو آهيان.
questions.explanation: 'On cloud nine' is an idiom meaning very happy or delighted, not literally sitting on a cloud.

questions.question: Exercise 4(B): 'This amount of money is ______ if you want to buy a new computer.' (correct, sufficient, active, attentive, complete)
questions.answer: This amount of money is insufficient if you want to buy a new computer.
questions.explanation: 'Insufficient' means not enough, which fits the idea that the money is too little for a new computer.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'My brother got the first rank in his final tests.'
questions.answer: میرے بھائی نے اپنے آخری امتحانات میں پہلی پوزیشن حاصل کی۔ (Here 'rank' is a noun meaning position or grade = پوزیشن/درجہ۔) Sindhi: منهنجي ڀاءُ پنهنجي آخري امتحانن ۾ پهرين پوزيشن حاصل ڪئي.
questions.explanation: 'Rank' is used as a noun (position) here, unlike sentence 12 where it means a soldier's grade or status.

questions.question: Exercise 4(C): Fill in the blank using the prefix 'dis' with the appropriate word (satisfied, obedient, honest, loyal, agree): 'We sometimes ______ even with our very close friends.'
questions.answer: We sometimes disagree even with our very close friends.
questions.explanation: The prefix 'dis-' gives an opposite meaning; 'disagree' means not to agree.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Translate into Urdu/Sindhi: 'The rank of a soldier depends on many factors.'
questions.answer: ایک سپاہی کا رتبہ بہت سے عوامل پر منحصر ہے۔ (Here 'rank' is a noun meaning a soldier's grade or status = رتبہ۔) Sindhi: هڪ سپاهي جو درجو گهڻن عنصرن تي منحصر آهي.
questions.explanation: 'Rank' here means a soldier's official grade or status, a different sense from that in sentence 11.

questions.question: Exercise 4(C): 'We cannot trust ______ people as they can cheat us.' (satisfied, obedient, honest, loyal, agree)
questions.answer: We cannot trust dishonest people as they can cheat us.
questions.explanation: 'Dishonest' means not honest; such people may cheat us, so they cannot be trusted.

questions.question: Exercise 4(C): 'A ______ child can cause many problems for the whole family.' (satisfied, obedient, honest, loyal, agree)
questions.answer: A disobedient child can cause many problems for the whole family.
questions.explanation: 'Disobedient' means not obedient, and such a child may cause trouble for the family.

questions.question: Exercise 4(C): 'Our teacher was ______ with our performance in the competition.' (satisfied, obedient, honest, loyal, agree)
questions.answer: Our teacher was dissatisfied with our performance in the competition.
questions.explanation: 'Dissatisfied' means not satisfied or not pleased, which fits a poor performance.

questions.question: Exercise 4(C): 'We should never be ______ to our country.' (satisfied, obedient, honest, loyal, agree)
questions.answer: We should never be disloyal to our country.
questions.explanation: 'Disloyal' means not loyal, which is what one should never be towards one's country.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Write a compare and contrast essay (at least four paragraphs) on any one of the following topics: (i) Reading story books and reading course books (ii) What happens when a school has a good principal or a bad one.
questions.answer:
MODEL ESSAY - Reading Story Books and Reading Course Books

Reading is one of the most valuable habits a person can develop. Both story books and course books are read by students, yet they serve very different purposes. A course book is studied for examinations and knowledge, while a story book is read for pleasure and imagination. Although both improve our language and our thinking, comparing them helps us understand the special value of each.

There are several points of similarity between the two. Both require the skill of reading and the habit of concentration. Both enrich our vocabulary and improve our grammar, because we meet new words and sentences in each. Both can teach us valuable lessons about life: a course book gives us facts, while a story book teaches us moral values through its characters. In both cases, the more we read, the better we learn.

The differences, however, are greater than the similarities. A course book is based on a fixed syllabus and is read systematically, with notes, exercises and revision, mainly to pass examinations. A story book, on the other hand, is read freely and continuously, without any pressure of tests, simply for enjoyment. The language of a course book is formal and often technical, while a story book uses simple, expressive and imaginative language. Finally, a course book develops our knowledge and reasoning, but a story book develops our imagination, feelings and creativity.

In conclusion, story books and course books are not rivals but companions. A good student learns to respect both, because course books give him knowledge and success in examinations, while story books give him pleasure, a rich imagination and wisdom about life. A balanced reader who enjoys both grows into a well-rounded and thoughtful person.
questions.explanation: A four-paragraph compare-and-contrast essay: introduction, similarities, differences, and conclusion, as required by Unit 3.4's structure.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Write (individually) a compare and contrast essay on the remaining topic from the two given in Exercise 1: 'What happens when a school has a good principal or a bad one.'
questions.answer:
MODEL ESSAY - A School with a Good Principal and a School with a Bad One

A school is like a body, and its principal is like the head that guides it. The whole atmosphere, discipline and standard of a school depend largely upon its principal. A good principal can turn an ordinary school into one of the best, while a bad principal can spoil even a school that has fine buildings and clever students. A comparison of the two shows clearly how great the influence of the head of a school really is.

There are some things that are common to both situations. In every school there are teachers, students, classrooms and a fixed syllabus, and in both cases examinations are held and results are declared. Both kinds of schools must deal with parents, maintain discipline and follow the rules laid down by the education department. Yet the way in which these same duties are carried out differs greatly because of the principal's conduct.

When a school has a good principal, everything runs smoothly. He has a clear vision and plans for the progress of the school. He treats his teachers with respect and encourages them to teach well; as a result, the teachers work with dedication. He is firm but fair with the students, rewards good work and corrects mistakes patiently. He keeps the buildings and laboratories in good condition, arranges sports and co-curricular activities, and meets the parents regularly. Under such a principal, the students are disciplined and confident, and excellent results follow. When a school has a bad principal, however, the picture is quite the opposite. Such a principal has no plan or vision. He is often unfair, harsh or careless. He may favour some teachers and quarrel with others, which demoralises the whole staff. Students become undisciplined, the buildings and facilities are neglected, and no one cares about results or activities. Slowly the good teachers and good students begin to leave, and the reputation of the school falls.

In conclusion, a school is judged by its principal. A good principal builds a happy, disciplined and successful school, while a bad principal destroys it from within. Therefore, the selection of a wise, honest and hardworking principal is the most important duty of those who run our schools.
questions.explanation: A full four-paragraph compare-and-contrast essay on the second topic, following the structure taught in Unit 3.4.

questions.question: Exercise 3: Discuss how a letter is different from an email. Note the differences in your notebook.
questions.answer:
Differences between a letter and an email:
1. Speed and delivery: A letter is written on paper and is delivered by post, which takes days; an email is typed on a computer or phone and reaches the receiver in seconds.
2. Writing tool: A letter is handwritten or typed on paper, whereas an email is always typed and sent electronically.
3. Cost: A letter needs a paper, envelope and postage stamp (money), while an email costs almost nothing.
4. Address: A letter needs the full postal address of the receiver and the sender's address; an email needs only the receiver's email address.
5. Subject line: An email has a short 'subject line' that tells the receiver at once what the message is about; a traditional letter has no subject line.
6. Greeting and ending: A letter begins with 'Dear Sir/Madam' and ends with 'Yours sincerely/faithfully' and a signature; an email is usually more relaxed, often starting with a simple greeting or 'Hi' and ending just with the sender's name.
7. Attachment: An email can carry photos, documents and other files as attachments; a letter cannot.
8. Record: A copy of every email is stored in the computer and can be found easily, while a letter must be filed carefully to be kept.
9. Length and style: A letter tends to be longer and more formal, while an email is usually short, clear and to the point.
10. Formality: Business letters follow a strict set format, whereas emails, especially informal ones, are simpler and friendlier in style.
questions.explanation: This is a discussion task; the model answer lists the main differences between a letter and an email that students should note down.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (Topic 1): Write an informal email to a class fellow requesting help with some school work that you are finding difficult.
questions.answer:
To: ahmed.khan@email.com
Subject: Need your help with Maths homework

Hi Ahmed,

How are you? I hope you are well. I am writing to ask you a small favour.

We were given a difficult Maths homework on algebra yesterday, and I am really finding it hard to solve question numbers 4 to 7. I have tried several times but I keep getting confused about the steps.

You are very good at Maths, and I remember you solved these sums easily in class. Could you please help me with them this Saturday afternoon? If you are free, we can sit together at my house after lunch, or we can meet at the school library. Even a short explanation from you would be a great help.

I would be very grateful for your help. Please let me know what time suits you.

Thanks a lot,
Bilal
questions.explanation: A complete informal email to a classmate asking for help; it follows the informal email format (To, Subject, friendly greeting, body and closing).

questions.question: Exercise 5: Work individually and write an email to your partner on the remaining topic in Exercise 4. Then edit it, exchange it with your partner, write a response, read and edit the response, and write both in your notebooks.
questions.answer:
Model email (the remaining topic: requesting help with difficult school work):

To: kamran.raza@email.com
Subject: Help needed with English essay

Hi Kamran,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing because I need your help with our English assignment.

Our teacher has asked us to write a compare and contrast essay of four paragraphs on 'Reading story books and reading course books'. I understand how to compare, but I am confused about how to organise the paragraphs, and my introduction does not look good. Since you scored the highest marks in the last essay, I thought you could guide me.

Could we meet in the school library tomorrow at break time? Please bring your essay with you so that I can see how you planned it. If tomorrow is not possible, kindly suggest another time.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,
Usman

Model response (reply to the above email):

Hi Usman,

Thanks for your email. Of course I will help you - that is no problem at all.

Your topic is an interesting one. Remember to write four clear paragraphs: an introduction that introduces both kinds of books, a paragraph on how they are similar, a paragraph on how they are different, and a conclusion. Do not list too many points; three or four in each paragraph are enough.

Let us meet in the library tomorrow at break time. Bring your rough draft and we will improve the introduction together. Do not worry, you will manage very well.

See you tomorrow,
Kamran
questions.explanation: The exercise asks for an email on the remaining topic, an edited response, and both written in the notebook. The model provides a complete email and a complete reply.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (Topic 2): Write an informal email to a class fellow suggesting that you do something together during your free time.
questions.answer:
To: sara.ali@email.com
Subject: Let's do something fun this weekend

Hi Sara,

How are you? I hope your exams went well. I haven't seen you properly for many days because we have both been busy studying.

Now that our tests are over, we have some free time this weekend. I was thinking that we could do something together. How about going for a picnic to the seaside park on Sunday morning? We could take some snacks and a ball, and my cousin can come along too. If you prefer, we could go to the book fair in the city instead, or simply meet at my house to watch a movie and do some painting.

Please tell me which idea you like best. I really hope you will join me, as it will be great fun after all our hard work.

Waiting for your reply,
Hina
questions.explanation: A complete informal email suggesting a shared activity during free time, in the proper informal email format.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Read the poem 'Abou Ben Adhem' by James Henry Leigh Hunt silently, and then, in groups of four, recite the poem with one student reading one verse each.
questions.answer:
The poem 'Abou Ben Adhem' has four verses and tells the story of a pious man, Abou Ben Adhem, who wakes from a peaceful sleep and sees an Angel writing in a book of gold. When he asks what the Angel is writing, the Angel replies that it is writing the names of those who love the Lord. Abou asks whether his own name is among them, and the Angel answers, 'Nay, not so.' Abou then humbly requests, 'I pray thee, then, / Write me as one that loves his fellow men.' The Angel writes and disappears. The next night the Angel returns with a great, shining light and shows the names of those whom God's love has blessed - and 'lo! Ben Adhem's name led all the rest.' 
Recitation plan for a group of four: Student 1 reads verse 1 (lines 1-5, describing the Angel in the moonlight); Student 2 reads verse 2 (lines 6-10, the Angel's reply about those who love the Lord); Student 3 reads verse 3 (lines 11-15, Abou's humble prayer to be written among those who love their fellow men); Student 4 reads verse 4 (lines 16-19, the Angel's return and Abou's name leading all the rest). The group should read slowly and clearly, in a soft voice, with the right pauses and expression.
questions.explanation: This is a recitation/reading task. The model gives a short summary of the poem and a simple plan in which each of the four members reads one verse.

questions.question: Exercise 2: Find the rhyming words from the poem 'Abou Ben Adhem' and fill them in the first two columns. Then write two other words that rhyme with them in the next two columns. (The first one, increase/peace, has been done as an example.)
questions.answer:
Rhyming pairs from the poem, with two additional rhyming words for each:
1. increase - peace | cheese - geese (example)
2. room - bloom | broom - gloom
3. gold - bold | cold - told
4. said - head | bed - red
5. accord - Lord | board - sword
6. so - low | go - snow
7. then - men | pen - ten
8. night - light | bright - kite
9. blessed - rest | best - test

(Remember: rhyming words may have different spellings but similar sounds.)
questions.explanation: The poem is written in rhyming couplets. Students identify each rhyming pair and then supply two extra words with the same ending sound.

questions.question: Exercise 3: Work with a partner and, using words from the additional rhyming words, write a short poem having at least eight lines.
questions.answer:
MODEL POEM (8 lines, using rhyming words):

Beneath the moon so bright,
The geese all took their flight.
They sailed across the night
And vanished out of sight.

A girl who loved to read
Took out her book with speed.
She planted a small seed
And did a kindly deed.

(Rhyming words used: bright, flight, night, sight; read, speed, seed, deed.)
questions.explanation: The task asks students to create a short poem of at least eight lines using the rhyming words collected in Exercise 2. The model shows a simple poem with an AAAA and BBBB rhyme scheme.

questions.question: Find the odd one out. From INDISCREET many new words can be formed. One of the six words given is wrong (it has a letter that is extra or not present in the main word). Circle the wrong word: (a) credit (b) erect (c) street (d) cried (e) steer (f) trees. Also add two more words of 4 letters or more.
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'street'. INDISCREET contains only one letter 'T', but 'street' uses two T's, so it has an extra letter. The other five words (credit, erect, cried, steer, trees) can all be formed from the letters of INDISCREET. Two more words (4 letters or more): direct, insert.
questions.explanation: The rule is that one word contains a letter that is extra or missing compared with the main word. 'Street' needs two T's while INDISCREET has only one.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) credit (b) erect (c) street (d) cried (e) steer (f) trees

questions.question: Find the odd one out from CONSISTENTLY: (a) silent (b) style (c) scent (d) costly (e) sister (f) scones. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'sister'. The letter 'R' does not appear in CONSISTENTLY, so 'sister' cannot be formed from it. The other five words (silent, style, scent, costly, scones) can all be formed from its letters. Two more words: listen, stolen.
questions.explanation: CONSISTENTLY has no letter R, so any word containing R (like 'sister') is the odd one out.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) silent (b) style (c) scent (d) costly (e) sister (f) scones

questions.question: Find the odd one out from PARADISE: (a) praise (b) draper (c) parade (d) pride (e) spire (f) spider. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'draper'. PARADISE contains only one letter 'R', but 'draper' uses two R's. The other five words (praise, parade, pride, spire, spider) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: raise, spied.
questions.explanation: PARADISE has a single R; 'draper' needs two R's, so it is the wrong word.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) praise (b) draper (c) parade (d) pride (e) spire (f) spider

questions.question: Find the odd one out from FORTNIGHT: (a) fright (b) throng (c) thing (d) tonight (e) tight (f) nought. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'nought'. The letter 'U' does not appear in FORTNIGHT, so 'nought' cannot be formed from it. The other five words (fright, throng, thing, tonight, tight) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: right, thorn.
questions.explanation: FORTNIGHT has no letter U, so 'nought', which needs a U, is the odd one out.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) fright (b) throng (c) thing (d) tonight (e) tight (f) nought

questions.question: Find the odd one out from ENDEAVOUR: (a) rounder (b) drove (c) devour (d) vendor (e) endure (f) round. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'rounder'. ENDEAVOUR contains only one letter 'R', but 'rounder' uses two R's. The other five words (drove, devour, vendor, endure, round) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: endear, oven.
questions.explanation: ENDEAVOUR has a single R; 'rounder' needs two R's, so it is the wrong word.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) rounder (b) drove (c) devour (d) vendor (e) endure (f) round

questions.question: Find the odd one out from DISREPUTABLE: (a) bleat (b) petal (c) brute (d) stable (e) steep (f) tablet. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'tablet'. DISREPUTABLE contains only one letter 'T', but 'tablet' uses two T's. The other five words (bleat, petal, brute, stable, steep) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: durable, debate.
questions.explanation: DISREPUTABLE has a single T; 'tablet' needs two T's, so it contains an extra letter.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) bleat (b) petal (c) brute (d) stable (e) steep (f) tablet

questions.question: Find the odd one out from CREATURE: (a) cruet (b) trace (c) curate (d) truce (e) centre (f) create. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'centre'. The letter 'N' does not appear in CREATURE, so 'centre' cannot be formed from it. The other five words (cruet, trace, curate, truce, create) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: crate, cure.
questions.explanation: CREATURE has no letter N, so 'centre', which needs an N, is the odd one out.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) cruet (b) trace (c) curate (d) truce (e) centre (f) create

questions.question: Find the odd one out from IMPERTINENT: (a) temper (b) inert (c) intent (d) mitten (e) repent (f) invent. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'invent'. The letter 'V' does not appear in IMPERTINENT, so 'invent' cannot be formed from it. The other five words (temper, inert, intent, mitten, repent) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: entire, permit.
questions.explanation: IMPERTINENT has no letter V, so 'invent', which contains a V, is the odd one out.

questions.question: Find the odd one out from ADMINISTRATION: (a) strain (b) station (c) mansion (d) strong (e) rations (f) storm. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'strong'. The letter 'G' does not appear in ADMINISTRATION, so 'strong' cannot be formed from it. The other five words (strain, station, mansion, rations, storm) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: domain, ration.
questions.explanation: ADMINISTRATION has no letter G, so 'strong', which needs a G, is the odd one out.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) strain (b) station (c) mansion (d) strong (e) rations (f) storm

questions.question: Find the odd one out from SEPARATE: (a) spear (b) spare (c) pears (d) trade (e) steep (f) repeat. Also add two more words (4 letters or more).
questions.answer: The odd one out is 'trade'. The letter 'D' does not appear in SEPARATE, so 'trade' cannot be formed from it. The other five words (spear, spare, pears, steep, repeat) can be formed from its letters. Two more words: spate, pares.

questions.optionsRaw: (a) spear (b) spare (c) pears (d) trade (e) steep (f) repeat

questions.question: Pre-Reading 1: Work in groups of four. Share with each other some of the good things that you remember from your childhood. Remember to talk in English. Select one incident from all those shared in the group for sharing with the class.
questions.answer: Model response: In our group of four each member shared a happy childhood memory. Amina remembered flying kites with her cousins on the roof. Bilal recalled the day his grandfather took him to the fields to watch the sugarcane harvest. Sara spoke about a rainy day when the whole family made paper boats and floated them in the courtyard. I shared the memory of my first bicycle, which my father taught me to ride in the lane behind our house. We selected Sara's rainy-day incident to share with the class because it showed the simple joys of family life and how such small moments bring everyone together even today.
questions.explanation: This is a group oral activity that builds speaking skills. The model gives four recollections and shows how the group selects one incident to present to the class.

questions.question: Exercise 1 (While Reading): Read the diary entries quickly and find out information for filling the table with Item, Day, Date, Topic, Place Mentioned, No. of Paragraphs and Type of Text for Entry 1 and Entry 2.
questions.answer:
Entry 1: Day - Wednesday; Date - 10th February, 2015; Topic - Village life; Place Mentioned - Karachi and the village; No. of Paragraphs - 7; Type of Text - Narrative.
Entry 2: Day - Friday; Date - 4th August, 2017; Topic - 'We Need to Store Rain Water' (storing rain water and barrages); Place Mentioned - the river Indus, Guddu Barrage, Sukkur and Jacobabad districts of Sindh and the Kalat division of Balochistan; No. of Paragraphs - 8; Type of Text - Descriptive.
Entry 1 is a narrative because the writer tells the story of his own feelings and memories, while Entry 2 is descriptive because it explains facts about barrages and how they work.
questions.explanation: Skimming the two diary entries gives the day, date, topic and place directly; the paragraph counts follow the printed paragraphs and the two text types are named in the exercise itself.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (Vocabulary): The words in the box have been taken from the text. Find them in the reading text and underline them. Entry 1: desperately, siblings, commuting, credit, gossips, devices, compromised, distanced, access, replaced. Entry 2: devastation, havoc, capture, retain, structures, releases, irrigation, tamed, self-sufficient, surplus.
questions.answer:
All the words occur in the two entries. Examples of where they are found: 'desperately' - 'But I am desperately missing my village'; 'siblings' - 'we, my parents and siblings, lived in another room'; 'commuting' - 'Commuting from one place to another was not an issue'; 'credit' - 'willing to give goods on credit'; 'gossips' - 'shared news and gossips'; 'devices' - 'not people via devices'; 'compromised' - 'our luxurious life style has compromised our health'; 'distanced' - 'The availability of devices has distanced us from people'; 'access' - 'The access to technology has replaced the human touch'; 'replaced' - 'has replaced the human touch'.
Entry 2: 'devastation' and 'havoc' - 'too much of it can cause flooding and devastation' and 'floods create havoc'; 'capture' and 'retain' - 'capture and retain the rain water'; 'structures' - 'building structures to hold the water'; 'releases' - the text uses the verb 'release it for irrigation'; 'irrigation' - 'release it for irrigation, through the canals'; 'tamed' - 'The barrage has tamed the river'; 'self-sufficient' - 'Pakistan becomes self-sufficient'; 'surplus' - 'grow surplus food items'.
questions.explanation: This exercise trains students to locate target vocabulary in context. The model shows where each word appears so that learners can underline it in the text.

questions.question: Exercise 3: Work in pairs and write two paragraphs. Use at least five words from Entry 1 to write one paragraph, and five words from Entry 2 to write the second paragraph.
questions.answer:
Paragraph 1 (Entry 1 words): I desperately miss the days when my siblings and I lived together in our small mud house in the village. In those days, commuting was never a problem because we simply walked everywhere, and we did not need money or credit to buy from the local shopkeeper. In the evening, people gathered and shared gossips, and no one felt alone. Today, however, modern devices have replaced real human contact and distanced us from one another, and our luxurious lifestyle has compromised the simple health and happiness that our forefathers enjoyed.

Paragraph 2 (Entry 2 words): In Pakistan, heavy monsoon rains often create havoc and cause devastation in villages and cities. To overcome this problem, people have learnt to capture and retain rainwater by building strong structures such as barrages across the rivers. A barrage releases water in a controlled way and supplies it for irrigation throughout the year. The Guddu Barrage has tamed the mighty Indus and helped farmers grow surplus crops, moving the country closer to becoming self-sufficient in food.
questions.explanation: The model uses more than five words from each entry, as the note for teachers allows, and keeps the two paragraphs on topics of the writer's own choice.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (a): 'There were no roads and no vehicles.' Write the number of the paragraph to which this sentence is related.
questions.answer: Paragraph 4
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph of Entry 1 says that the village had no roads or streets, only narrow mud lanes, and that people just walked. This sentence is therefore the summary of paragraph 4 (already given as the worked example in the book).

questions.question: Exercise 5: How was the village life of the past different from the city life of today, as given in the text? Complete the table for the ten items: Houses, Roads/Streets, Mode of travel, Atmosphere, Shops/Markets, Buying from shops, Source of news, Information about people, Source of entertainment, Communicating with people.
questions.answer:
1. Houses - Village 60 years ago: made of wood, straw and mud, with no furniture; City today: made of cement, painted in beautiful colours, with tiled floors and gardens.
2. Roads/Streets - Village: no roads or streets, only narrow mud lanes that became slippery in the rains; City: clean streets, wide metalled roads.
3. Mode of travel - Village: people just walked, no cars, buses or motorbikes; City: cars, buses and motorbikes are used.
4. Atmosphere - Village: pollution-free, quiet and peaceful; City: polluted, noisy and busy.
5. Shops/Markets - Village: only a few small shops selling everyday goods; City: big shops and supermarkets.
6. Buying from shops - Village: goods could be had on credit because shopkeepers knew everyone by name; City: one needs money or credit cards.
7. Source of news - Village: word of mouth, the Otak and the village well; City: television and Facebook.
8. Information about people - Village: face to face, in the flesh and blood; City: through SMS, email and social media.
9. Source of entertainment - Village: folk songs sung to the tune of the ghaghar and tamboora and shared jokes at the Otak; City: YouTube and television.
10. Communicating with people - Village: by meeting people directly; City: through devices and messages.
questions.explanation: Most rows come from the contrasts the writer draws between his present city life and the village he remembers. The table is to be done in the notebook after discussion with a partner.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (a): Complete: 'Very few people had knee problems in the village because ....................'
questions.answer: Very few people had knee problems in the village because they sat and slept on the floor, which exercised their knees.
questions.explanation: The text explains that the villagers sat and slept on the floor and that this constant bending and sitting kept their knees exercised and healthy.

questions.question: Exercise 7 (a): What are the things that the writer was missing?
questions.answer: The writer was missing his simple village, its loving and caring people, the simple mud house that they lived in, the simple toys that gave them so much pleasure, and the carefree life of the village among simple, friendly people.
questions.explanation: In the first paragraph the writer lists the people, the house and the simple pleasures of village life that he misses after moving to Karachi.

questions.question: Exercise 8: Draw a mind map in your notebook providing information about the Guddu Barrage using the given hints (1. Built on, 2. Breadth of river at Guddu, 3. Breadth of barrage, 4. Length of barrage, 5. Amount of flood water that can flow through it, 6. Number of main canals, 7. Names of right and left bank canals, 8. Total area to be irrigated, 9. Names of districts irrigated, 10. Number and kind of people involved in construction, 11. Started working on).
questions.answer:
Mind map of the Guddu Barrage:
1. Built on: the river Indus.
2. Breadth of river at Guddu: about fourteen kilometres.
3. Breadth of barrage: about one kilometre.
4. Length of barrage: 1355 kilometres.
5. Amount of flood water that can flow through it: about 1.2 million cusecs.
6. Number of main canals: three (two on the right bank and one on the left).
7. Names of right and left bank canals: Begari Sindh Feeder and Desert Pat Feeder (right bank); Ghotki Feeder (left bank).
8. Total area to be irrigated: 2.7 million acres.
9. Names of districts irrigated: Sukkur and Jacobabad in Sindh and the Kalat division in Balochistan.
10. Number and kind of people involved in construction: more than 5000 engineers, technicians and labourers.
11. Started working on: 4th February, 1962.
questions.explanation: A mind map places the main topic 'Guddu Barrage' in the centre and connects each hint to its fact from Entry 2. All the figures are taken directly from the text.

questions.question: Pre-Reading 2: Discuss the issues that Pakistan is facing due to water shortage and what the citizens should do and what steps the government should take to solve this problem. Fill the information in the table (Problem / Solution / Responsibility), then decide which problem and solution your group would like to share with the class.
questions.answer:
Filled table:
1. Problem: Shortage of water for drinking and agriculture. Solution: Build small dams, barrages and rainwater storage tanks. Responsibility: Government.
2. Problem: Wastage of water in homes and leaking taps. Solution: Repair leaks and use water carefully; reuse water for plants. Responsibility: Citizens.
3. Problem: Flooding during the monsoon and loss of stored water. Solution: Control river flow with barrages and canals and store the excess rain water. Responsibility: Government.
4. Problem: Unclean, unsafe drinking water causing disease. Solution: Install water filtration and purification plants; boil water before drinking. Responsibility: Government and citizens.
Our group chose to share Problem 3 with the class: monsoon flooding can be controlled by building barrages and canals, which is the responsibility of the government.
questions.explanation: This group discussion links the water issue to the reading text about barrages. The model gives a complete four-row table plus the group's chosen problem and solution.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (b): 'The modern lifestyle has affected our health and our relationships.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 7
questions.explanation: The last paragraph of Entry 1 begins 'Alas! Our luxurious life style has compromised our health' and says that devices have distanced us from people, so it matches this sentence.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (b): Complete: 'The people in the village did not need vehicles because ....................'
questions.answer: The people in the village did not need vehicles because they just walked from one place to another within the village.
questions.explanation: Distances in the village were short enough to walk, so cars, buses and motorbikes were unnecessary.

questions.question: Exercise 7 (b): Why did the lanes in the village become slippery in the rainy season?
questions.answer: The village had no roads or streets, only narrow mud lanes. During the rainy season the mud lanes became wet and muddy, and so they became very slippery.
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph explains that the unpaved mud lanes turned slippery whenever it rained.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (c): 'I miss the simple village life.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 1
questions.explanation: The first paragraph opens with the writer saying that he is desperately missing his simple village and wishes he could go back sixty years; it is the general statement of the whole entry.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (c): Complete: 'People could buy things from the shops without money as ....................'
questions.answer: People could buy things from the shops without money as the village shopkeepers knew everyone by name and were usually willing to give goods on credit.
questions.explanation: In the close-knit village, shopkeepers trusted their customers and allowed them to pay later.

questions.question: Exercise 7 (c): Is the writer happy with his present life? Why? Why not?
questions.answer: No, the writer is not fully happy with his present life. Although he lives in a beautiful modern house in Karachi with clean streets and facilities, he feels that the luxurious lifestyle has compromised our health and that the use of devices has distanced people from one another. He misses the human touch, the simple people and the carefree village life, so he wishes for a time machine to take him back.
questions.explanation: The writer praises the comforts of city life but repeatedly returns to the health, relationships and warmth of the village that the modern lifestyle has taken away.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (d): 'Men met and discussed things at the Otak and women at the village well.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 6
questions.explanation: The paragraph about the Otak describes men meeting in the evening to share news and gossips, while the women had the village well as the centre of their activities.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (d): Complete: 'When the men met at the Otak in the evening they ....................'
questions.answer: When the men met at the Otak in the evening they shared news and gossips, laughed at shared jokes, talked about the weather, their crops and village issues, and enjoyed folk songs sung to the tune of the ghaghar and tamboora.
questions.explanation: The Otak was the village meeting place where men spent their free time in lively social conversation.

questions.question: Exercise 7 (d): Why do most parts of Pakistan have flood problem in summer?
questions.answer: Most parts of Pakistan have a flood problem in summer because during the monsoon season heavy rains fall and the rivers overflow their banks, causing floods and devastation.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph of Entry 2 states that floods create havoc when rivers overflow their banks during the monsoon season.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (e): 'Three families lived in three rooms.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 2
questions.explanation: The second paragraph describes the house with three rooms where the grandparents, the writer's family and the uncle's family lived, sharing a common kitchen.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (e): Complete: 'The writer wanted a time machine so that ....................'
questions.answer: The writer wanted a time machine so that he could go back sixty years to his simple life, simple people, simple interests and simple wants and needs in the village.
questions.explanation: The writer repeatedly wishes for a time machine that would carry him back to the carefree life of his village.

questions.question: Exercise 7 (e): Why did people start building barrages?
questions.answer: People started building barrages to capture and retain the rain water for later use, to control the flow of water in the flood season, to store it, and to release it for irrigation through canals throughout the year.
questions.explanation: The third and fourth paragraphs explain that barrages were built to store excess rain water and prevent flooding while supplying water for farming.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (f): 'The houses were not made of cement.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 3
questions.explanation: The third paragraph contrasts the writer's present cement house with the village houses that were all made of wood, straw and mud.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (f): Complete: 'Rivers have always been important for two reasons: ....................'
questions.answer: Rivers have always been important for two reasons: they served as trade routes, and they were important for growing food crops.
questions.explanation: The text says that before roads and railways, trade was carried on along rivers by boats and ships, and that rivers made the land fertile for farming.

questions.question: Exercise 7 (f): Do you agree / think that we should build bridges? Why? Why not?
questions.answer: Yes, bridges are useful because they help people and vehicles cross rivers, especially where there is no other way to cross. However, for solving the problem described in the text, we should build more barrages and other water-storage structures, because bridges only help us cross a river whereas barrages control floods, store water and supply it for irrigation throughout the year. Since water shortage and flooding are the bigger problems for Pakistan, building more barrages should be our priority, along with bridges wherever they are needed for transport.
questions.explanation: The question invites a reasoned opinion. The model balances the usefulness of bridges with the greater importance of barrages for flood control and irrigation.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 1 (g): 'People bought things from small shops.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 5
questions.explanation: The fifth paragraph says the village did not have big shops or supermarkets but just a few small shops where goods could be bought on credit.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (g): Complete: 'The main purpose of barrages is ....................'
questions.answer: The main purpose of barrages is to control the flow of water in the flood season, store it, and release it for irrigation through the canals throughout the year.
questions.explanation: A barrage is a wall with gates built across a river so that water can be stored in the flood season and used for farming all year round.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (a): 'One of the barrages in Pakistan is the Guddu Barrage.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 5
questions.explanation: The fifth paragraph of Entry 2 says, 'The Guddu barrage, built on the river Indus, is one of the many barrages built in Pakistan.'

questions.question: Exercise 6 (h): Complete: 'The Guddu barrage has made a difference in this region by ....................'
questions.answer: The Guddu barrage has made a difference in this region by taming the river and putting an end to the damage caused by floods in that area.
questions.explanation: Before the barrage was built, floods caused heavy damage; the barrage now controls the river and protects the region.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (b): 'Construction of more barrages is an important need of Pakistan today.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 8
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says that it is about time the government started constructing more barrages to control flooding and supply water throughout the year.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (i): Complete: 'Pakistan needs more barrages to ....................'
questions.answer: Pakistan needs more barrages to control flooding during the rainy season and to supply water throughout the year for irrigating more land.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph argues that more barrages would both prevent floods and provide year-round water for farming.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (c): 'The Guddu barrage irrigates land in two provinces.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 6
questions.explanation: This paragraph states that most of the irrigated area lies in the Sukkur and Jacobabad districts of Sindh and the rest in the Kalat division of the Balochistan province - two provinces.

questions.question: Exercise 6 (j): Complete: 'Through proper water management we can ....................'
questions.answer: Through proper water management we can become self-sufficient in meeting our demands for grains, fruits and vegetables, and can even grow surplus food items which we can export and earn foreign exchange.
questions.explanation: The writer concludes that storing and using water wisely can make Pakistan self-sufficient in food and a food exporter.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (d): 'Rivers have always been important for travel and for growing crops.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 2
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says rivers served as trade routes from the earliest times and were important for growing food, which is why most ancient towns were built near rivers.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (e): 'The flow of water is controlled through gates in a barrage.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 4
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph defines a barrage as a kind of wall that has gates through which water passes in a limited quantity to control the flow of water.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (f): 'Many different people worked to complete the Guddu barrage.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 7
questions.explanation: The seventh paragraph says that more than 5000 engineers, technicians and labourers worked day and night to complete it before it was put into operation on 4th February, 1962.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (g): 'A way was found to store extra water for later use.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 3
questions.explanation: The third paragraph explains that people found a way to capture and retain rainwater for later use by building structures such as barrages across rivers.

questions.question: Exercise 4, Entry 2 (h): 'Rains cause rivers to overflow, leading to flood.' Write the number of the related paragraph.
questions.answer: Paragraph 1
questions.explanation: The first paragraph of Entry 2 states that floods create havoc when rivers overflow their banks during the monsoon season.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Work in groups of four and form two pairs, Pair A and Pair B. For each assigned topic, Pair A prepares and presents points in favour and Pair B against it, and then the group holds a quick debate following the simple conventions of debate. Prepare your debate on the suggested topics (e.g. 1. Girls are more intelligent than boys; 5. You get respect if you give respect; 7. It is the government's responsibility to take care of all the needs of its citizens).
questions.answer:
Model debate on the topic 'You get respect if you give respect':
Pair A (in favour): (i) Respect is like a mirror - what you give comes back to you. (ii) When we treat others politely and fairly, they respond with the same warmth; for example, a student who respects teachers is respected by them in return. (iii) Respect builds trust and strong relationships in families, schools and society. (iv) Great leaders are respected only because they first respected the people they served. We therefore support the motion.
Pair B (against): (i) Some people are respected for their wealth, power or talent even if they are rude to others. (ii) Fear can also earn a kind of respect, as in the case of a strict boss. (iii) Circumstances and culture, not only our own behaviour, decide how people treat us. (iv) Therefore respect does not always depend on giving respect.
Pair A (rebuttal): Wealth or fear produces only outward obedience, not true respect; genuine respect can be earned only by giving respect to others.
Model points for 'Girls are more intelligent than boys': For - girls often get better examination results and show greater care and patience in their work; Against - intelligence is not decided by gender, and boys also excel in many fields such as science, mathematics and sports. Remember to follow the conventions: state your stand, give one reason at a time, support each reason with an example, and refute your opponents' points.
questions.explanation: This speaking task practises the simple conventions of debate - stating agreement or disagreement, giving one reason at a time, supporting it with examples or facts, and refuting the opponent's arguments.

questions.question: Exercise 2: The whole class is divided into four groups, each split into two sub-groups. Each group is given one topic, prepares for ten minutes, and then conducts a debate in front of the class; the class later votes for the sub-group that gave better arguments. Here are the suggested topics: (1) Only close family and friends should be invited at weddings. (2) Upto class 8 students should be promoted to higher classes without exams. (3) We should try and please all the people all the time. (4) Wealth can give us all the happiness we want.
questions.answer:
For each topic the sub-group in favour presents its points, the sub-group against refutes them, and the class votes. Model points:
1. Invite only close family and friends at weddings. For: weddings then remain simple, affordable and free from show-off and waste, and the money saved can help the poor. Against: a wedding is a social occasion that strengthens ties with the whole community, and excluding relatives and neighbours hurts feelings and breaks relationships.
2. Promote upto class 8 students without exams. For: young children face stress and the fear of failure too early, and automatic promotion keeps their confidence high. Against: without exams students do not study seriously, weak students move ahead with poor basics, and the standard of education falls.
3. Try to please all the people all the time. For: good manners and a helpful nature win friends and avoid conflict. Against: it is impossible to please everyone, and always saying 'yes' makes a person lose his own identity; it is better to be honest and sincere than to try to please all.
4. Wealth can give all the happiness we want. For: money buys good food, health care, education and comforts that remove many worries. Against: health, love, respect and peace of mind cannot be bought with money, and many rich people are unhappy while many poor people are content.
questions.explanation: This class debate task uses the same conventions as Exercise 1 but is performed before the whole class. The model supplies balanced arguments for and against each suggested topic so that both sub-groups have material.

questions.question: Exercise 1 (Degrees of adverbs), Row 1: Positive = angrily. Write the comparative and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Comparative: more angrily; Superlative: most angrily
questions.explanation: Adverbs of two or more syllables form the comparative with 'more' and the superlative with 'most'; 'angrily' has three syllables, so it follows this rule.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (1): Fill in the blank with the correct degree of adverb (from the list in Exercise 1, each used once): 'My uncle went the __________ from his home during the recent floods.'
questions.answer: My uncle went the farthest from his home during the recent floods.
questions.explanation: The definite article 'the' with a superlative meaning requires the superlative 'farthest' (from 'far').

questions.question: Exercise 3: Complete the passage using the correct degree of the adverbs given below, using each adverb only once: well, probably, easily, loudly, happily, quickly, long, hard, carefully, noisily. Then write the complete passage, underlining all the adverbs.
questions.answer: The teacher had to shout loudly the second time, before the students settled down. The reason why the students were working noisily was because they wanted more time to do the work. The teacher said that the student who finishes the work quickly would get two extra marks. Salim wanted to perform better than his friends because he wanted to get the scholarship. He had worked hard for his English paper and wanted to be able to do the paper more easily than he had been able to do in the previous test. He read each section carefully to avoid silly mistakes. He knew that he would probably finish well in time to be able to edit his work. He worked the longest on the writing section because he wanted to write a good essay. He submitted his paper happily when the teacher announced that the time was up.
questions.explanation: Each of the ten given adverbs is used exactly once, some in a comparative or superlative form where the sense demands it (better from 'well', more easily from 'easily', longest from 'long'). The ten adverbs to underline are: loudly, noisily, quickly, better, hard, more easily, carefully, probably, longest and happily.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (1): Put in the quotation marks: 'We are going to be late for school, Amjad, said his sister.'
questions.answer: "We are going to be late for school, Amjad," said his sister.
questions.explanation: The exact spoken words are enclosed in quotation marks, and the comma is placed inside the closing quotation mark before the reporting clause.

questions.question: Exercise 5: In the story 'Frogs', insert quotation marks, capital letters, full stops and commas where required. Rewrite the complete story with all the above additions.
questions.answer:
Once upon a time there was a bunch of tiny frogs who arranged a running competition. The goal was to reach the top of a very high tower. A big crowd had gathered around the tower to see the race and cheer on the contestants.

The race began. No one in the crowd really believed that the tiny frogs would reach the top of the tower. One person said, "Oh, way too difficult!"

Another one said, "They will never make it to the top."

"Not a chance that they will succeed," said an old man. "The tower is too high!"

The tiny frogs began collapsing, one by one. However, some of them kept their spirits high and continued climbing higher and higher. The crowd continued to yell, "It is too difficult! No one will make it!"

More tiny frogs got tired and gave up, but one frog continued to climb higher and higher and higher. This one wouldn't give up.

At the end, everyone else had given up climbing the tower except for the one tiny frog who, after a big effort, was the only one who reached the top. Then all of the other tiny frogs asked each other, "How did this one frog manage to do it?"

A contestant asked the tiny frog, "How did you find the strength to reach the goal?" It turned out that the winner was deaf!

The wisdom of this story is: never listen to other people when they are being negative or pessimistic, because they take away your most wonderful dreams from you.

Always remember that words have power and everything you hear and read will affect your actions. Therefore, always be positive, have positive friends and listen only to positive people. Above all, be "deaf" when people tell you what you can and cannot do. Believe in yourself and always say, "With God's help, I can do this."
questions.explanation: Capital letters are added at the start of every sentence, full stops and commas are inserted at the right places, and the exact words spoken are enclosed in quotation marks. Each direct quotation begins with a capital letter.

questions.question: Exercise 6 A (1): Fill the blank with an adjective formed by adding the suffix 'able' to one of the words punish, comfort, cure, move, wash: 'We needed space to do our project work so we moved all the __________ furniture to one side.'
questions.answer: We needed space to do our project work so we moved all the movable furniture to one side.
questions.explanation: Adding the suffix '-able' to the verb 'move' gives the adjective 'movable' (able to be moved).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 2: Superlative = most bravely. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: bravely; Comparative: more bravely
questions.explanation: Since the superlative is 'most bravely', the positive form is 'bravely' and the comparative is 'more bravely'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (2): 'Let's see who runs the __________ in the race.'
questions.answer: Let's see who runs the fastest in the race.
questions.explanation: 'the ... in the race' points to a comparison among more than two runners, so the superlative 'fastest' is needed.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (2): Put in the quotation marks: 'The students stood up and said, Good morning, teacher.'
questions.answer: The students stood up and said, "Good morning, teacher."
questions.explanation: The greeting actually spoken is placed inside quotation marks, and the full stop goes inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.question: Exercise 6 A (2): 'When travelling, we should try and take easily __________ clothes with us.'
questions.answer: When travelling, we should try and take easily washable clothes with us.
questions.explanation: Adding '-able' to the verb 'wash' gives 'washable' (that can be washed easily).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 3: Positive = carefully. Write the comparative and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Comparative: more carefully; Superlative: most carefully
questions.explanation: 'Carefully' is a multi-syllable adverb, so it takes 'more' and 'most'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (3): 'The workers protested __________ at getting low salaries, as compared to long working hours and shorter breaks.'
questions.answer: The workers protested more angrily at getting low salaries, as compared to long working hours and shorter breaks.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'as compared to' signals a comparison between two situations, so the comparative 'more angrily' is used.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (3): Put in the quotation marks: 'The cleaner said, I have cleaned your yard, and then he went away.'
questions.answer: The cleaner said, "I have cleaned your yard," and then he went away.
questions.explanation: The spoken words are enclosed in quotation marks; because the sentence continues, a comma is placed inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.question: Exercise 6 A (3): 'This is a very __________ chair.'
questions.answer: This is a very comfortable chair.
questions.explanation: Adding '-able' to 'comfort' gives the adjective 'comfortable' (giving comfort).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 4: Comparative = more comfortably. Write the positive and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: comfortably; Superlative: most comfortably
questions.explanation: 'More comfortably' shows 'comfortably' to be a multi-syllable adverb, so its superlative is 'most comfortably'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (4): 'The Bolan Express is the __________ train you can take, the rest leave after 10 o'clock.'
questions.answer: The Bolan Express is the earliest train you can take, the rest leave after 10 o'clock.
questions.explanation: 'the ... you can take' compares it with all other trains, so the superlative 'earliest' is required.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (4): Put in the quotation marks: 'The small child was crying, and kept saying, Where is my mother?'
questions.answer: The small child was crying, and kept saying, "Where is my mother?"
questions.explanation: The question that the child kept asking is enclosed in quotation marks, with the question mark placed inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.question: Exercise 6 A (4): 'Non-payment of taxes is a __________ crime.'
questions.answer: Non-payment of taxes is a punishable crime.
questions.explanation: Adding '-able' to the verb 'punish' gives 'punishable' (deserving to be punished).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 5: Comparative = earlier. Write the positive and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: early; Superlative: earliest
questions.explanation: 'Early' is a two-syllable adverb ending in -y, so it takes -er and -est (early - earlier - earliest).

questions.question: Exercise 2 (5): 'The drivers from Germany drove their cars __________ than those from Japan.'
questions.answer: The drivers from Germany drove their cars more carefully than those from Japan.
questions.explanation: The word 'than' shows a comparison between two groups, so the comparative 'more carefully' is used.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (5): Put in the quotation marks: 'Come on in, children, said the gatekeeper, I am going to close the gate.'
questions.answer: "Come on in, children," said the gatekeeper, "I am going to close the gate."
questions.explanation: The speaker's words are interrupted by the reporting clause, so each part of the speech is enclosed in its own pair of quotation marks.

questions.question: Exercise 6 A (5): 'We can recover from __________ diseases quickly if we go to the doctor.'
questions.answer: We can recover from curable diseases quickly if we go to the doctor.
questions.explanation: Adding '-able' to the verb 'cure' gives 'curable' (that can be cured).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 6: Superlative = most easily. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: easily; Comparative: more easily
questions.explanation: The superlative 'most easily' gives the positive 'easily' and the comparative 'more easily'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (6): 'Salim climbed __________ than Fazal but Hanif climbed the __________.'
questions.answer: Salim climbed higher than Fazal but Hanif climbed the highest.
questions.explanation: 'than Fazal' needs the comparative 'higher'; 'the ...' among three people needs the superlative 'highest'.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (6): Put in the quotation marks: 'All the people were shouting, Pakistan Zindabad! We have won the match!'
questions.answer: All the people were shouting, "Pakistan Zindabad! We have won the match!"
questions.explanation: The two exclamatory sentences that were shouted are enclosed in a single pair of quotation marks with the exclamation mark inside.

questions.question: Exercise 6 B (1): Fill the blank with an adjective formed by adding the suffix 'less' to one of the words use, bone, home, taste, job: 'This food is __________ as compared to the food we had yesterday.'
questions.answer: This food is tasteless as compared to the food we had yesterday.
questions.explanation: Adding '-less' to 'taste' gives 'tasteless' (having no taste).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 7: Positive = loudly. Write the comparative and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Comparative: more loudly; Superlative: most loudly
questions.explanation: Although 'loud' can take -er/-est, the adverb 'loudly' is a two-syllable form and normally uses 'more' and 'most'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (7): 'As compared to the soldiers in the first and middle rows, the soldiers in the last row fought the enemy __________.'
questions.answer: As compared to the soldiers in the first and middle rows, the soldiers in the last row fought the enemy more bravely.
questions.explanation: 'As compared to' shows a comparison between two sets of soldiers, so the comparative 'more bravely' is used.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (7): Put in the quotation marks: 'I have lost my car keys, said the old man. How can I start my car now?'
questions.answer: "I have lost my car keys," said the old man. "How can I start my car now?"
questions.explanation: There are two separate utterances; each is enclosed in its own pair of quotation marks, and the question mark goes inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.question: Exercise 6 B (2): 'I asked my mother to buy __________ chicken for the new dish that I wanted to try.'
questions.answer: I asked my mother to buy boneless chicken for the new dish that I wanted to try.
questions.explanation: Adding '-less' to 'bone' gives 'boneless' (having no bones).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 8: Superlative = fastest. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: fast; Comparative: faster
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is a one-syllable adverb, so it adds -er and -est directly (fast - faster - fastest).

questions.question: Exercise 2 (8): 'Saima answered __________ than her friends.'
questions.answer: Saima answered more easily than her friends.
questions.explanation: The word 'than' shows a comparison with her friends, so the comparative 'more easily' is used.

questions.question: Exercise 4 (8): Put in the quotation marks: 'Be careful! There are many bees flying here. They may bite you, said Zahra.'
questions.answer: "Be careful! There are many bees flying here. They may bite you," said Zahra.
questions.explanation: All three sentences spoken by Zahra are enclosed in one pair of quotation marks, with the comma before the reporting clause placed inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.question: Exercise 6 B (3): 'This fellow is __________ as far as work is concerned.'
questions.answer: This fellow is useless as far as work is concerned.
questions.explanation: Adding '-less' to 'use' gives 'useless' (of no use; not helpful at work).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 9: Comparative = more gently. Write the positive and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: gently; Superlative: most gently
questions.explanation: The comparative 'more gently' gives the positive 'gently' and the superlative 'most gently'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (9): 'Newborn babies should be handled __________ than all other age groups.'
questions.answer: Newborn babies should be handled more gently than all other age groups.
questions.explanation: The comparison marked by 'than' requires the comparative 'more gently'.

questions.question: Exercise 6 B (4): 'Finally, I have found work after being __________ for six months.'
questions.answer: Finally, I have found work after being jobless for six months.
questions.explanation: Adding '-less' to 'job' gives 'jobless' (without a job).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 10: Superlative = most happily. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: happily; Comparative: more happily
questions.explanation: 'Happily' is a multi-syllable adverb, so it forms its degrees with 'more' and 'most'.

questions.question: Exercise 2 (10): 'My father was sitting __________ in his chair and enjoying the talk show on TV.'
questions.answer: My father was sitting comfortably in his chair and enjoying the talk show on TV.
questions.explanation: No comparison is being made here, so the positive degree 'comfortably' is used.

questions.question: Exercise 6 B (5): 'Many __________ people sleep on the footpaths.'
questions.answer: Many homeless people sleep on the footpaths.
questions.explanation: Adding '-less' to 'home' gives 'homeless' (having no home).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 11: Positive = hard. Write the comparative and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Comparative: harder; Superlative: hardest
questions.explanation: 'Hard' is a one-syllable adverb, so it takes -er and -est (hard - harder - hardest).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 12: Superlative = most probably. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: probably; Comparative: more probably
questions.explanation: The superlative 'most probably' gives the positive 'probably' and the comparative 'more probably'.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 13: Comparative = longer. Write the positive and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: long; Superlative: longest
questions.explanation: 'Long' is a one-syllable adverb, so its degrees are long - longer - longest.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 14: Superlative = farthest. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: far; Comparative: farther
questions.explanation: 'Far' has two comparative/superlative sets; the regular set used here is far - farther - farthest.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 15: Comparative = more noisily. Write the positive and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: noisily; Superlative: most noisily
questions.explanation: The comparative 'more noisily' gives the positive 'noisily' and the superlative 'most noisily'.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 16: Positive = high. Write the comparative and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Comparative: higher; Superlative: highest
questions.explanation: 'High' is a one-syllable adverb, so it takes -er and -est (high - higher - highest).

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 17: Positive = quickly. Write the comparative and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Comparative: more quickly; Superlative: most quickly
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' is a two-syllable adverb, so it forms its degrees with 'more' and 'most'.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 18: Comparative = more skillfully. Write the positive and superlative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: skillfully; Superlative: most skillfully
questions.explanation: The comparative 'more skillfully' gives the positive 'skillfully' and the superlative 'most skillfully'.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 19: Superlative = most truthfully. Write the positive and comparative degrees.
questions.answer: Positive: truthfully; Comparative: more truthfully
questions.explanation: The superlative 'most truthfully' gives the positive 'truthfully' and the comparative 'more truthfully'.

questions.question: Exercise 1, Row 20: Positive = well, Comparative = better. Write the superlative degree.
questions.answer: Superlative: best
questions.explanation: 'Well' is an irregular adverb; its degrees are well - better - best.

questions.question: Exercise 1: Choose a profession from the list you made at the beginning of this unit and write a job application for it, following the given format (Date, Name of recipient, Designation, Name of Institution, Name of city, Subject, Dear Sir/Madam, three paragraphs, Thanking You, Yours sincerely, Name of sender, Address of the sender).
questions.answer:

The Principal,
Government Boys' Secondary School,
Karachi.

With reference to your advertisement in the daily newspaper 'Dawn' dated 10th March, 2024, I have come to know that a vacancy exists for the post of Subject Teacher of English in your esteemed school. Help them in writing an application for one of these positions, then exchange it with your partner for positive feedback.
